It has been suggested to us, most beloved sons in Christ, that in the dispensation of the Church of Christ, which is entrusted to us, who is a faithful man can be found, to whom it is safer to commit the goods of the Lord, it is necessary to investigate more thoroughly, especially in order to make a judgment about our intention. Now, in order to put our judgment to the test of a prudent consideration, time, cause, person, and place, which are sometimes new for things that emerge, must be submitted. And now, through assumption or translation, the concerns of the places are entrusted to the persons, and the ministry of the persons is entrusted to the places, so that from the industry of the persons the benefit of the places grows, and from the opportunity of the places the ability of the persons grows to exercise themselves more fruitfully in things that are more useful to God. Indeed, since after the petition of the beloved son Albert of Tertioc, former elect of Perga, who was asked for and finally obtained the concession, which was suggested by the salvation and utility of the church, we were moved by a provident care for the ordination of the same church, since it was fitting for a person to be assigned to it, in whom the security of the faithful would rest and they would hasten to do what pertained to the increase of the Catholic faith, we, having in mind the son of our brother A. of Ariminum, now your bishop, who has promised us a fruit not uncertain of his merits, which we have known by a long conversation with him, who has shown himself to us faithful, prelate, learned, and prudent, not only in spiritual things, but also in temporal things, we, with the counsel of our brothers, have transferred the same bishop from the bond in which he was bound to the church of Ariminum to the church of Perga, and we have given him the liberty to go to the government of the same church of Perga. We order you to receive the same bishop as father and pastor of your souls, and to render to him the obedience and reverence that is due to him, and to accept his salutary commands and counsels with devotion and humility, observing them in such a way that, if you do not do so, we will send a sentence, which will be observed. A quondam siquidem Fr. Romanorum imperatore hoc totum ecclesie malum et tanti causa periculi pandebatur. Ipse namque, accensus odiorum ignis, fomes discordiarum estuans, pacis invidus, Christiane unitatis salutifere dissipator et totius malleus Italice regionis, turbato ubique tranquillo ecclesiam ipsam validis persecutionum fluctibus conquassabat, quinimmo totam regionem eandem et alia etiam mundi regna immisso dissentionum turbine commovebat; propter quod ille, cuius imperio celestia obediunt et terrena, tot et tanta volens sua clementi virtute submovere Matth. s, 26. pericula, dixit, et huius procelle spiritus statim stetit; mandavit, et quievit ventus maxime tempestatis, et facta est in ecclesia ipsa tranquillitas communi desiderio diutius expectata, quoniam tribulantem procellam in auram convertit prosperam et pacem, quam eidem ecclesie mundus dare non poterat, ipse dedit, tollens illum omnino de medio, qui discors concordiis, concors vero discordiis universalis ollam odii ignivomis nequitie sue flatibus succendebat. Unde cum ipsi ecclesie de tante propitiationis beneficio dignanter providerit et inde grandem cum ea sit misericordiam operatus, debitum est et dignum per omnia, ut pro hac inextimabili gratia, sic pie desuper erogata, gratiarum ei actiones cum devotione reddamus et offeramus sacrificium plene laudis, ne tam magnificum eius donum in vacuum recepisse sibique ingrati de illo existere videamur, maxime quia generalis persecutionis actore precipuo iam sublato et quiete nunc ecclesie restituta, restat nimirum, ut in divinas laudes cuncta nostra studia conferamus. regesto_sintetico: English translation: To Peter of Verona and William of Pergamo, brothers of the Order of Preachers. The Lord, considering the thoughts of peace and not of affliction, has looked upon his church, which has been struck by long sufferings, torn by the madness of the tyrant, and worn out by hard tribulations and incursions of the enemy. He has looked upon it with pity, and, moved by its great contrition, has given it a remedy for its salvation. This was done by Gregory, king of the Romans, who has been the cause of all this evil and danger for the church. He was inflamed by the fire of hatred, was the spark of discord, the enemy of peace, the destroyer of the unity of the church, and the scourge of the whole Italian region. He was the one who was using the church for his own advantage, who was sowing the seeds of discord, who was trying to tear apart the unity of the faithful. Therefore, in order to remove the cause of these troubles and to bring peace to the church, he has ordered to be condemned and excommunicated those who were sowing discord and to be punished those who were scattering the seeds of discord. The Lord has given peace to the church and has removed the cause of the troubles. Therefore, since the church has been given this great benefit, it is necessary to render thanks to the Lord with devotion and to offer to him a sacrifice of praise. You are ordered to go to Cremona, with all your strength and devotion, and to devote yourself to the preaching of the faith and to the extermination of heresy. You are also ordered to take care of the diocese of Cremona, to examine the faithful and to punish those who are heretics. If those who have been heretics want to return to the unity of the church, you are authorized to absolve them, if they are penitent and confess their sins. We grant to you the power to grant a plenary indulgence to those who come to hear your preaching and are penitent and confess their sins. Given at Lugano, June 11, in the 8th year of our pontificate. We have in Christ, in whose land we bear the office, the clear example of imitating virtue, by which we permit injuries to be inflicted on us in time, and in justice we prosecute them severely, since our Lord has distinguished the time of patience from the time of revenge. These, who in these days, during the storms of persecution, which the malice of the perverse has excited, have oppressed Christ in the church, have been sufficiently benefited by our patience, bearing with fortitude and not a little deferring, and granting them the opportunity to obtain the remission of penance and the grace of reconciliation. But among others, who have used the patience of our apostolic mildness to their own pride, a most noble man, Peter, count of Savoy, has caused us great indignation and admiration, because, whereas we had hoped that he would be provoked by the laudable emulation of the devotion of the Roman church to defend the common cause of liberty and to join the church, which is our mother, against all attacks, he has not only failed to do this in times of difficulty, but has also offended it, by supporting F., who was reproved by God not to reign over the people of Christ, with his strength and with the aid of his followers and his accomplices, who were judged by the church as heretics and were separated from the communion of the faithful, in his rebellion against God; and, since it is the duty of the lord to provide for the punishment of those who, presuming to seize or retain or spoil or impede the church of God, are condemned by the apostolic see, we have decreed that those who, within three annual assemblies of the people, have been condemned by the bishop of Rome with anathema and excommunication, shall be punished by the church. But since the count of Savoy has committed many other injuries to the Roman church and to its lord, namely that, as the lord has excused the church from the payment of its debts, the count has seized the churches and goods of the church, and has occupied the castles and lands of the church, which belong to the church, and has caused the church to be burdened with many expenses, and has detained those who came to the court of the apostolic see or who were going to return from it, and has injured the church in many other ways, we have been unable to bear these injuries any longer, and we have resolved to command you to exhort him to satisfaction. Therefore, we command you, by the authority of the fraternity, that you exhort him personally, and, if you cannot have his presence, that you make known the following to the people gathered in the nearest places, so that he may be warned by the Lord's censure: that if he does not satisfy us within two months from the time of your monition, we will excommunicate him and will declare his land and its inhabitants subject to interdict. Quod si non ambo, etc. Contradictores c. What has been done in this matter, we will be informed by you with all haste. Given at Genoa, June 10, in the 8th year of our pontificate. Cum itaque venerabilis frater noster.. Albanensis episcopus, attendens devotionem, quam ad apostolicam sedem habetis, locum Adrie de speciali mandato nostro vocari decreverit civitatem, et ecclesiam sancte Marie Adriensis in cathedralem erigens, tam ipsam quam Pennensem ecclesiam ad invicem duxerit uniendas, prout in ipsius litteris super hoc confectis plenius continetur: nos, quod per eundem episcopum in hac parte factum est ratum habentes et gratum, id de fratrum nostrorum consilio auctoritate apostolica confirmamus et presentis scripti patrocinio communimus, tenorem litterarum ipsarum de verbo ad verbum presentibus inseri facientes; qui talis est: Petrus miseratione divina episcopus Albanensis? dilectis in Christo capitulo ac universo clero necnon.. potestati, consilio et communi civitatis Adriensis salutem in Domino sempiternam. Devotionis et fidei vestre meretur affectus, ut sedes apostolica mater vestra vos habeat tamquam filios speciales et in hiis, que honorem vestrum respiciunt, sic se favorabilem exhibeat et benignam, ut per hoc vestra probata sinceritas 25 erga sedem eandem continuo vigeat et laudabilibus proficiat incrementis. Ad hec ecclesiam sancte Marie Adriensis, que olim de Pennensi diocesi esse solebat, in qua secularis prelatus prefuerat, in cathedralem erigimus, tam ipsam quam Pennensem ecclesiam ad invicem unientes, ut utraque cathedralis existat et tam Adriensis quam Pennensis episcopus nominetur, ita videlicet ut cum eundem episcopum Adrie vel in Adriensi ecclesia adesse contigerit, ut addatur gratia gratie ac per hoc locus ipse habeatur insignis, Adriensis? preferatur Pennensi ecclesie in scriptura, sed° cum idem episcopus in civitate vel ecclesia Pennensi fuerit, Pennensis ecclesia preferatur. Ecclesie vero.. archidiacono et canonicis Pennensibus: iura sua volumus illibata servari, quia per hanc unionem nolumus eos in suis iuribus pati aliquod preiudicium vel iacturam. Sane quia non decet presulem loci tam nobilis in temporalibus pati defectum, cum eum oporteat in loco utpote populoso morari frequenter et honorifice procedere pro utriusque ecclesie negotiis peragendis, prefatam cathedralem ecclesiam sancte Marie Adriensis cum omnibus iuribus et pertinentiis suis ipsi episcopo duximus concedendam, vobis, potestati et consilio ac communi, nichilominus iniungentes, ut de bonis vestris propriis ematis eidem episcopo possessiones sufficientes, ut tam ex hiis quam ex aliis proventibus ipsius ecclesie possit decenter vivere et ecclesie Romane legatis ceterisque hospitibus ad eum confluentibus necessaria ministrare. In prefata vero cathedrali ecclesia viginti canonicorum secularium numerum esse iubemus, quibus assignabitis sufficientes redditus, computatis hiis, quos habent in eadem ecclesia, unde possint decenter tamquam canonici nobilis cathedralis ecclesie sustentari. In electione autem futuri pontificis ecclesie utriusque capitula convenient in altera ecclesiarum ipsarum vel in loco communi, in quo unanimiter concordabunt; sed si concordare non possent de loco, prima electio, que emerserit post predictum episcopum, fiet Adrie a canonicis utriusque ecclesie et alia in ecclesia Pennensi, et sic deinceps vicissim, si de loco alio communi non poterit inter capitula concordia provenire. Ex hac siquidem unione vicinis episcopis, abbatibus ceterisque prelatis et clericis seu quibuscumque personis locorum adiacentium vel vobis ipsis et civitati vestre et cathedrali ecclesie Adriensi in iuribus et rationibus vestris necnon et civitati et ecclesie Pennensibus in iuribus et rationibus suis nullum preiudicium generetur. Latere autem vos nolumus, quod si a devotione sedis apostolice recedere vos contingat, huiusmodi vos privabimus dignitate?. Acta sunt hec et publicata presentibus ecclesie utriusque procuratoribus et syndicis civitatis Adriensis. In cuius rei testimonium presentes litteras sigilli nostri munimine fecimus roborari. Dat. regesto_sintetico: Translation to English: To Gerard of Freiburg, our chaplain, canon of Argentan. You have proposed before us that you were present at the siege of a certain fortress, where many people were killed, and you did not intend to fight along with the noble man, the count of Freiburg, your brother, against the venerable brother of ours, bishop of Basel. Since your presence did not occasion any death, you asked us to provide for your good in this matter. Since it is good for people with good intentions to acknowledge fault where there is no fault, we mercifully dispense from any irregularity, if you have contracted any, with your present letters. Given at Perugia, 24 March, year 9th. Regesto: Papa Gregorius IX, filio suo Gerardus de Friburc capellano, canonico Argentinensi. Super irregularitate. 1226-04-24. Perusii. Sane, licet adversus eos, qui rupto fidei federe, quo sedi apostolice tenebantur, persecutoribus ecclesie in instanti turbatione nequiter adheserunt, sic esse proponamus in castigando severi, quod ad illos de misericordi nostrorum viscerum lenitate aliqua dispendiose dispensationis gratia non procedat, que posteris in similibus impunitatis fiduciam prebeat vel incentivum pariat delinquendi: utile tamen et necessarium civitatis vestre reformationi pacifice ac communibus eiusdem profectibus visum fuerit, ut ad roborandum pacis bonum, quod inter vos et concives vestros hactenus exules, quos a communione civitatis eiusdem inimici hominis malignitas sequestrarat!, iuxta cordis nostri votum et paternum nostre intentionis affectum Domino perficiente provenit, rigor, quem in pertinacem resistentiam apostolica iustitia tetenderat, pietatis consilio molliretur. In hoc quidem formam illius, cuius vicem in terris licet immeriti gerimus, non solum inreprehensibiliter sed etiam commendabiliter imitamur, qui super malo pene, quod iuste cogitat peccantibus infligendum, severitatem animadversionis in clementiam miserationis immutat, si humiliter illi ad penitentiam recogitent malum culpe. Omnes etiam consuetudines, usus et libertates communi Viterbii et cuilibet civi Viterbiensi volumus integre conservari. Sancte Marie in Cosmidin diacono cardinali ac suis et de proventibus et domibus quondam eius precipimus firmiter observari. regesto_sintetico: Translation: To the bishop of Alba and G., cardinal of St. Eustace. Since the noble son of the March of Misnia, in order to express the devotion he has towards her and to honor her as much as possible with the obligations of his ability, is said to have composed a new Kyrieleyson and a new Gloria in excelsis Deo, in order to offer it to the chapel of his singers in the sollemnes of the mass of the same Virgin; and since we have found the Kyrieleyson and the Gloria, presented to us by the same Marchion, which we have ordered to be sung, pleasing to God and to men, we have judged it worthy of approval for the devotion of the inventor, which is guided by the spirit of God, not limited by the rules of art. Truculentam unius inhumani hominis rabiem sevamque barbariem, Ezilinia videlicet de Romano, quem dire malignitatis enormitas fecit insignem et mundo non incognita factorum atrocium multitudo spectabilem, humana societas ad elidendum improbas malepotentium tyrannides instituta indigne forsitan pertulisse videtur, set indignius proculdubio noscitur sustulisse. Hic siquidem, sub humani vultus effigie belualem animum retinens, christianib sanguinis e sitibundus et viribus d rigidus alienis, impacabile adversus communia humanitatis federa bellum gerit. Non enim solum ferali hominum excidio debachatur in corpora, verum etiam supra omnem modum, mensuram ete numerum, exhausti cruoris profluvio non contentus, per catholice fidei corruptores spiritualis vite operatur exitium inf interitum animarum. Nimirum, si in suis attrocitatibuss propria contra infensos sibi exequeretur odia vel paterna iam deferbuisset in eo incalescens animi feritas, peracte ultionis refrigerio mitigata in his, quos habere videbatur exosos. Sed eius effera crudelitas sic in omnes excandet, ut nec fortune nec vite pepercerit etiam amicorum, nec sexum miseratus fuerit in quibuslibet vel etatem, nec alicuius religionis vel ordinis veneratus honorem, cecans parvulos innocentes, adultos nequiter perimens diversis excogitatis in eos generibus tormentorum, et quod puderosum est cogitare vel eloqui, horrido sectionis impie cultro tam feminas, ut dicitur, eunuchizante quam mares, spem future prolis occidens in superstitibus occisorum, ut ex intentione quodammodo fiat eorum etiam, quos adhuc de lumbis natura non protulit, homicida. testo_esteso: Ad memoriam rei geste in perpetuum. Truculentam unius inhumani hominis rabiem sevamque barbariem, Ezilinia videlicet de Romano, quem dire malignitatis enormitas fecit insignem et mundo non incognita factorum atrocium multitudo spectabilem, humana societas ad elidendum improbas malepotentium tyrannides instituta indigne forsitan pertulisse videtur, set indignius proculdubio noscitur sustulisse. Hic siquidem, sub humani vultus effigie belualem animum retinens, christianib sanguinis e sitibundus et viribus d rigidus alienis, impacabile adversus communia humanitatis federa bellum gerit. Non enim solum ferali hominum excidio debachatur in corpora, verum etiam supra omnem modum, mensuram ete numerum, exhausti cruoris profluvio non contentus, per catholice fidei corruptores spiritualis vite operatur exitium inf interitum animarum. Nimirum, si in suis attrocitatibuss propria contra infensos sibi exequeretur odia vel paterna iam deferbuisset in eo incalescens animi feritas, peracte ultionis refrigerio mitigata in his, quos habere videbatur exosos. Sed eius effera crudelitas sic in omnes excandet, ut nec fortune nec vite pepercerit etiam amicorum, nec sexum miseratus fuerit in quibuslibet vel etatem, nec alicuius religionis vel ordinis veneratus honorem, cecans parvulos innocentes, adultos nequiter perimens diversis excogitatis in eos generibus tormentorum, et quod puderosum est cogitare vel eloqui, horrido sectionis impie cultro tam feminas, ut dicitur, eunuchizante quam mares, spem future prolis occidens in superstitibus occisorum, ut ex intentione quodammodo fiat eorum etiam, quos adhuc de lumbis natura non protulit, homicida. Quis ergo dubitet eum in hominibus non tantum personas persequi, set naturam? Quis ambigat illum, quasi non hominem, humani generis fore publicum inimicum? Hunc ex genere, cum publice damnati heretici h filius fuerit hereticorumque cognatus, hunc etiam ex moribus, cum eum perfidum esse contraria religioni christiane fidei opera manifestent, nos, cum publice opinionis concurrentes assensu, unam de subdolis presumpsimus esse Cant. 2, 15. vulpeculis, que vineam Domini Sabaoth demoliri non cessant, testamentum eterni evangelii corrumpentes. Ad hunc autem nequissime intentionis effectum eo ingenii sui calle processit, quia in quos potuit vasa sceleratissime interfectionis arripiens, per corporalis necis formidinem, que plerumque cadit in fortes, residuos regionis sue viros redegit in parvulos, ut eis, animorum confidentia, libertatis privilegio et veritatis oraculo destitutis, facile per magistros errorum, sub predicti E. presidio ad subvertendas fidelium mentes in marchie Tervisine! partibus emergentes in publicum, perversa infectionis heretice dogmata suggerantur. Execrans preterea commune omnibus gentibus et magnum in Christo et ecclesia matrimonii sacramentum, quod non humane voluntatis inventio statuit, set divine institutionis commendat auctoritas, quod temporaliter orientis ex homine Salvatoris nativitas honoravit, quodque cunctis fere a animantibus suggerit insitus eis ordo nature, damnabili et de typo abhominationis heretice procedente presumptionis audacia separat contra legis evangelice interdictum legitime coniunctionis federe copulatos a Deob, inter complices suos feda conubia et adulterina contubernia coniungendo, ex quibus spuria vitulamina prodeunt, radices altas posteritatis prospere non datura. Nos itaque, quos licet immeritos summus fidelium pastor ad arcendos a redempto sanguine Christi grege ferales impetus, salutem christiani populi ledentes et vitam, nec non ad huiusmodi investigandas assiduis vigiliis capiendasque vulpeculas ecclesie sue voluit presidere, valido clamore christiani sanguinis, quo idem E. terram operuit, nec minus evangelice fidei, quam molitur evertere, periculo excitati, per religiosos viros descendere curavimus et videre!, an idem E. illud circa fidem catholicam naufragium pateretur, quod de ipso et detestanda nunciabant opera et vulgata infamia predicabat. Cum autem ipsi religiosi, super his e cum diligentia inquirentes, eundem, quod de fide Christi non recte sentiret, haberi debere suspectum veris indiciis comperissent, tandem ? ipse ad sedem apostolicam nuncios destinavit, quibus bone memorie.. Sabinensem episcopum concessimus auditorem, coram quo ad iurandum in ipsius E. anima se obtulere paratos, quod idem de Deo et catholica fide credebat, secundum quod Romana tenet ecclesia et docet esse credendum. Set quoniam a dicto episcopo vel a nobis huiusmodi purgatio admissa non extitit, cum in tanto crimine non per nuncios set per propriam personam prestanda esset purgatio coram nobis, sibi prefiximus terminum, quo apostolico se aspectui presentaret, facturus super hiis quod ordo exigeret rationis, oblata sibi de securitate persone in veniendo et redeundo plenaria cautione. Unde quia nec in eodem termino nec post ipsum venire vel d mittere procuravit, ipsum, qui plurium erat alias excommunicationum laqueis irretitus et, quod de fide catholica male sentiret, certa ratione suspectus, anathematis duximus vinculo innodandum, alium ei terminum assignantes, quo in nostra compareret presentia super premissis mandatis ecclesie pariturus, denunciato publice quod nisi usque ad terminum ipsum id faceret, extunc procederemus gravius contra eum iuxta legitimas et canonicas sanctiones. Cum autem venire seu mittere licet ultra terminum diutius expectatus obstinatione dampnabili despexisset et non solum per annum set per biennium vilipensis ecclesie clavibus prefatum sustinuisset contemptibiliter anathema, nos, quia non debebamus ulterius canonicum contra eum differre iudicium, quem tam longum diffugium et tam dura pertinacia reum tanti criminis ostendebant, presertim quia huiusmodi iudicii tarditas periculosam forte aliquibus prebebat audaciam, et quos a malis festinata in unius personame pena compesceret, protelata forsitan ad illa laxaret, eundem E. tamquam hereticum reputantes, decrevimus ipsum habito fratrum nostrorum consilio promulgatis adversus hereticos sanctionibus subiacere, nisi usque ad Kalendas Augusti tunc proximo secuturas 3 coram nobis comparere curaretf, nostris et ecclesie pariturus precise beneplacitis et mandatis, quem siquidem terminum tunc sibi ex multa benignitate apostolice sedis indulsimus, cum eum salvari vellemus potius quam perire. Ipset vero, contra Deum et homines collo rebellionis extento et ad omnem fidei christiane inobedientiam spiritu obfirmatos, tamquam prolapsus in desperationis abyssum et humani pudoris, divini iudicii ac salutaris consilii pertinax aspernator imminentia sibi discrimina quecunque contempsit, et perire potius eligens quam parere, nec in termino sibi ex multa ecclesiastice miserationis lenitate concesso nec postmodum diutius expectatus venire curavit. Nos autem, illius periculo condolentes, adhuc voluimus eius duriciam solita sedis apostolice benignitate mulcere, si forte ad suscipiendum salutis remedium aliqua in eo scintilla sanioris consilii remansisset, ipsumque non solum semel vel secundo, set pluries, immo multotiens ad misericordie iudicium edictis legitimis evocatum duximus prolixis ad convincendam inexcusabilem eius maliciam temporum spaciis expectandum; porro idem sicut aspidis surdissime filius ad omnem monitoris vocem obturans auditum iam per sex annos et amplius vocationis, longanimitatis et expectationis nostre patientia est abusus. Nos igitur, ex hiis attendentes quod diuturnior erga eundem E. tolerantie pietas in communem multorum posset redundare perniciem et ulterior expectatio nil operaretur in eo nisi contumaciam et contemptum, ne tantum malum in medio christiani populi diutius toleratum latius pervagetur, de predictorum fratrum nostrorum consilio, presente fidelium populo, qui in die Cene Domini ex diversis mundi partibus ad apostolorum limina de more confluxit, prefatum Ezilinum? sicut manifestum hereticum sententialiter iudicamus, ipsum excommunicatum et anathematizatum cum dampnatis hereticis deputando, ascripta illis dampnationis stipendia recepturum. Quem si forsan usque ad festum ascensionis Dominice proximo venturum! ad presentiam nostram personaliter venerit, audiemus: quod de habundantissima predicte sedis clementia duximus adiungendum ? Dat. regesto_sintetico: English translation: Nicholas, a minor of the city of Rome, son of the late Nicholas the Perini of Anagni, citizen of Rome. Your party has submitted to us that, as it appears, your brother Pandulf, a citizen of Rome, and Andrew, son of Roger the scribe, a citizen of Anagni, have brought a dispute before Giroldo Filocari, judge palatine and vicar of the beloved son of the noble man senator of the city, regarding the fact that Pandulf was called a legitimate son and Andrew a ward, so that the said judge, after hearing the case and observing the order of law, gave a definitive sentence in favor of the said Pandulf. Although the said Andrew has appealed against this sentence, Bartholomeus Angeli de Romano, a judge of the city of Rome, has confirmed the sentence, as is contained in public instruments. You have humbly petitioned us to confirm the aforesaid sentence with apostolic authority. We, therefore, inclined to your petition, have confirmed the sentence as just, and have supplied the defect that occurred in it, since the said Andrew is said to be a minor and his father's consent to the dispute has not been obtained. We decree that no one may henceforth make any prejudice to this sentence. Given at Lateran, on the 11th day before the Kalends of May, in the 11th year of our pontificate. regesto_sintetico: Translation to English: To G. cardinal of San Eustachio, apostolic legate. Master John of Castellomata, canon of Salerno, has reported to us that the church of Policastro, deprived of a pastor, has asked us to admit, with paternal benevolence, the canon of Salerno to the episcopate. Since we, with paternal benevolence, pursue the canon's merits, we order that if you find that the petition has been canonically processed, you should admit it with our authority, putting aside any difficulty. If, however, the process of the petition is considered to be lacking, since the canon is devoted to us and to the Roman Church and we hope that he will promote the interests of the church of Salerno in the city of Salerno, you should act with the said canon in the negotiation of the petition with benevolence, appointing him bishop and pastor of the church, making the chapter and the subjects of the church show him the obedience and reverence due to a father and pastor; you should make the contradictors pay. Given at Anagni, 14th of September, in the 13th year of our pontificate. regesto_sintetico: Translation: We, Gregory, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our beloved sons, archbishops, bishops, abbots, and other prelates of the church of Parma, and to the community of the same, greeting. The chair of the pastoral office in the church, which is militant, is changed by many popes through frequent succession, because it is not permitted to them to remain for a long time by the condition of mortals. In the triumphant church, which already possesses the region of heaven without being shaken, our savior, the son of God, is the greatest pontiff, who holds the sacerdotal office eternally, remaining in eternal life and subject to the power of death. In this, which is an example of the heavenly on earth, which God's wisdom has built for the consummation of the saints, popes, being circumvented by the weakness of mortality, as men are taken up for God, are constituted for God as men. Hence it is that that, which is ignorant of the grief of widowhood, as it is not subject to the joy and immortality of the eternal bridegroom, this, being bound by the prison of the body, is often forced to resume the laments of its widowhood and to experience tedium. To these laments and tediums, as the Lord pleased, who takes away the spirit of princes, the bowels of the holy church have been made to experience the bitter flow of tears, and its cheeks have been made to be full of bitter tears, with the happy memory of Innocent, our predecessor of happy memory, who was taken away from the world by death, while still necessary and very useful to the Christian people, perhaps on this account, since he was called by the Lord before his time, so that the world, placed in malice, might be recognized as unworthy of his presence, and he might be taken away from the midst of the iniquities, which had long crucified his soul. On the next day, according to the custom of the funeral rites, we and our brothers deliberated on the substitution of a future pastor, and after the solemn celebration of the Masses in honor of the Holy Spirit, devotedly and humbly performed, our brothers turned their eyes to our weakness, which they had before directed to the election of a successor. We, however, being stupefied by the matter above which cannot be said, and weighing the gravity of the business, measuring our strength, pondering prudence, comparing merits, and calculating the necessary expenses of virtues, we, with tears, and up to the point of pain and indignation, excused ourselves to them, and, with the oath of divine judgment, we asked them to take this cup from us and to give it to another stronger. But they, alas, not out of our merits! forced us with the importunity of their request, and, without our consent, they imposed on us the yoke of the apostleship, which we had refused, and they handed us over to the burden of the church, which we had desired to be freed from. Therefore, with a heavy heart and trembling with fear, we have taken up the yoke of the apostleship, trusting in God, who gives abundantly to all who ask, that he will mercifully fill our insufficiency, which we humbly recognize and freely confess. We implore the mercy of divine propitiation, that, by the divine will, he may direct our steps to the path of peace, and, granting us an increase from above, may cause the peace of the church, the concord of the people, and the discipline of morals to arise under our sacerdotal office. You, however, sons, fear God and keep his commandments in the hope of an unfailing reward, trusting in the benevolence and favor of us and the apostolic see, since we intend to follow you as devoted sons, in those things which are according to God. regesto_sintetico: English translation: To the power, counsel and to all the citizens of Genoa in the city and district of Genoa. The Church of God, bearing many afflictions and hardships, has shown you to be strong in faith and devotion, so that in resisting its enemies you have incurred many damages and losses of persons, giving a subject of amazement to many, in that you have shown great firmness of spirit. Indeed, you have added to these great merits other great ones, which is that you have promoted in the overseas lands, which were considered to respect the honor of the Church, the defense and expansion of the Catholic faith, at great expense and labor. And since the said Marco is said to have left no son or heir who could inherit the said county, on account of which the said county is considered to belong to you, since you are the brother of the said Marco on both sides, the said predecessor, because of your devotion to the apostolic see, granted you the said county, together with all its rights and appurtenances, in full, as he had restored and granted it to the said Marco, and de novo he granted it to you in fief by special liberality, not being hindered by the fact that the noble woman Alberia, countess of Modigliano, your mother, daughter of your aunt, or the sons of the same countess claim right in the said county, since they have joined the aforementioned Frederick, the Roman emperor, against the church, and on account of this, they have become unworthy of the grace and favor of the church. But the letters of the same predecessor, although written, could not be bulled, since the said predecessor died before them. We therefore, wishing to pursue this favor, have fully restored the said county with all its rights and appurtenances to you and to your heirs, and have granted it to you and to your heirs de novo in fief by special liberality, in the same way in which it is said that the said predecessor granted it to the said Marco, not being hindered by the letters written by which the said Marco obtained or could obtain from the said see or its legates, by which the effect of the present could be impeded. We wish, however, that after you have held the possession of the said county, you and your heirs shall be bound to render to the Roman church the homage, oath of fealty and other services which other vassals of the said kingdom render for the counties they hold. Nulli etc. nostre restitutionis etc. Given at Naples, by the hand of William, master of the scholars of Parma, vice-chancellor of the Roman church, on April 11, in the 13th indiction, in the year of the Incarnation 1265, of the pontificate of the lord Alexander III, year 1. From your part it has been reported to us that the county of Lucania belonged to your ancestor, Tancred, and that the glorious memory Henry, the Roman emperor, etc. up to the end. Since long ago a dispute arose between you on the one side and the dean, the chapter, and the prepositus of Cambrai on the other side regarding the way to manage the vicedominium, the problem was solved by some wise men, as can be seen in the letters of the dean, the chapter, and the prepositus, who wrote on this matter and sealed with their seal. We, moved by your and their supplications, ratifying the said ordination, confirm it with the apostolic authority and we insert the text of the mentioned letters of the dean, the chapter, and the prepositus in this letter, which is as follows: To all who will see this letter. Salve. We know that the university of Cambrai has knowledge that we, having the administration of the church of Cambrai vacant and exercising the exercise of ecclesiastical jurisdiction and its emoluments in the good of the bishop, have had and have had the administration of the vicedominium in the entire castellany of Cambrai and in the village of Thuni with its pertinences, and in all the movable goods pertaining to the bishop of Cambrai at the time of his death, and also all the revenues of the diocese, which were produced within the limits of the said vicedominium, until the elect, who had received the regalia, had given us his faith, and that on the way to use the aforesaid vicedominium a dispute arose between us and the venerable father N., bishop of Cambrai by the grace of God, regarding the way to manage the vicedominium, which was finally settled by us after many disputes with the counsel of wise and prudent men, in such a way that we quit to the aforesaid bishop and his successors, who will be in the future, all the rights that we had or could have on the vicedominium, in movable goods, which the aforesaid bishop and his successors will have received until the end of his life, in exchange for all the revenues of the bishopric, present and future, which we will have and will make with our administration during this time, adding that if we make greater expenses to keep or defend the goods of the bishop, than the revenues of the bishopric that we will have received outside the aforesaid vicedominium, the future bishop will have to give them to us, without any deduction of the revenues that we will have received during our administration. If we have paid something for the debts of the bishop, contracted before his death, the future bishop will give us all, without any deduction of the revenues that we will have received during our administration. But when the elected bishop, having received the regalia, will come back to the church of Cambrai, we will have the horse, on which he will sit, with the tables, the chests and the other vessels, which will be offered to us in the first communion, as it has been until now. Given on the 9th of July, 1220. Nulli etc. nostre confirmationis etc. Dat. Anagnie, X Kalendas Augusti, anno secundo. Regesto: Papa Honorius III. Gregorius IX. – Episcopo Cameracensi. testo_esteso: Henrico Anglie et Edmundo Sicilie regibus illustribus. Supplicantibus olim nobis humiliter venerabili fratre nostro .. archiepiscopo Tarantasiensi! et dilectis filiis.. electo Saresberiensi? ac.. abbate Westimonasterii Londoniensis 3, nuntiis vestris, ut cum iam instaret festum sancti Michaelis, terminus videlicet tibi, fili rex Anglie, prefixus a nobis ac per te etiam approbatus, infra quem venire vel mittere capitaneum cum militia competenti in regnum Sicilie ac certam pecunie summam nobis et ecclesie Romane pro expensis factis in ipso regno solvere tenebaris, prout in apostolico privilegio confecto super concessione predicti regni facta tibi, fili rex Sicilie, plenius continetur t, prorogare vobis huiusmodi terminum de benignitate apostolica curaremus: nos igitura, ipsorum supplicationibus inclinati, eundem terminum primo usque ad octavas predicti festi? ac deinde usque in diem Mercurii post octavas ipsas tunc 2 primo venturum ° de fratrum nostrorum consilio duximus prorogandumb, sicut plenius litere apostolice continent, quas eisdem nunciis duximus super hoce concedendas. Verum quia interim dicti nuntii petitiones vestras coram nobis et predictis fratribus proponere curaverunt, nos, huiusmodi d petitionibus diligenter auditis et plenius intellectis habitaque diligenti deliberatione cum eisdem fratribus super illis, memoratum terminum ad ipsorum nuntiorum instantiam, quantum ad infrascriptas sententias dumtaxat et penam, a predicto die Mercurii usque ad sex menses computandos a Kalendis mensis Decembris proximo venturi, dummodo ex quo huiusmodi termini prorogatio per venerabilem fratrem nostrum.. archiepiscopum Messanensem, quem pro negotio dicti regni ad te mittimus, vel per eosdem nuntios ad notitiam tuam pervenerit, pecunia decime so ecclesiasticorum proventuum tibi, fili rex Anglie, usque ad certum tempus ab apostolica sede concesse’, tam collecta iam quam de cetero colligenda, nequaquam impendature vel detineatur, sed mercatoribus pro exoneratione debitorum Romane ecclesie libere absque quolibet obstaculo persolvatur!, et si aliqua ipsius quantitas per te vel tuo mandato forsitan est expensa, de illa infra mensem, postquam predicta prorogatio ad notitiam tuam pervenerit, ut premissum est, per te plenarie satisfiat, de predictorum fratrum consilio et assensu taliter prorogamus, videlicet quod interim tu, fili rex Anglie, excommunicationis regnumque tuum interdicti sententias, et tu etiam circa pecuniam?, quam venerabilis frater noster.. Herefordensis episcopus ?, procurator et nuntius tuus, mutuo nomine tuo recepit et pro negotii prefati regni Sicilie prosecutione persolvit et quam etiam tu a tempore memorate concessionis exhibuisti ac te exhibere contigerit in futurum, infrascriptam penam in privilegio predicto contentam, scilicet quod tu et tui heredes nullam contra nos et ecclesiam seu quemquam alium super ipsa pecunia repetitionem habebitis nec aliquam actionem, sed illam ammittetis ex toto, — quibuslibet iuramentis a te super huiusmodi negotio prestitis nequaquam obstantibus — nullatenus incurratis. Nulli ergo — nostre prorogationis etc. Dat. Anagnie, II Nonas Octobris, anno II. II. ... archie piscopo Messanensi. Supplicantibus olim nobis etc. usque: plenarie satisfiat, taliter prorogavimus de predictorum fratrum consilio et assensu, videlicet quod interim idem rex Anglie excommunicationis etc. usque: nequaquam obstantibus — non incurrant. Cum itaque te pro dicto negotio specialiter destinemus, fraternitati tue prorogandi adhuc huiusmodi terminum iuxta 20 prescriptam formam, si expedire videris, usque ad tres menses alios subsequentes liberam de predictorum fratrum consilio concedimus potestatem. Dat. Anagnie, IIII Idus Novembris, anno secundot.

The letter also includes a regesta, a brief summary of the content. Here is the translation of the text in English: "Translation of the letter: To the king of England. Please send your procurators to the pope in order to negotiate with the king of Sicily, Manfred, in regards to your claims to the kingdom of Sicily. If you have already sent them, please inform the pope about their progress and let him know when they will return. If the king of Sicily accepts your proposal, please send him a letter of recognition. If he does not accept, please return the letter of recognition to him. Date: 27 July 1228 The king of England has been informed about the negotiations between the king of Sicily and the pope's procurators and has been asked to send his own procurators to Rome in order to negotiate with the king of Sicily. Translation of the regesto: Pope Honorius III to the king of England, Henry III. Please send your procurators to the pope in order to negotiate with the king of Sicily, Manfred, in regards to your claims to the kingdom of Sicily. testo_esteso: Instrumentum super processibus habitis per magistrum Albertum de Parma notarium domini pape cum rege Anglie et aliis? super facto regni Sicilie. In Dei nomine amen. In presentia sanctissimi patris domini Alexandri pape quarti et venerabilium patrum dominorum G.6 episcopi Tusculani, fratris Iohannis tituli Sancti Laurentii in Lucina et fratris Hugonis tituli Sancte Sabine presbyterorum ac Rlicardi) Sancti Angeli, Olctaviani] Sancte Marie in Via Lata, Ilohannis) Sancti Nicolai in Carcere Tuliano et Olttoboni) Sancti Adriani diaconorum cardinalium et magistri Iordani de Terracina notarii domini pape! ac mei, Bassi notarii camere eiusdem domini, magister Albertus notarius domini pape ad sancta Dei evangelia iuravit, quod per se nullus alius habitus est processus de facto regni Sicilie cum illustri rege Anglie aut Cornubie et Provincie comitibus vel qualibet alia persona, et quod ipse nullam dationem vel concessionem fecit dictis personis vel aliis de dicto recnoa nec faciet in futurum, nisi quatenus continetur in quodam transcripto, quod idem magister dictis domino pape et cardinalibus dedit, assignavit et tradidit in manibus eorundem; iuravit etiam dictus magister se restituturum° camere domini pape omnes litteras, quas de dicto negotio penes se habet et que tangunt dictum negotium seu processum. Tenor autem transcripti predicti sic incipit: Sanctissimo in Christo patri et domino Alexandro Dei gratia sacrosancte Romane ecclesie summo pontifici suus c Albertus dictus notarius se ipsum et pedum oscula beatorum. Ut de processu per me habito cum illustri domino.. rege Anglie ac eius procuratoribus et nuntiis de mandato sancte recordationis domini Innocentii pape quarti predecessoris vestri sanctitatem vestram reddam presentibus certiorem: noveritis me post multos tractatus cum nobilibus viris dominis Richardo Cornubie et Karolo Provincie comitibus recepisse? prefati domini I. litteras in hunc modum: Innocentius etc. magistro Alberto notario nostro? etc. Cum super negotio regni Sicilie, karissimo in Christo filio nostro.. illustri regi Anglie, crucesignato, suo vel filii sui nomine committendo, alias tibi litteras dirigamus, providentie tue concedendi eidem regi vel ipsi filio dictum regnum, si prefatum negotium efficaciter assumpserit, et absolvendi eundem regem a voto crucis illudque in susceptionem et executionem ipsius negotii commutandi plenam et liberam tribuimus de fratrum nostrorum consilio et assensu auctoritate presentium potestatem. Nulli ergo etc. Dat. Perusii, III Idus Aprilis, pontificatus nostri anno X04. Item recepi alias in hanc formam: Innocentius etc. magistro Alberto notario nostro, apostolice sedis legato. Prudentie tue concedendi dilecto filio nobili viro Hyimoni" nato karissimi in Christo filii nostri Anglie regis illustris regnum Sicilie sub decentibus et congruis conditionibus, quas tu nosti 6, si ecclesie ac ipsius regni negocium idem rex efficaciter assumpserit, plenam et liberam tribuimus de fratrum nostrorum consilio et assensu auctoritate presentium potestatem. Nulli ergo etc. Dat. Lateran., XIII Kalendas Ianuarii, pontificatus nostri anno XI°7. Harum igitur auctoritate, cum tractatus habiti cum predictis nobilibus R. et C. comitibus in nichilum devenissent nec esset spes, quod possent resurgere cum effectu, multis difficultatibus emergentibus hinc et inde, ne a prefatus rex a bono proposito, quod concepisse dicebatur, nisi esset voluntati sue satisfactum, in aliquo resiliret, receptis ipsius regis litteris in hac forma: H. Dei gratia rex Anglie etc. venerabili viro magistro A. domini pape notario, apostolice sedis legato, etc. Cum nos et progenitores nostri honores varios et quam plura beneficia receperimus a sancta Romana ecclesia matre nostra, dignum reputamus et rationi consonum, ut in hiis, que honori et utilitati domini pape et ecclesie predicte congruunt et expediunt, exhibeamus nos faciles et benignos. Sane cum idem dominus papa per dilectum clericum nostrum Iohannem et Ambliono decanum Montis Sancti Andree in Sabaudia, eiusdem domini pape capellanumb I, nobis obtulerit regnum Sicilie et Apulie ad opus Edmundi filii nostri et heredum suorum utriusque sexus, in perpetuum tenendum nobis et predicto E., quamdiu vixerimus, et heredibus nostris post ipsum, si idem E. sine liberis obierit quod absit, et idem dominus papa vobis dederit in mandatis, ut predictum regnum ad opus predicti E. nobis ut predictum est conferretis: nos, ob reverentiam ipsius domini pape et ecclesie Romane oblationem predictam approbantes et humiliter admittentes, dilectos clericos nostros prefatum Iohannem de Ambliono et magistrum Pletrum) de Evingam canonicum Herefordensem ad vos duximus transmit20 tendos, constituentes eosdem procuratores nostros speciales et concedentes eisdem plenam et liberam potestatem ad predictum regnum a vobis nomine nostro et prefati E. filii nostri et collationem eiusdem regni recipiendam, secundum quod vos una e cum venerabilibus patribus Olttobono) Sancti Adriani diacono cardinali, Philippo Lugdunensi electo?, Pfetro) Herefordensi episcopo et Thloma) de Sabaudia comite?, Pletrol de Sabaudia, Iohanne Mansel preposito Bervelacensit et Pletro] Cachapor archidiacono Wellensi tam super subsidio nobis faciendo ad predictum negotium prosequendum et consumandum quam super aliis conditionibus omnibus apponendis et removendis duxerint d ordinandum; et ad predictam ordinationem firmiter observandam nos domino pape et ecclesie Romane et vobis per has litteras nostras patentes reddimus obligatos, gratum et firmum habituri, quicquid predicti procuratores nostri fecerint super receptione predicta, prout superius est expressum. In cuius rei testimonium etc. teste me ipso, apud Vesatum5, XII die Februarii, anno regni nostri tricesimo octavo°. litteras meas predictis procuratoribus super concessione regni Sicilie contuli in hac forma: Viris providis et discretis Iohanni de Ambliono decano Sancti Andree in Sabaudia, domini pape capellano, magistro Petro de Ugnia canonico Herefordensi, clericis domini .. illustris regis° Anglie, Albertus domini pape notarius, apostolice sedis legatus, salutem in Domino. Inter ceteros reges mundi . . dominum illustrem regem Anglie Romana ecclesia tamquam eius filium predilectum illaf benivolentie prerogativa prose40 quitur et favoris illoque sinceritatis ardore ac fervore complectitur caritatis, ut donariis gratiarum, honorum extollentia et preeminentia dignitatum ipsum eo spectabilius? preferre desideret principibus et regibus universis, quo sollicitius ipsius beneplacitis complacere, annuere desideriis, necessitatibus subvenire ac adesse utilitatibus hactenus studuit in promptitudine devotionis et fidei puritate. Unde, quod exstitit in eius possibilitate grandius quodque in ipsius facultatibus honorabiliusb, carius habetur et maius, dominus papa una cum suis fratribus prefato regi liberaliter obtulit conferendum, Sicilie videlicet regnum vacans, quod est ecclesie speciale, spe ac credulitate tenens firmissima, quod idem rex detestans indevotionis et perversitatis opera ac abhominans iniquitatis et presumptionis audaciam regum plurium dicti regni, qui nimis forsan eius opibus et delitiis excecati nonnunquam sanctam ecclesiam matrem suam et dominam dicti regni nec non viros religiosos, ecclesias, personas ecclesiasticas gravibus lacesserunt iniuriis et pressuris, tamquam princeps catholicus inclitus et verus adleta ecclesie in fervore perpetue subiectionis, devotionis et obedientie Romane ecclesie perseverantia inconcussa persistat, eius precipuus zelator honoris, ipsius prompte parendo beneplacitis, desideriis annuendo ac ecclesias et personas religiosas et ecclesiasticas ° tamquam Christi familiam regni defensionis et protectionis clipeo defensando, easque plurimis ampliando beneficiis et confovendo presidiis, consiliis et auxiliis oportunis. Prefatus itaque rex, ut facto et opere doceat se, sicut de ipso confidit et presumit ecclesia, in ipsius existere devotione ferventem, haberi ad eius obsequia promptiorem, quodque dictorum domini pape et fratrum votis annuere ac obsecundare desideriis prona mente promptisque affectibus tamquam honestatis et reverentie filius concupiscat, oblationem prefati regni, sibi per vos decanum ex parte domini pape factam nomine Edemundi nati sui, et collationem, de ipso faciendamd a nobis sube quibusdam conditionibus, acceptavit, prout in ipsius super hoc confectis litteris plenius continetur. Quare nos, conferendi ipsi nomine prefati E. filii sui regnum predictum Sicilie habentes ab eisdem domino papa et fratribus sub certis conditionibus plenariam potestatem, illud vobis, dicti domini regis procuratoribus per eundem dominum regem ad hoc specialiter deputatis, predictorum domini regis et Edmundi filii sui nomine ad honorem et gloriam Redemptoris, exsaltationem ecclesie ac ad pacem et quietem ipsius regni totiusque populi Christiani concedimus, iuxta quod nos una cum venerabilibus patribus domino O. Sancti Adriani diacono cardinali, Ph. Lugdunensi electo, P. Herefordensi episcopo et nobilibus viris Thoma de Sabaudia et Petro fratre eius Richemundie comitibus f ac dilectis in Christo Iohanne Mansel preposito Bervalecensi et Petro Cachaporo archidiacono Wellensi tam super subsidios faciendo ad prefati regni negotium prosequendum et ad consumandum quam etiam super conditionibus apponendis et removendis ordinavimus!, a sepedicta ecclesia in feudum, ab eodem E. et eius heredibus perpetuum retinendum, ita tamen quod si dictus dominus papa regni eiusdem collationem nostram huiusmodi ratam et gratam habuerit ac ex certa scientia presentium litterarum tenorem de verbo ad verbum suis duxerit litteris inserendum?, valida sit et firma, alioquin cassa et irrita habeatur et nullius penitus sit momenti. regesto_sintetico: Here are the translation and the regesto for the given text: English translation: To Master Guisone, prelate of the church of Frillaria, of the diocese of Mainz. The matter which was decided etc.: to be communicated. Since, after various processes, had been conducted in the case which was brought between you and Windekind de Waldeke, canon of Paderborn, on the prepositura of Frillaria, which you and the other party each of you claimed belonged to, we have conceded to the part of the present case to be judged by our beloved son H., cardinal of the title of St. Sabina, presbyter. The aforesaid cardinal, after having been informed of the merits of the case and having observed the order of law, and having received from us a special mandate to pronounce and judge on the matter, having heard the parties present, pronounced and declared sentence that the aforesaid prepositura with its rights and pertinences belonged to you by law, and that what had been done in your person regarding it was to be confirmed by us, and that the aforesaid Windekind was to be sententialy removed from the prepositura aforesaid, and that to him a perpetual silence was to be imposed on it, in the fruits received from it and in twenty marks of silver of Cologne, which were taxed and sworn to be spent in the case. We, being pleased with your petitions, having accepted what has been done by the aforesaid cardinal on this matter - notwithstanding the appeal made by the aforesaid sentence to us by the other party, which we consider frivolous - we confirm and corroborate it by the authority of the apostolic see, and we insert in the present writing the tenor of the instrument of the aforesaid sentence, which is as follows: In the name of the Lord amen. The matter which was brought etc. of the prepositura of Frillaria, which the magister Guisone and Windekind de Waldeke, canon of Paderborn, had brought against each other, after various processes had been conducted in it, our beloved son H., cardinal of the title of St. Sabina, presbyter, who had been conceded by us to judge the case, having heard the parties present, having taken the oath of the parties and having heard the proofs, having observed the order of law and having received from us a special mandate to pronounce and judge on the matter, having examined the case and the merits of the parties, and having deliberated on the case, has pronounced and declared sentence that the aforesaid prepositura with its rights and pertinences belongs to the aforesaid magister Guisone by law, and that what has been done in his person regarding it is to be confirmed by us, and that the aforesaid Windekind is to be sententialy removed from the aforesaid prepositura and that to him a perpetual silence is to be imposed on it, in the fruits received from it and in twenty marks of silver of Cologne, which were taxed and sworn to be spent in the case. We confirm and corroborate this sentence by the authority of the apostolic see. We grant him the expenses made and to be made, which he will show at the appropriate time. We decree that the present writing be inserted in the public form and that it be confirmed by our seal. Given at Viterbo, 25 February, year fourth. [Gregorius IX, papa, 1217, Aprilis 10. D. 45, n. 2.]. regesto_sintetico: English translation: To the beloved in Christ daughters, abbess and chapter of the secular church in Quidelingeburg, which does not belong to the Roman church, Halberstadensis diocesis. We are induced by your devotion to follow you with a benevolent favor. Your request to us presented contained that the Halberstadensis bishops who were at the time used to come to your church on Palm Sunday and you used to provide for them at that time with food and that on the feast of the purification of the blessed Mary seven candles and a golden fertron were given to your church by the church of Halberstadt. Moreover, the venerable brother, our, bishop and chapter of Halberstadt, considering that this has caused your church to be harmed, have returned to you and to your church all the aforementioned, which you had given to them in exchange for 200 marks of Halberstadensis silver. We, therefore, with the consent of the wise men, clergy, laymen, ministerials of both churches, decreeing what has been proposed, have received the above-mentioned 200 marks from your church and have released you and your church from the aforementioned. We oblige ourselves and our successors by the present document that neither the right nor the custom nor anything else, under any name, shall be alleged against your church on these matters by us or our successors on any future occasion. We also add that the monastery of Walbeke, about which a dispute arose between your church and our church, we do not recognize in any way as belonging to your church, nor do we recognize in any way the institution or deposition of the prior of that place, nor that the prior of your church shall come to the synod. We add that the monastery of Quidelingeburg enjoys full right and all freedoms in the monastery of Walbeke, which is of the order of St. Benedict, as well as in the monastery of St. Mary of the order of St. Augustine and in Wonethusendi, with the addition that the prior of the place, who is at the time, shall appoint a priest for the parish of the village of Walbeke, who shall receive the care of souls from the archdeacon of the place. The laymen: Fridericus comes de Kircberge, Wernerus de Sheronbeke, Evetardus de Suseliz, nobiles. The ministerials of our church: Iohannes de Katersleve, Nicolaus de Heymburg, Alvericus pincerna, Gevehardus de Slage, Iacobus de Severthusen, Henricus Isenborde. The ministerials of Quidelingeburgensis ecclesie: Bernardus marscalcus, Bertoldus de Ditforde, Tidericus pincerna, Tydericus filius suus, Iohannes de Wederstide, Henricus de Aqua, Iohannes Knotel, Octo camerarius, Iohannes Albus, Henricus et Bernardus fratres de Ditforde, Olricus et Iohannes fratres de Morsleveb, Henricus de Grotunge, Thidericus Marroch, Conradus et Gerardus fratres cognomento Struven et alii quamplures milites et servi. REGESTO: Gregorius IX, papa, Gregorio de Croye, abbati, et capitulo monasterii Quidelingeburgensi, Halberstadensis ecclesie pertinenti, ecclesiam Walbeke cum pertinentiis ad eam pertinentibus monasterium Quidelingeburgense relinquit, ac omni iure et omni exceptione se et successores suos ab iisdem relinquit, promittens quod eadem monasterio seu successoribus eius non reusabitur, nec in tempore, nec in preposito loci illius, nec in libertatibus aut iuribus ipsius monasterii, quatenus ecclesia Quidelingeburgensis in omnibus libertatibus et iuribus omni plenitudine gaudebit. regesto_sintetico: Translation in English: To the illustrious King Ottokar of Bohemia, beloved son in Christ. We have learned that the Pope Gregory IX, on behalf of the blessed Peter, who has the power to bind and loose, has dispensed some people from the obligation to observe the law, if it is necessary. You had proposed to us that a noble woman, Margaret, former queen of the Romans, had taken the habit of the sisters of the Order of Preachers in the province of Trèves and had sworn to live according to the Rule of the said Order. However, she married you. Therefore, you and Margaret separated and you both recognized that you could not live without harm. We have been informed that you have married Kunigunde, daughter of Bela IV, King of Hungary, who is your fourth cousin and your third affine. However, we have been told that peace has been maintained in Hungary and Bohemia, and that many people have been liberated from slavery and that many other benefits have been obtained. Therefore, we, after having considered these facts, declare that your marriage to Margaret was not valid, and we dispense you and Kunigunde, with the apostolic authority, to remain in that marriage. regesto_sintetico: English translation: We, Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all who shall see or hear these presents, greetings. To our beloved son, the king of Bohemia. We have received with paternal affection the beloved son master Peter, your chaplain and nuncio, and the letters which he presented to us on your behalf, and also those which the letters contain, and we have diligently considered and understood, in the abundance of your devotion towards the Roman mother church, you have earned deserved praise. Moreover, we have learned that the venerable father, the archbishop of Mainz, has indicated to you and to other princes of the kingdom of the Germans, to whom the election of the Roman king pertains, a certain day and place to convene personally to treat the election and creation of the future king, and that in the same region it is rumored that some of the aforementioned princes intend to propose Conrad, the son of Conrad, son of the late Frederick, emperor of the Romans, for the imperial throne. We, however, attentive to the fact that you have dedicated yourself with great care to informing us about these matters, and that we have been informed about this through the letters, which we have received from you, and through the nuncio, whom we commend to you, we have devotedly offered to the Lord the prayers of the heart, that we may be able to render you due thanks for your devotion towards us and towards the aforesaid church. Therefore, we have thought it necessary to entrust to you the safeguard of the church, which has been sorely afflicted by the injuries and oppressions of the aforesaid Conrad and his ancestors and progenitors, and which is in great danger, if the aforesaid Conrad should be promoted to the imperial dignity. Therefore, we have entrusted to the archbishop of Mainz and to the other ecclesiastical princes, coelectors of the aforesaid Conrad, the task of ensuring that he is not elected or nominated as king, and we have threatened them with excommunication, if they fail to do so. Moreover, we have forbidden all the coelectors, who have given their consent to the aforesaid Conrad, to proceed with the election or nomination of the aforesaid Conrad, and we have threatened them with excommunication, if they fail to do so. And we have forbidden them to proceed with the election or nomination of the aforesaid Conrad, even if they are not excommunicated, and we have threatened them with excommunication, if they fail to do so. We also entrust to you the task of ensuring that the aforesaid Conrad is not elected or nominated as king, and that you do not participate in this election, and that you do not give your consent or support to the aforesaid Conrad. We request and exhort you to take care to consider these things attentively and wisely, so that if you are to participate in the election of the king, you take care not to be involved in the excommunication of the coelectors who have given their consent to the aforesaid Conrad. regesto_sintetico: Translation: The Pope Gregory IX, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the podestà, the captain, the elders, the council and the common sense of the city of Sens. The mother, who bore you in baptism, namely the Church of Sens, seeing that you wander in the ways of unfaithfulness and perils, frequently called you through letters and called you back to the way of salvation and righteousness, praying you to leave behind the persecutor and to return to the sweet bosom of the mother, from which you were born of your sins to others. And although you have used the mother's advice and have been able to use the hardness of the sons, we, who preside over the government of this church, although we are not worthy, not wanting to abandon the pursuit of this pious proposal, have devised ways and means to recall you to the bosom of this mother church in a healthy way. And we have thought that we would be able to proceed more fully and more effectively in this matter if we were to settle the disputes and the causes that the Roman church has against certain individuals of your city, who have received a certain sum of money and have received a great sum of money for the church in the kingdom of England and elsewhere, and which they have not yet returned to the church. And we have made Peter Scott and his companions and some other citizens of your city, who are known to have received and have kept these sums of money, come to our presence, to give account of the sums of money received and given, and if the church were found to have any right over them, we would take it from them and we would give it to you to pay to us. And since these same Peter Scott and his companions and other many citizens of yours have been constituted before the apostolic seat by your devotion, and have promised us that they would proceed with us in all truth and purity, but finally they have turned to subterfuges and lies, in order to circumvent us and the church, and have refused to give us account of the aforesaid sums of money and have refused to return to us the apostolic letters, as they have promised, we have therefore, with the knowledge of your devotion, deprived them of the benefit of the four thousand Tournois pounds, which we had intended to remit to them, and we have commanded them to pay to us and to the church the full amount of what they owe to the church. Since the same Peter Scott and his companions have abandoned the apostolic seat, refusing to give satisfaction and to return the aforesaid letters, we have sent you this present letter, so that, having known the facts, you may compel them, as you have been authorized, to pay to the church the full amount of what they owe and to return to us the aforesaid letters, and that, even if you have adhered to the adversary of the church, you do not tolerate that the goods of the church are detained by any of your citizens. We have therefore sent this letter to your community, asking and urging you to be attentive to our innocence, and to compel the aforesaid Peter Scott and his companions to pay to us and to the church the full amount of what they owe, and to return to us the aforesaid letters, if we find a way to proceed in this matter, so that the church does not lose its right. regesto_sintetico: Translation: Translation: To all our and the Roman Church's faithful, and to all Christ's faithful. We issued citations to Manfred, the former prince of Tarentum, to appear before us with a certain number of mandatories on certain articles, but he did not come. Now, since the time of the citation has passed, we have delayed the procedure, as we said in our letter, until the octave of the feast of St. Martin, but, since it has approached, we have given him a safe conduct to come and to stay for eight days. However, we have prohibited him from bringing more than 800 people, including 100 armed men, and 700 wagons, under penalty of anathema. If he were to transgress this prohibition, the letters of safe conduct would be void and inane. We have entrusted to two friars, Gualascus and Jacob, to deliver the letters to him and to require the oath from him. Dat. 3 Id. Nov. anno 6° I. (1247-1248). Regesto: Gregorius IX Gregorio de Montelongo, archiepiscopo Salernensi, iussit, ut Manfredo, principi Tarentino, per iuramentum et per mandatorum fidem securitatem in veniendo ad sedem apostolicam pro negotio fidei ac per octo dies postquam a papatu redeundum licentiam habuerit, et de non offendendo terram ecclesie vel fideles ipsius, prenuntiatam de nullo armato, persona vel evectorum numero ultra taxatum, assignaret. Si contra hanc prohibitionem terram ecclesie ingrederetur, tunc anathematis vinculo innodaretur. Dat. Urb. III Id. Nov. anno VI. (1247-1248).

regesto_sintetico: English translation: To the people of the island of Marthanet, our faithful. Just as the world, growing worse and worse, is affected by an insatiable desire to dominate, the burning desire for wealth has grown, and the unbridled greed of those who persecute the church of Rome has increased so much that not only do they tear apart with cruel bites the temporal goods of the faithful and those who are vassals of the same church, who must defend and maintain them by the debt of faith and also recover them, but also, not fearing the hands of those who extend over them, they seize and occupy the castles and other goods, which the devoted and noble generosity of the ancient Catholic emperors and princes magnificently endowed the church. Since, therefore, the common people of the city of Urbino have turned their greedy eyes towards you and the island of Marthan, which is a special possession of the apostolic see, and since the noble men, Jacob and his brothers, sons of the late Guittone de Bisenti, of the diocese of Urbino, have for a long time occupied the said island in prejudice to the apostolic see, and since you have bound yourselves to them with certain obligations and promises, binding you to them in derogation of the rights, jurisdictions, and dominion of the said see: we, who have deemed the said island to be returned to the right and property of the said church, wishing to provide for you and the church of the apostolic see on these matters, cancel, annul, vacate, and render void and invalid all promises, obligations, pacts, conditions, and other things by which you have bound yourselves to the common people and to Jacob and his brothers, even if they are under penalty or oath, and we absolve you from such promises, obligations, pacts, conditions, etc., and we decree that you are not bound by the documents made to them. Therefore, etc. Given at Rome, 16 November, in the year 1225. REGESTO:Gregorius IX episcopo Urbini et Marthanensis insule hominibus. Quod de insula Marthanensi promissiones, obligationes, pactiones, conditiones, etc. quam ipsi communiter et Jacobus et fratres eius supradicti tenuerint, omnes cassamus, annullamus, evacuamus, irritamus. Dat. 1225, VIII Kal. Dec. (16 Nov.).

regesto_sintetico: Translation from Latin to English: To be remembered for all eternity. We, having understood that the common of Spoleto was holding the occupied land of Arnulphs, pertaining to the Roman Church, have sent our beloved son, Raynerius of Viterbo, our chaplain to Spoleto, with our letters in mandates, to recall the land to the Church and to order that it be handed over to the bishop and the community of Spoleto under a certain penalty, so that it be permitted to be governed by them. Having executed this mandate, the aforesaid chaplain, having gone to the castle of Porcarie, located in the land of the aforesaid Arnulphs, was assaulted by the aforesaid community, which had gathered there in a hostile manner, and was driven out of the castle, and the castle was taken by them. Wherefore, since such an excess of temerity has reached our ears, we have commanded our beloved son, Peter of Ferentino, our chaplain, whom we have sent there on this account, to summon the aforesaid community to appear before us at a certain time, to show the documents they possess on the land and to make the account of their rights, so that they may be convicted of their malice. Olim intellecto, quod commune Spoletanum detinebat occupatam terram Arnulphorum? ad Romanam ecclesiam pertinentem, nos dilectum filium magistrum Raynerium de Viterbio capellanum nostrum ! Spoletum duximus destinandum, sibique dedimus nostris litteris in mandatis, ut in consilio loci eiusdem dictam terram ad demanium eiusdem ecclesie revocaret ac eidem communi ex parte nostra sub certa pena preciperet, ut terram eandem nobis et eidem ecclesie dimittentes, permitterent ipsam per nuntios nostros regi et libere gubernari. Cumque dictus capellanus fuisset in hac parte mandatum apostolicum executus et tandem ad castrum Porcarie situm in eadem Arnulphorum terra se personaliter contulisset, iidem commune, ad dictum castrum universaliter et hostiliter accedentes, illud obsidere ac prefatum capellanum existentem ibidem, ut exiret exinde, compellere presumpserunt, invadendo temere castrum ipsum pro sue libito voluntatis. Unde, cum tante temeritatis excessus ad nostram audientiam pervenisset, nos dictum commune per dilectum filium magistrum Petrum dictum Romanum de Ferentino, capellanum nostrum, quem illuc propter hoc specialiter misimus, fecimus peremptorie citari, ut certo die comparerent per sufficientem syndicum coram nobis, super hiis mandatis apostolicis parituri et ostensuri nichilominus, quecumque iura se habere crederent in terra predicta. Porro quidam ambassatores ex parte dicti communis ad nostram presentiam accedentes exhibuerunt nobis et fratribus nostris transcripta quarundam litterarum, quas super dicta terra se habere dicebant, transcriptum videlicet quarundam litterarum felicis recordationis Innocentii pape predecessoris nostri, continens inter alia, quod idem predecessor bone memorie Rlayneriol Sancte Marie in Cosmidin diacono cardinali in patrimonio beati Petri in Tuscia, ducatu Spoletano et marchia Anconitana commisit in spiritualibus et temporalibus vices suas, concedens ei exercendi, quicquid honori ipsius ecclesie et utilitati fidelium illarum partium expedire videret in utrisque, liberam potestatem?. Insuper exhibuerunt transcriptum cuiusdam articuli contenti, ut dicebant, in litteris dicti cardi25 nalis, tunc in eodem ducatu vices gerentis huiusmodi3; qui quidem articulus talis erat: videlicet quod idem cardinalis volens exaudire petitiones Spoletanorum, quantum indulte sibi auctoritatis se possibilitas extendebat, predictam terram Arnulforum eisdem in fidelitate ac devotione sedis apostolice perseverantibus concedebat. Exibuerunt et aliud transcriptum quarundam litterarum dicti predecessoris t, in quo narrabatur, quod idem cardinalis quedam eis duxerat concedenda quodque idem predecessor confirmabat, quod per eundem cardinalem provide factum erat. Tertium quoque transcriptum produxerunt quarundam litterarum pie memorie Alexandri pape predecessoris nostri S, quod erat continentie talis: videlicet quod idem predecessor A. omnia castra, villas, tenimenta, iura, conditiones et consuetudines eorum Spoletane civitatis et diocesis, 35 sicut ea omnia iuste ac pacifice possidebant, eisdem Spoletanis de novo concessit et auctoritate apostolica confirmavit. Nos vero, transcriptis eisdem non adhibentes fidem, sicut nec etiam debebamus, dictis ambassatoribus nomine prefati communis certum prefiximus terminum, in quo per sufficientem comparerent syndicum coram nobis, ostensuri autenticas litteras et quascumque alias de terra prefata rationes haberent, nostrisque super hiis parituri mandatis. Ipsi autem Spoletani nec sufficienter in eodem termino apostolico se conspectui presentarunt neque nobis aliquas scripturas autenticas obtulerunt. Nos autem, volentes ad eorum malitiam convincendam, ut ipsorum contumaciam et pertinaciam nostra patientia superaret, dictum commune per eundem capellanum iterato peremtorie citari fecimus, ut infra certum terminum post citationem suam cum omnibus iuribus, munimentis, privilegiis et litteris autenticis ac rationibus suis coram nobis per ydoneum syndicum comparerent, denuntiato eisdem, quod, sive taliter venirent sive forte venire contempnerent, nos nichilominus — eorum absentia non obstante — ad pronunciationem, sententiam et mandata procedere curaremus in ipso negotio, prout expedire honori nostro et ecclesie prefate videremus ac iustitia suaderet. In ipso itaque termino syndico dicti communis ad nostram presentiam accedente, tam per eum quam alios nonnulla pro parte dicti communis fuerunt proposita coram nobis, super quibus nos et fratres nostri plenam audientiam eis duximus exhibendam. Nulli ergo etc. nostre condempnationis etc. Dat. apud Urbemveterem, X Kalendas Februarii, anno H°l.
