Dudum ad apostolice sedis perlato notitiam, quod Conradinus, nepos quondam Friderici olim Romanorum imperatoris, inconsulte nimis et temerarie ambitionis spiritu concitatus non solum ad obtinendum Romanum conabatur imperium, sed et sibi regnum Sicilie intitulare non veritus, sub eiusdem regni titulo sibi nomen regium ascribebat, quodque cum aliquibus inimicis ecclesie diversarum Italie partium scelestas iniens factiones, suas per civitates et loca varia sub premissa intitulatione typario regie maiestatis impressas litteras destinando, turbare pacem ecclesie ac populum commovere in nostrum et ipsius ecclesie ac carissimi in Christo filii nostri Caroli regis Sicilie illustris discrimen et preiudicium nitebatur: nos in festo dedicationis Basilice beatorum apostolorum Petri et Pauli pontificatus nostri anno secundo in hac maiori ecclesia Viterbiensi, presente tunc multitudine copiosa fidelium, de fratrum nostrorum consilio eidem Conradino districte precepimus, ut a premissis penitus abstineret, districtius inhibentes, ne similia ulterius presumeret aut quomodolibet usurparet. 20 Prohibuimus etiam universis etc. ut p. 667, lin. 20 — p. 668, lin. 8 usque: subiacere ". Cumque prefatus Conradinus, precepta, inhibitiones et comminationes huiusmodi presumptuose contempnens et nequaquam abstinens a premissis, suos in Tuscia diceretur vicarios ordinasse etc. ut p. 683, lin. 33 — p. 684, lin. 2 usque: ac specialiter incolas castri Sancti Miniati Lucane diocesis !, qui spretis etc. ut p. 684, lin. 3—21 usque: Demum vero in festo dedicationis Basilice Principis Apostolorum, pro eo quod idem Conradinus prefatas nostras inhibitiones etc. ut p. 684, lin. 22—32 usque: proclamans, alias contra inhibitiones, comminationes et sententias predictas temere veniendo: nos de fratrum eorundem consilio Conradinum eundem in hac eadem ecclesia denuntiavimus latam in eum per nos ut premittitur excommunicationis sententiam incurrisse etc. ut p. 684, lin. 41 — p. 685, lin. 14 usque: tenebantur eidem. Omnes vero et singulos, qui eidem Conradino in predictis prestarent auxilium, consilium vel favorem, et spécialiter Ludovicum ducem Bavarie, .. comitem Tyroli, Bosum de Dovaria, Manfredum Malet, qui se comitem camerarium nominabat, et Conradum Trinza, quos notorium erat ipsi Conradino in predictis assistere ipsumque fovere, ceterosque marchiones, comites, barones et alios, cuiuscumque forent dignitatis aut status, qui eius nuncios seu litteras contra predictas inhibitiones nostras veniendo temerario ausu receperant seu alias prestiterant eidem auxilium, consilium vel favorem, excommunicationis, civitates vero, castra et cetera loca, que predictas nostras inhibitiones contra ipsas veniendo contempserant, interdicti declaravimus sententiis subiacere ac nichilominus de novo ex eisdem causis, exigente proculdubio aucta eorum ex tanti temporis continuatione perfidia, similibus sententiis duximus innodandos. Specialiter autem terram memorati Ludovici ducis Bavarie, nisi dux ipse infra duos mensesb exinde computandos prorsus a Conradini eiusdem in premissis favore desisteret, ecclesiastico extunc supposuimus interdicto. Omnes vero marchiones etc. ut p. 685, lin. 32 — p. 686, lin. 11 usque: libere capienda, aliis etiam civitatibus et locis Italie, que dictos Conradinum vel capitaneum seu gentem suam contra prefatas nostras inhibitiones, comminationes et sententias deinceps reciperent, comminantes aperte nos ad similes privationum penas, prout foret expediens, processuros. Verum prefatus Conradinus, ut ad nichilum deveniat velut aqua decurrens, ad Ps. 57, s. sententias, monitiones et comminationes nostras sicut aspis surda suas prorsus aures obturans, nec premissis inhibitionibus acquievit nec expavit sententias nec monitionibus paruit nec perversitatis sue propositum comminationibus immutavit; sed in precipitium preceps ruens et premissis excessibus, illos pro viribus continuando, institit et quos potuit nichilominus novos adiecit. TESTO ESTESO:Ad notitiam presentium et memoriam futurorum. Visceribus matris ecclesie gravi diebus istis inquietudine concitatis et turbationis insolite vulnere lacessitis, contra cor nostrum° impellimur novum cogitare consilium, quod extrema necessitas exigit, coacte c benivole voluntatis, quam dilectio paterna conservat, terminos preterire. Licet enim ipsius matris fecunditas cunctos populos Christiane fidei professores uberum suorum lacte reficiat sitque de illorum salubri statu sollicita, cives tamen Romanos potissime, quos peculiares filios divina sibi dispositio statuit, gerit specialius in intimo gremio caritatis et eos, quos semper amplis sublimare consuevit honoribus, potiori affectione prosequitur et in eorum salute plenius delectatur, sicut predecessorum nostrorum Romanorum gesta pontificum beneficiorum largitione gratuita, privilegiorum concessione munifica, spiritualium et temporalium honorum exhibitione largiflua et prerogativa multarum ac grandium dignitatum clara demonstratione testantur. Decens profecto fuisse censemus et debitum Urbem et Urbis incolas gratiis muniri magnificis et donis sublimibus decorari, quam apostolorum sanguine consecratam superna clementia statuit caput orbis, constitutis inibi sedis apostolice precipuis fundamentis. Hii sunt incole, soliti sedem ipsam veneratione debita colere, fructus ei devotionis impendere ac in adversitatibus ferventer assistere veluti vigiles et indefessi libertatis ecclesiastice defensores, cuius promovendo negotium temporibus oportunis proprium agi commodum reputabant. Inde fit, quod quanto filiis matris liberalitate maiorum incrementa munerum provenerunt, tanto gravius et indecentius veritatis iudicio cernitur, si per eos honori compensetur obprobrium et pro beneficiis rependantur offense, a quorum gratiis manum mater provida non subduxit, quinimmo novas liberaliter adicit et munit robore confirmationis antiquas. Inter alia quoque, nec mirum, grandis et miranda causa nobis turbationis emersit ac doloris perfodit aculeo mentem nostram, quod cum Conradinum, dampnati stipitis surculum, hostem ecclesie manifestum, omnesque fautores, consiliarios et adiutores ipsius excommunicationis sententia publice duxerimus innodandos, quod ad cunctorum fidelium, maxime Romanorum, potuit notitiam pervenire, Galvanus Lancea!, maledictionis filius ab olim viam dampnationis ingressus, eiusdem Conradini vexillis explicitis et erectis Urbem ingrediens, usque Lateranum a Romanis pomposo fastu sibi occurrentibus obviam habita comitiva pervenit, multiplicis honoris exhibitione preventus?; cuius iidem Romani debuerant adventum, ne contagione macularentur ipsius, potius aspernari. Et quidem, cum tam detestabilis et horrendus excessus, nobis et fratribus nostris odibilis, innotuisset tam senatori quam civibus, ipsi, non ut decuit penitentes erroris, sed excedendo lascivius patrantes graviora prioribus, prefatum Galvanum ad eorum ludos, ut ipsis illuderet, venientem non solum pari, sed maiori fastu, sicut accepimus, receperunt et munificentius honorarunt. Quis igitur admirari sufficeret urbem tam magnificam, tantis dotatam viris prudentibus, viris devotione conspicuis, viris alti consilii, sic improvide, sic indevote, sic inconsulte dilapsam, ut non solum vitare despiciat divine maiestatis offensam aut dicte matris iniuriam et discrimen, verum etiam fame proprie, cuius gloria inextricabilem per hoc probatur recipere maculam, dispendium non advertit, ducta miserabiliter in errorem sub quodam vehiculo cecitatis. Huius nempe talis eversio non minus quam dampnum ecclesie nos incitat ad dolendum, cum vertatur in paterne sinceritatis angustiam status oberrantium filiorum. Verum ipsi Romani, predictis insolentiis non contenti, quosdam alios eiusdem nuncios Conradini suas, ut audivimus, litteras deferentes honorifice recipere postmodum ac eis in Capitolio congregare consilium non vitarunt, solemni eis audientia prestita super his, que proponere voluerunt. Hec quidem propositio, sicut est verisimile, illusione non caruit; nam ille quondam Fredericus coluber tortuosus, de cuius venenosa radice Conradinus iam prodiisse videtur in regulum cuiusque doctrinam eius ministri dolosis fictionibus imitantur, adulationibus, promissionibus et fellitis versutiis fideles evertere nitebatur et in agro mentium illorum proditionis zizaniam seminabat; et munitus Sathane furentis astutia, sepe movebat in Urbe discidium, sponsam Christi ponere satagens in ruinam, cuius sanguinem, illius satiatus angustiis, ad eius exterminium sitiebat. Non autem credimus, quod enormes iniurias, irreparabilia dampna, cuiuslibet extimationem excedentia pretii, et atroces offensas, que dictus Fredericus Romanis hostiliter intulit, prout anguste obsidionis opprobrium et multorum meniorum, castrorum ac turrium memorialis subversio representat, preter innumera scelera, quibus ad iram contra se ac posteritatem suam Dominum provocavit, illa propositio contineret; nam et proponentes forte minus audacter pulpitum conscendissent, et audientium animi non tanta suscepissent iocunditate sermonem. testo_esteso: Ad notitiam presentium et memoriam futurorum. Visceribus matris ecclesie gravi diebus istis inquietudine concitatis et turbationis insolite vulnere lacessitis, contra cor nostrum° impellimur novum cogitare consilium, quod extrema necessitas exigit, coacte c benivole voluntatis, quam dilectio paterna conservat, terminos preterire. Licet enim ipsius matris fecunditas cunctos populos Christiane fidei professores uberum suorum lacte reficiat sitque de illorum salubri statu sollicita, cives tamen Romanos potissime, quos peculiares filios divina sibi dispositio statuit, gerit specialius in intimo gremio caritatis et eos, quos semper amplis sublimare consuevit honoribus, potiori affectione prosequitur et in eorum salute plenius delectatur, sicut predecessorum nostrorum Romanorum gesta pontificum beneficiorum largitione gratuita, privilegiorum concessione munifica, spiritualium et temporalium honorum exhibitione largiflua et prerogativa multarum ac grandium dignitatum clara demonstratione testantur. Decens profecto fuisse censemus et debitum Urbem et Urbis incolas gratiis muniri magnificis et donis sublimibus decorari, quam apostolorum sanguine consecratam superna clementia statuit caput orbis, constitutis inibi sedis apostolice precipuis fundamentis. Hii sunt incole, soliti sedem ipsam veneratione debita colere, fructus ei devotionis impendere ac in adversitatibus ferventer assistere veluti vigiles et indefessi libertatis ecclesiastice defensores, cuius promovendo negotium temporibus oportunis proprium agi commodum reputabant. Inde fit, quod quanto filiis matris liberalitate maiorum incrementa munerum provenerunt, tanto gravius et indecentius veritatis iudicio cernitur, si per eos honori compensetur obprobrium et pro beneficiis rependantur offense, a quorum gratiis manum mater provida non subduxit, quinimmo novas liberaliter adicit et munit robore confirmationis antiquas. Inter alia quoque, nec mirum, grandis et miranda causa nobis turbationis emersit ac doloris perfodit aculeo mentem nostram, quod cum Conradinum, dampnati stipitis surculum, hostem ecclesie manifestum, omnesque fautores, consiliarios et adiutores ipsius excommunicationis sententia publice duxerimus innodandos, quod ad cunctorum fidelium, maxime Romanorum, potuit notitiam pervenire, Galvanus Lancea !, maledictionis filius ab olim viam dampnationis ingressus, eiusdem Conradini vexillis explicitis et erectis Urbem ingrediens, usque Lateranum a Romanis pomposo fastu sibi occurrentibus obviam habita comitiva pervenit, multiplicis honoris exhibitione preventus?; cuius iidem Romani debuerant adventum, ne contagione macularentur ipsius, potius aspernari. Et quidem, cum tam detestabilis et horrendus excessus, nobis et fratribus nostris odibilis, innotuisset tam senatori quam civibus, ipsi, non ut decuit penitentes erroris, sed excedendo lascivius patrantes graviora prioribus, prefatum Galvanum ad eorum ludos, ut ipsis illuderet, venientem non solum pari, sed maiori fastu, sicut accepimus, receperunt et munificentius honorarunt. Quis igitur admirari sufficeret urbem tam magnificam, tantis dotatam viris prudentibus, viris devotione conspicuis, viris alti consilii, sic improvide, sic indevote, sic inconsulte dilapsam, ut non solum vitare despiciat divine maiestatis offensam aut dicte matris iniuriam et discrimen, verum etiam fame proprie, cuius gloria inextricabilem per hoc probatur recipere maculam, dispendium non advertit, ducta miserabiliter in errorem sub quodam vehiculo cecitatis. Huius nempe talis eversio non minus quam dampnum ecclesie nos incitat ad dolendum, cum vertatur in paterne sinceritatis angustiam status oberrantium filiorum. Verum ipsi Romani, predictis insolentiis non contenti, quosdam alios eiusdem nuncios Conradini suas, ut audivimus, litteras deferentes honorifice recipere postmodum ac eis in Capitolio congregare consilium non vitarunt, solemni eis audientia prestita super his, que proponere voluerunt. Hec quidem propositio, sicut est verisimile, illusione non caruit; nam ille quondam Fredericus coluber tortuosus, de cuius venenosa radice Conradinus iam prodiisse videtur in regulum cuiusque doctrinam eius ministri dolosis fictionibus imitantur, adulationibus, promissionibus et fellitis versutiis fideles evertere nitebatur et in agro mentium illorum proditionis zizaniam seminabat; et munitus Sathane furentis astutia, sepe movebat in Urbe discidium, sponsam Christi ponere satagens in ruinam, cuius sanguinem, illius satiatus angustiis, ad eius exterminium sitiebat. Non autem credimus, quod enormes iniurias, irreparabilia dampna, cuiuslibet extimationem excedentia pretii, et atroces offensas, que dictus Fredericus Romanis hostiliter intulit, prout anguste obsidionis opprobrium et multorum meniorum, castrorum ac turrium memorialis subversio representat, preter innumera scelera, quibus ad iram contra se ac posteritatem suam Dominum provocavit, illa propositio contineret; nam et proponentes forte minus audacter pulpitum conscendissent, et audientium animi non tanta suscepissent iocunditate sermonem. TESTO ESTESO:Ad certitudinem presentium et memoriam futurorum. Frequenter universis Christi fidelibus publice ac expresse prohibere curavimus, ne Conradino, nato quondam Conradi olim Fr. quondam Romanorum imperatoris filii, sicut regi Sicilie scriberent nec ab ipso litteras velut a rege Sicilie vel sub regia, ratione regni Sicilie, intitulatione vel denominatione reciperent, nec cum armis vel sine armis, facto vel verbo aut alias quomodolibet ad turbandam ecclesie Romane pacem vel contra carissimum in Christo filium nostrum Carolum Sicilie regem illustrem prestarent ei auxilium, consilium vel favorem. Specialiter autem marchionibus, comitibus, baronibus, civitatibus, communitatibus et universitatibus castrorum, villarum et quorumcunque locorum Italie duximus prohibendum, ne ipsius Conradini dominio vel regimini se supponerent aut eum vel pro eo seu in favorem ipsius alium in potestatem admitterent vel rectorem, quocunque nomine censeatur, vel ei sive alii pro ipso seu in favorem eius dominium aut posse aliquod in se, terras aut districtus suos quocunque ingenio aut machinatione concederent, nec societatem, coniurationem seu fedus aliquod inire presumerent cum eodem seu alio in auxilium vel favorem ipsius. Illos vero, qui contra premissa vel aliquod premissorum per se vel per alium quocunque dolo. arte vel machinatione facerent, cuiuscunque forent preminentie, dignitatis aut status, excommunicationis sententiam, quam extunc in eos tulimus, incurrere voluimus ipso facto. Et nichilominus tam personis ecclesiasticis quam secularibus, cuiuscunque forent dignitatis, preminentie seu status, varias penas, si non observarent prohibitionem huiusmodi, comminantes, civitates, communitates et universitates quaslibet, que prefatam prohibitionem nostram violare quocunque dolo, ingenio vel machinatione temptarent, voluimus interdicti sententie subiacere. Specialiter autem marchionibus, comitibus, baronibus, civitatibus, communitatibus et universitatibus castrorum, villarum et quorumcunque locorum Italie duximus prohibendum, ne ipsius Conradini dominio vel regimini se supponerent aut eum vel pro eo seu in favorem ipsius alium in potestatem admitterent vel rectorem, quocunque nomine censeatur, vel ei sive alii pro ipso seu in favorem eius dominium aut posse aliquod in se, terras aut districtus suos quocunque ingenio aut machinatione concederent, nec societatem, coniurationem seu fedus aliquod inire presumerent cum eodem seu alio in auxilium vel favorem ipsius. TESTO ESTESO:Ad notitiam presentium et memoriam futurorum. Notum est omnibus non solum Christicolis sed etiam aliarum diversarum populis nationum, quod excellens prosapia generis carissimi in Christo filii nostri.. regis Castelle ac Legionis illustris, apud Deum et Romanam ecclesiam inclita devotione 15 prefulgens, Romanos pontifices et sedem apostolicam semper filialibus studiis honoravit ac defendere studuit decorem et privilegium ecclesiastice libertatis, nec ab hiïs idem rex et progenitores sui manum retraxerunt vel animum, quin circa talia devota et assidua fuerint operatione constantes, prout eorum gesta prelucida manifestant. Turbamur igitur nec indigne dolemus, quod de tam clara et excellenti progenie filius exasperans descendisse conspicitur, Henricus videlicet senator Urbis, regis prefati germanus, qui a clarissimis proprii generis actibus declinans in devium assumpto senatorie Urbis officio prefatam ecclesiam et suos non ut tenetur extollit honoribus, sed potius gravaminibus afficit ac lacessere gravibus iniuriis non veretur; propter quod in die cene Domini proximo preterito?, quibusdam de suis excessibus in hac Viterbiensi ecclesia narratis in publico, qui honeste dissimulari vel equanimiter tolerari non poterant, tam ipsum et Guidonem de Montefiltro eius in Urbe vicarium quam ceteros officiales eorum et omnes, qui voluntarii Galvano Lancee ac aliis Conradini nuntiis ad Urbem accedentibus occurrerunta vel receperunt eosdem, excommunicationis etc. similibus verbis ut p. 701, lin. 18-34 usque: procedere curaremus. Ipse vero, contra dictam ecclesiam et propriam salutem vultum obfirmans et, quantum in eo est, in gloria sui generis ponere maculam non abhorrens, non solum quod non paruit monitis et preterita non correxit, sed de malo labens in peius deteriora commisit. Inter alia enim, sicut accepimus, diversos clericos cepit seu capi fecit et sub custodia detineri, ac non sine tam inclite Urbis iniuria pariter et infamia nonnulla deposita diversorum Christi fidelium de sacris edibus Urbis seu locis eis adiacentibus extraxit seu fecit extrahi?, licet ex lege divina et humana ubilibet tuta manere debeant sub securitatis privilegio singulari. Unde quia premissa redundant in divine maiestatis offensam et predicte sedis iniuriam ac enorme dispendium ecclesiastice libertatis, eundem senatorem, presente hac fidelium multitudine, monemus sibique precipimus, ut infra festum apostolorum Petri et Pauli proximo futurum! tam de commissis circa clericos et deposita predicta quam de prefatis domibus nostris ac offensis et dampnis illatis cardinalibus et capellano predictis et ceteris, de quibus alium terminum sibi prefiximus, sicut superius est expressum, plenam satisfactionem impendat et a qualibet offensa predictorum cardinalium et capellani, ecclesiarum etiam et cleri Urbis prorsus abstineat. Alioquin exnunc in eum excommunicationis sententiam promulgamus, quam extunc eo ipso incurrat, si premissa neglexerit vel contempserit adimplere aut similia duxerit perpetranda. regesto_sintetico: Translation in English: It has come to our knowledge and will be remembered for the future that the illustrious family of the son of our beloved son in Christ, king of Castile and León, has always shown an exemplary devotion to the Roman pontiffs and the apostolic see, and has always been devoted to defend the honour and privilege of ecclesiastical liberty. We are therefore upset and not a little saddened that from such a noble and excellent lineage, Henry, the senator of the city of Rome, son of the aforementioned king, has come to be known to have been exasperated and to have taken a different path, by not working with the devotion and constant effort of his ancestors. He has not lifted up the honour of the church and his relatives as he should, but rather has burdened the church with evils and has not hesitated to attack it with serious injuries. For this reason, on the day before the last Easter, when some of his excesses in the church of Viterbo were narrated in public, which could not be tolerated with honesty or equanimity, he and Guido de Montefiltro, his vicar in Rome, and all the officials of his who met and received the aforementioned Galvano Lancese and other Conradini nuncios, who came to Rome, were excommunicated with the same words as above. He, however, strengthened his face against the church and his own salvation, and, as much as he could, wanted to stain his own glory with a stain, and, not only did he not obey the warnings and did not correct his past, but he also committed worse evils. Among other things, as we have learned, he has taken or had taken and detained in custody various clerks, and he has not only not refrained from taking away some of the faithful from the sacred buildings of Rome or from places adjacent to them, but he has also taken away some of them, in such a way that they have not been able to remain in any place under the protection of the law. Wherefore, since these things give rise to an offense to the divine majesty and to the injury of the apostolic see and to the great damage of ecclesiastical liberty, we exhort and command him, in the presence of a multitude of faithful, to make satisfaction for the offenses he has committed towards the clerks and for the goods he has taken away, and for the damage and the harm he has caused to the cardinal, the chaplain, the churches and the clergy of Rome, as we have previously indicated, and to refrain from any offense towards the aforementioned cardinals and chaplain and the churches and clergy of Rome. Otherwise, we excommunicate him, and he will incur the same excommunication from the present moment on if he does not comply with our warnings or contemptuously refuses to do so or attempts to do something similar. And, in order that this process of ours may be published, as in the previous case, so that the aforesaid Henry and his officials and all those who are involved in the process may know it, we command that it be published in the same way as above. REGESTO: Gregorius IX (ad Henricum senatorum Romanorum) 17 Maii 1228 (Viterbo). Ulloque super excommunicatione Henrici senatoris Romanorum, qui clericos captos detinebat, et de aliiis in ecclesiam Romanam commissis. Injungit, ut satisfactionem eorumdem clericorum pro captivitate et de bonis extortis ecclesiae Romanorum faciat. Dat. Viterbi, 17 Maii 1228 (Gregorius IX, Regestum epistolarum, nr. 6709).

The aforesaid excommunication sentences etc. as is written above, chapter XIoa, up to: will be published, so that the city and others, whom the process will reach, will be subject to the above-mentioned penalties. regesto_sintetico: Translation: To the king of Jerusalem. The most great Lord and greatly praiseworthy etc. — In the year of the lord 1216, on the 22nd of July, at the 11th pontificate of our predecessor Innocent VII, the lord was called to the region of the holy spirits, and on the following day the funeral rites were celebrated with the due honors, and his body was placed in the sepulcher. Then we, together with our brothers, convened to elect a successor, and on the third day, invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit, we deliberated on this matter and after a long discussion it pleased us to burden the shoulders of all brothers with this task, although insufficient. Although we were at first opposed to it, lest we seem to resist the divine call, we submit our shoulders to bear the burden, hoping that he who anticipates the aspirations of the brothers by prevenient grace will also follow them with assistance. For we have such a confidence in Christ through God, not that we are sufficient in ourselves, as if we were able to do something from ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God, who called us to his ministry. Therefore, it should not be considered that your heart is hindered or feared, as if the succor of the Holy Land would be hindered because of the death of our predecessor, since, although our ability may seem inferior, we aspire to its liberation with vows no less, and God, who never leaves those who trust in him, grants us the effect and the accomplishment of what our ability does not obtain, and bestows on us his grace. We therefore implore and exhort the royal serenity to be secure in God's favor, and to be strengthened in him and in his power, and to intend the conservation of the land valiantly and wisely, and to fight battles for the Lord when the time is opportune, and to receive from him the grace in the present and the glory in the future. The time of salvation is at hand and the day of salvation has arrived, when those who have sold themselves to the devil will be able to recover the freedom they have lost and redeem their souls, captured by diabolical fraud, with the price of the new redemption. Therefore, arise now, sleeper, and be awakened from the works of the dead, so that Christ may enlighten you and you may run in the splendor of the Lord's armor, girded for the battle to be fought against Him who promises the crown to those who contend lawfully. And since it is not for man to repay the Lord, who has given us the form of a servant, who delivered himself up to death for us, at least to drink the cup of passion in proportion to the retribution due to us, it is a shame for the Christian people that the king, who created all and created all that lies within the heavens, was expelled from his own throne for our favors and lost the land, which is the heritage of his, which he obtained not by corruptible gold and silver, but by his precious blood. It is also a shame for all who boast of being under the prince Christ that our prince has lost the glory of his kingdom and the land of his birth, in which he appeared corporally among men, and the land of the slave, which is not a free heir with the son. But where is the indignation of Moses, when he said: Who is the Lord that he may go with me, and that I may put every one that is of the holy ones to sword? (Exod. 32, 27) Where is the zeal of Phinees, who with his sword pierced the Israelite and the Midianite who were together? (Num. 25, 7) Where is the magnanimity of Mathathias, who, seeing the holy people profaned, rose up to defend the law and the paternal observances? (1 Macc. 2, 24-26) Let the faithful be girded, therefore, and be sons of the powerful. It is time, in fact, for them to do vengeance on the nations, that is, on those who hold and profane the land of the Lord and mock the glory of the cross of Christ and the shame of the Lord's passion. Therefore, arise now, and let every one hasten to the brim of this felicity, and let the faithful man take up his cross and follow the banner of the glory of the supreme King, and let no one excuse himself from the service of Jesus Christ, who wishes to reign with Him, except that he rather abandons himself and goes out from the land and from his kin, handing over to Him everything that He has given to all. We, however, according to the statute of the general council, receive under the special protection of the apostolic see the persons and goods of those who are marked with the sign of the cross, and we grant them full remission of their sins, on which they have been truly contrite in heart and confessed with the mouth, and we promise them an increase of eternal salvation. apparato: Hon. III Reg. Vol. I, 106, 107; Lib. I, 436. Potthast, Reg. 5503.
testo_esteso: Nobili viro comiti de Los crucesignato. Sacrosancta Romana ecclesia etc. usque: inclinati, ad exemplar felicis recordationis Innocentii pape predecessoris nostri compositionem inter te ac nobilem virum Willielmum de Hollandia Traiectensis diocesis super raptu nobilis mulieris A. uxoris tue necnon Hollandia et aliis terris, ad te ratione uxoris eiusdem spectantibus, mediante quondam Philippo marchione Namucensi tune balivo comitatus Flandrensis, amicabiliter initam et iuramentis prestitis hinc inde firmatam, sicut sine pravitate provide facta esta et ab utraque parte sponte recepta, et in scriptis autenticis inde confectis plenius continetur, auctoritate apostolica precipimus observari. Ut autem eadem compositio firmius observetur, tenorem ipsius presentibus iussimus annotari, qui talis est. Hec est forma compositionis et pacis perpetue inter Lodewicum comitem de Los et de Hollandia et dominum Willielmum, Florentii comitis Hollandie quondam filium, arbitrio domini Philippi marchionis Namucensis baiuli Flandrie et nobilium Flandrie virorum consensu et consilio firmate, et spontanea predictorum, comitis scilicet Lodewici et domini Willielmi, voluntate plenius approbate. Post longas siquidem controversias inter eos versatas tandem in bonum pacis consentientes L. comes de Los et de Ollandia et dominus W. predictus dicto et arbitrio domini Philippi marchionis Namucensis super universa terra, que fuit Theodorici comitis Hollandiensis, se commiserunt. Dominus igitur Philippus marchio Namucensis dicto et arbitrio suo assignavit comiti de Los comitatum Hollandie, excepto dotalitio matris domini Willielmi supradicti, post cuius domino decessum dotalitium illud ad dominum Willielmum in proprietatem deveniet. Assignavit etiam dominus Ph. marchio Namucensis comiti de Los Scarpenesse, Duvelant, Stavenesse et Drieskere et dominium domini Hugonis de Ostenvorne et de Westenvorne et de appenditiis. Tota vero alia terra ex hac parte Mose deversus Flandriam per dictum et arbitrium domini marchionis Namucensis remanet in parte domini Willielmi. Quicquid dominus Hugo” predictus tenet apud Apenbruch, et castellariam de Sellandia, et omne quod tenet infra insulas que assignate sunt domino W., tenebit ipse Hugo a domino W.; et inde excipiuntur quatuor insule predicte comiti de Los assignate. In winagio ! apud Gerulith habebit dominus W. omni anno quadringentas libras denariorum, et habebit illic nuntium suum ad denarios colligendos, quousque quadringentas libras receperit. Omne quod illis quadringentis libris supercreverit, comitis de Los et Ollandia erit; si quid autem ad illas quadringentas libras perficiendas defuerit, comes de Los et de Hollant infra annum perficiet. Cum nuntio domini W. comes de Los ministrum suum habebit ad computandum et sciendum denariorum receptionem in predicto winagio. Illas quadringentas libras guinagii dominus W. tenebit ab imperatore seu rege Romanorum, sicut comes de Los tenet ab codem rege residuum. Ad vinagium de Gherulieth homines domini V. nichil aliud solvent, quam solebant solvere tempore Florentii comitis Hollandie. Ad dictum et arbitrium domini Philippi debet dominus W. benefacte adheredare comitem de Los de omnibus supradictis, et comes de Los dominum W. bene etiam adheredare. Unde sciendum est, quod dominus W. ad dictum et arbitrium domini Philippi et consilii sui dedit ei obsides pro dicto et arbitrio suo tenendo sororem suam et filiam suam propriam et decem homines de Scondes. Homines de Hollandia, qui ipsa die Burgis erant, fecit dominus W. facere hominium comiti de Los et de Hollandia, et per castellanum de Leda, qui presens erat, debet comiti de Los facere haberi libere castellum de Leda, vel per nuntios suos. Debet quoque mandare et precipere omnibus hominibus Hollandie et totius terre comiti de Los assignate per litteras suas patentes et per nuntios suos, ut comiti de Los hominium faciant et fidelitatem sine aliquo malo ingenio; et in mandato illo et precepto debet hominibus illis intimare, quod si hominium illud et fidelitatem facere recusaverint, contra omnes qui rebelles erunt, erit comitis de Los in omni posse suo in auxilium, quousque hec consumata erunt comiti de Los et perfecta. Deinde debet dominus W. ire in curia domini episcopi Traiectensis et illic reddere feodum suum et guerpire ! ad opus domini comitis de Los, ad eum bona fide adheredandum sine suo dandos, et simili modo faciet dominus W. in curia domini ducis Lovaniensis. Illinc debet dominus W. ire apud Dordrech et ad Flardinghem et ad Ledam et ad Harlem, et ad quamque illarum villarum debet mandare et summonereb homines omnes vicinos et adiacentes illi ville et precipere eis, ut comiti de Los hominium faciant et fidelitatem, et dominus W. omnes homines illos a fidelitate, quam ei fecerant, et hominio liberos et absolutos clamabit et dimittet. Et si qui rebelles fuerint, dominus W. ad summonitioneme comitis de Los debet eum iuvare semel ad illos destruendos et fugandos, nec eos post dominus W. retinere vel iuvare, quousque ad fidelitatem et hominium comitis de Los et de Hollandia venerint; et hoc pepigit dominus W. comiti de Los bona fide. Dominus marchio Namucensis debet mittere nuntios suos cum domino W. et cum comite de Los ad curiam domini episcopi Traiectensis et ad curiam ducis Lovaniensis et in Hollandiam, ut eorum testimonio hec perficiantur, et corum testimonio quisque debet, tam comes de Los quam dominus W., hec, quantotius potuerit, adimplere. Precepit quoque dominus marchio Namucensis ipsis nuntiis in fidelitate et iuramento quod ei fecerant, quod hec bona fide perficere studeant. In omnibus viis iamdictis ad perficienda que dicta sunt, ibit comes de Los sub conductu domini W. et dominus W. sub conductu comitis de Los. Hiis quoque peractis secundum relationem et recordationem nuntiorum iamdictorum dominus W. obsides positos rehabebit liberos. Hec omnia comes de Los et dominus W. bona fide et sine malo inienio debent complere. Dominus W. debet mittere in Angliam nuntios suos ad rehabendam neptem suam et eam reddendam comiti de Los, et si per nuntios suos eam rehabere non potuerit, nuntii illi debent ei acquirere conductum, ut ipse illuc ire possit. Quod si non potuerint, dominus Philippus marchio Namucensis debet ei conductum illum acquirere d, et ipse dominus W. in propria persona debet illuc ire et bona fide laborare ad hoc, ut eam rehabeat sine suo dampno; et si in propria persona cam non rehabuerit, et dominus marchio Namucensis vel per litteras regis Anglie seu per credibiles nuntios scire potuerit, quod dominus W. posse suum inde non fecerit, et quod potuisset illam rehabuisse, si voluisset, iterum debet dominus W. illuc ire; et dominus marchio Namucensis debet cum eo mittere duos probos viros per iuramenta et unum abbatem in obedientia monitum, ut videant et inquirant, si dominus W. de illa rehabenda fecerit posse suum. Si nuntii illi testificati fuerint, quod dominus W. posse suum inde non fecerit, dominus marchio Namucensis debet eum cogere et ostagiis ! positis et omnibus modis, ut eam reddat. Si autem testificati fuerint, quod inde dominus W. posse suum fecerit, liber inde et quietus debet remanere. Dominus W. homines suos de Sellandia et de Schoudis debet dare obsides et facere iurare, quod si in supradictis compositionibus et conventionibus deficeret, homines illi essent ei in nocumentum et domino marchioni Namucensi in auxilium, quousque emendatum esset consilio curie Flandrensis. Resignato" quippe feodo a comite de Los in manum domini Philippi marchionis Namucensis baiuli Flandrie, quod Theodoricus comes Hollandie ultimis diebus vite sue tenuit a domino comite Flandrie, et inde adhereditato domino W., testimonio hominum Flandrie et Hainoie comitis et heredum suorum, ipse W. feodum suum assignavit comiti Namucensi ac marchioni baiulo Flandrie super predicta pace et conventione tenenda in ostagiariam. Lodewicus comes de Los et de Hollandia concessit et pepigit domino Ph. marchioni Namucensi ad eius dictum et arbitrium et consilii sui de conventione inter ipsum et dominum W. tenenda et pace et omni compositione dare ostagiariam et securitatem: videlicet quod coram episcopo Traiectensi ponet terram Hollandie in hostagiariam, quod si predictis compositionibus et conventionibus deficeret, terra illa remaneret in manu ipsius episcopi, ita quod comes de Los nichil interim acciperet in terra illa, quousque emendatum esset consilio curie Flandrensis; et litteras patentes ipsius episcopi debet comes de Los exinde facere haberi Philippo marchioni Namucensi. Quatuorque insulas supranominatas Scarponisse. Duvelant, Stavenisse et Driskire, et castellum de Leda cum villa et cum toto allodio, quod est in castellaria illa, que omnia ad dominium et feodum Flandrie dedit idem comes de Los et de Hollandia, posuit etiam in ostagiariam, quod si deficeret in predictis compositionibus et conventionibus, dominus marchio Namucensis manum mitteret ad feudum, quousque emendatum esset consilio curie Flandrensis. Homines quoque Hollandie et insularum predictarum ponet obsides comes de Los, ita quod faciet eos iurare, quod si deficeret in predictis, ipsi homines essent comiti de Los in nocumentum et domino Namucensi in auxilium, quousque emendatum esset consilio curie Flandrensis. Ponet quoque comes de Los dominum episcopum Leodiensem ostagium, quod si conventionibus prodictis deficerct, ipse episcopus manum mitteret ad feodum suum, et interim comes de Los nichil acciperet in feodo illo quod tenet ab episcopo, quousque emendatum esset consilio curie Flandrensis; et inde litteras ipsius episcopi patentes acquiret comes de Los domino Namucensi baiulo Flandrensi. Pro posse etiam suo sine suo dampno ponet comes de Los hostagium ducem Lovaniensem, quod si in conventionibus satisdictis deficeret, dux ad feodum suum manum mitteret, quousque emendatum essetb curie Flandrensi; et inde litteras ipsius ducis patentes faciet haberi domino Namucensi. De propria comitis de Los hereditate, quam posuit in ostagiariam, est in veritate? domini marchionis Namucensis, quod si comes de Los uxorem suam rehabuerit, et domino Namucensi visum fuerit, quod bene possit comes de Los per uxorem suam adheredare dominum W. de terra, que ei est assignata, et ipse comes de Los inde deficeret, tunc feodum domini Leodiensis et domini Lovaniensis essent in predicta ostagiaria. Hec omnia plenius tenenda et firmius observanda Lodewicus comes de Los et de Hollandia et dominus Willielmus tactis sacrosanctis iuraverunt. Dominus quoque marchio Namucensis baiulus Flandrie super hiis omnibus inviolabiliter observandis ad petitionem comitis de Los et domini W. obsidem se constituit, sigilloque suo cum sigillo comitis de Los et de Hollandia et cum sigillo domini W. sepedicti presens scriptum confirmari decrevit. Indeed, if he says that he fears to go to Padua, alleging that our friends can procure for him, we promise on oath, by the reverence of the apostolic see, that he will be free from fear, going to Padua and returning from there. regesto_sintetico: English translation: To the archbishop of Sens and his suffragans, as well as to all the faithful of Christ, both cross-bearers and others residing in their dioceses. The Christian army that has taken up the fight in the regions beyond the sea, where it either wins a full victory or is in manifest despair of being victorious, is besieging the city of Damietta, a very rich and great city. If the Lord our God were to deliver it into their hands, there would be no small obstacle in all Egypt for them to overcome, and rather the infidels who hold the holy city of Jerusalem would flee from it and leave it to the faithful without fighting. If, however, they are unable to take the aforementioned city, the army is in the utmost danger, since the champions of Christ have placed themselves in that place, so that if they do not gain victory, they must either conquer or perish; and if this were to happen due to our sins and the people of Christ, the hearts and hands of the cross-bearers and of all who aspire to their help would be shaken, and the great effort undertaken for the recovery of the Holy Land, which has shaken the whole Christian world, would be rendered useless, to the memory of which God avert. But we trust in the divine counsel, since the Lord does signs for us, making us hope for good. For He has removed the most impious sultan of the Sephadians, the scourge of the Holy Land, who had been the most bitter thorn to the Christians, and has brought discord among the infidels, so that the old sultan of Damascus, son of Saladin, who is at war with his brother and his son, the sultans, and is thus troubling the land of the infidels, has turned his hands against himself, so that it is hoped that God will divide their kingdom among themselves and will leave it desolate. He has also, seeing the devotion of his soldiers, given them a tower, which was a place of great strength, situated in the middle of a river and defended by iron chains, which denied access to the said city, and which was considered impenetrable, since three hundred armed men could fit in it. He has given it to the hands of the faithful and has also inspired such terror in his enemies that the mountain of Thabor, which the Christians had fortified at great expense, and other fortified places, which they had dug under the walls, have been abandoned by them, because they fear that the Christian army will conquer the city. Having considered these things, our venerable brother, the patriarch of Jerusalem, and our beloved sons, Stephen, the familiaris of the apostolic see, and Henry, brothers of the houses of the Hospital and the Temple, have supplicated us by letters and prayers, which have been able to melt even the hardest hearts into tears, to grant that, since the expenses which have been made and are being made for the machines and galleys, and other war expenses, which have been collected and will be collected, have been very great, and the army is daily dwindling, since the men of war, who are returning from the lack of resources, cannot provide for the soldiers, we hasten to send to them aid from the Christians on the other side, since they place all their hope in them. We therefore warn and exhort all of you to put before your eyes the joy and the exultation which will be for the just in the Lord, if the business which has been undertaken has a happy outcome, and the opposite, if the opposite happens, will bring shame and confusion to the whole Christian people. We therefore order that you hasten to succor the army, providing that you summon by a solemn exhortation the sons of the cross, the archbishops and the bishops, each one summoning the signatories of his diocese, so that they may go to the army. The vicesima and other money, which has been collected and will be collected for the subsidy of the Holy Land, shall be assigned to the present bearers, who have been appointed for this purpose, and who have been sent to you by us. To them we have given five thousand marches, which we will give more, if we can subtract them from the expenses of our family and of others which we have to make. We order that you attend to the expenses which have already been collected and which will be collected, and which have been sent, and which the present bearers will receive. We have not omitted to mention that the patriarch, the legate, the duke and the prince, and other prelates and magnates of the army have written to us that the detractors of God, who have tried to defame our beloved son John, king of Jerusalem, and the beloved sons of the Temple and the Hospital, have been found to be empty of truth, and that they have been found to be very faithful and virtuous, so that we have found it necessary to order that they be honored, loved and supported as true champions of Christ and defenders of the faith. In order that the dignity of the imperial court may not lack the company of the king, we warn and beseech you in the Lord, and we command under pain of excommunication, that you, children of the cross, prepare yourselves in such a way that, without excuse or delay, you reach the nearest feast of St. John the Baptist with the king, to take part in the journey to succor the aforementioned army, which is in great danger for the common cause of the entire Christian people. The usual letters of your highness having been received, our soul rejoices in the Lord, since you have shown to be the son of the father, in that you not only acknowledge the received benefits but also do not deny to be a debtor of the retribution. You can well notice how and of what kind has been the desire of the father, which has been expected and desired by us, that is, that you have removed with the excuse of reasonable reasons some things that appeared to be noticed by some and which were a subject of conjection for others, by presenting the contrary in the open and authentic letters to the knowledge of many. Although our love is brought forward by your kindness and your heart is instilled with prompt zeal for our cause, it is useful that not only we but also others know and understand by your acts that you are mindful of the riches which the pious mother church has poured on you and that you are mindful of the right hand with which the Roman pontiff, as a father, has extended to your promotion. However, there is something that appears exposed by the detractors of many and that it is not applied to excuses by some, namely that you do not provide a prompter and greater aid for the subsidy of the Holy Land. Behold, dear son, what two terms have been assigned to you, which have elapsed and have brought a profit? Which ships, which galleys have been prepared to cross the sea by your efforts? Which vessels useful for the crossing have been received or known by the sea or the shore? Be, dear son, that you have been delayed by some obstacles until now; the great affect of the great efforts should have made clear that the work, as much as it has been extended by the possibility of the effect, has been effective in the promptness of the will. And I would wish to be you rather the precursor than the sequac, and not only to insist on the repetition of the delay, but to strongly oppose to those who ask. Therefore may the Lord do this and add this, so that what He has inspired for this purpose, He may also bring about in a more wonderful way, so that devotion, begun in this way, may end in the same way, so that throughout your life you may be called the whole Church of God, the whole of Christ. O how much we desire you to be pleasing to God in His sight, o how much in the eyes of men, so that you may observe integrity of conscience before Him, and reputation for notable deeds in the eyes of men. But since he who loves much, fears much, it is not surprising that we fear, both for you, lest, because of repeated postponements, you incur the offense of a great king, and for us, lest we seem to have neglected the counsel of the highest pontiff, who offered himself to God the Father as a sacrifice on the cross for the salvation of the people. But you still urge us to grant a fourth postponement, and you do not take into account that, if, after three summons, you contemptuously refuse to appear in court, you can be charged with contempt. We know that you bring forward many excuses for your delay, and we also know that your enemies do not interpret them as your friends do. But we, lest we seem to expose the reputation of a dear son to contempt, until the next 1 May, we extend the term of your process, hoping that the royal dignity will thus effectively pursue the business of Jesus Christ, so that, since the postponement, which hitherto seemed to be open to calumny, will be attributed to prudence and will be assumed as a precaution, you may consider that the cause being discussed is Christ’s, the procurator is God’s, and the procurator is the Christian’s. And consider, consider, to whom belongs the cause, which is being prosecuted, to whom belongs the benefit, which is being sought, to whom belongs the glory, which is being sought. And the Lord leads you to these things by benefits, provokes you to them by miracles, and informs you by examples: by benefits, because He has raised the humble from the dust; by miracles, because He has fulfilled the desire of the weak Christian army, which had already lost hope; by examples, because even the poor and the weak have taken up this salutary business. Therefore, let the royal dignity, so great and noble, so powerful and strong, be careful not to incur the blame of excuse, as it seems, for the more it is able. Therefore, let the noble prince arise, let the mighty man arise, because, as we hope, the Lord is prepared to offer a great triumph, who has already brought a great crown from the labour of few. Take up the sword on your thigh, most powerful princes of the earth, take up the sword in humility, the powerful in humility, the humble in power, so that, relying not on your arm, you may receive the glory of this business, which is expected, from the hand of the Most High. But although the term has been postponed, you should still pursue it prudently and openly, as much as you can, since not only the prosecution, but also the fame of prosecution will lead many to the path, and will precede many to the help of the Holy Land, from which God will restore the strength of the army and will shake the parts of the enemies. regesto_sintetico: English translation: To the illustrious Emperor, always August and King of Sicily. You have taken joy in the promotion of the Emperor, as a father does in the growth of a son, and we have expected with great enthusiasm and joy that you would reach the height of the empire, as is known to him who knows everything and is aware of all secrets. We have been delighted with your promotion, as a father is delighted with the growth of his son, and we have believed that you would take care of us, our things and the Roman Church with great dedication, as a son is led by his father with dedication to perfection. Therefore, we write to you as a father to his son, without hiding anything, and we tell you that it is necessary for you to be very careful not to do anything against the Roman Church, especially in our times, so that you do not incur the fault of ingratitude. Do you not consider that you are bound by various and diverse oaths to cross over to the aid of the Holy Land, and that you have been absolved from the excommunication that you had incurred by your promise to obey our mandates, when you came to your coronation? You have certainly deceived the Christian army with your promises, and it is now in great danger today. And what we have heard and are hearing is that you are extending your hands to the elections of bishops, especially to the election of the bishopric of Aversa in the province of Salerno, which is vacant. Do you perhaps sigh for the abuse of your ancestors, which the Lord, who is zealous for justice, has opposed to them in such a way that, apart from you, hardly anyone remains from their descendants? But you also recall that you have renounced this abuse and that you have confirmed this renunciation by a privilege and oath, and that you have sworn not to do this again. But you do not respect the privileges and promises that you have made, and you do not respect the oath that you have sworn. You are even thinking of using the sword against us and the Roman Church, as if we were not aware of your thoughts, which are evil and full of malice. We do not say that we want to appoint bishops in your kingdom without your consent; rather, we propose that if we are attacked by you, we will be ready to provide for your kingdom's tranquility. We believe that these things are not done by you, but by the malice of others, who, as the proverb says, want to fish in troubled waters, and who want to create trouble between you and the Church, in order to gain something for themselves. You should not listen to such people, lest you fall into the hands of the living God. We tell you that you should not put on your glory a stain, nor should you dismiss your promises and privileges, nor should you act against the divine, canonical and human laws. We also warn you that, if you do not stop doing these things, we will bring your difficulties to the knowledge of the whole world, invoking the testimony of heaven and earth, and we will be very sorry and unwilling to do so. We write this to you, who have been treated by us as a true father, and we ask you to take it into consideration, and we remind you that your son has obtained peace in the land of Thuringia, and that we also know that you can obtain something that you want in Thuringia and other parts of the empire, as well as in the kingdom of Sicily. We also remind you that we have always shown you paternal affection, and we ask you to be careful not to create scandal between you and the Church, because if you do, we will be very sorry and we will be forced to bring our interior pain to the knowledge of the world. We send you our beloved son, prior of the new monastery of St. Mary, with our letters and a transcript of your privilege, and we ask you to correct the things that have been done wrongly, and to allow the elections to be held freely and without any defect. Otherwise, we will not be able to bear the harm that you will do to our souls, especially since people are always crying out against us that we have betrayed you to God, but we will bring your difficulties to the knowledge of the whole world, invoking the testimony of heaven and earth. Ne terra vaste solitudinis, quam in partibus Livonie Dominus per ministerium predicatorum suorum reducens ad cultum nominis Christiani facit de semine verbi sui nova fidelium segete pululare, quod absit, in salsuginem redigatur, set potius crescens in messem in fructum exhuberet oportunum, expedit, ut a paganis, qui adhuc gentilis erroris orrore sunt ispidi tanquam spine, nullatenus opprimi permittantur, set potenter defendantur ab eis, alias congruis auxiliis favorabiliter confovendi, quatinus ipsi non solum fortius radicentur in fide, verum etiam conversionem aliïs valeant efficacius suadere. Quantus enim dolor, quantusve pudor esset populo Christiano, et maxime circumposite regioni, si terra Domino acquisita nunc per desidiam fidelium taliter perderetur, qui ad acquirendam aliam totis deberent desideriis aspirare. Ut igitur Christi fideles quasi certo illecti stipendio ad succurrendum eis fortius animentur, nos omnibus de Saxonia, exceptis hiis qui vel voverunt vel proposuerunt ire in subsidium Terre Sancte, proficiscentibus et morantibus per triennium in subsidium noviter in Livonia conversorum, eam peccatorum suorum veniam indulgemus, que in Terre Sancte subsidium proficiscentibus est indulta, ipsis nichilominus cum familiis et omnibus bonis suis sub apostolice sedis et nostra protectione susceptis. regesto_sintetico: English translation: To all the faithful of Christ in Saxony. We wish that the land of a wide desert, which the Lord, through the ministry of his preachers, is making fruitful again through the cult of the name of Christ in the lands of Livonia, not be turned into a morass, but rather, growing, may bring a good harvest. It is necessary that the pagans, who are still wrapped in the thorns of heathen error, are not permitted to oppress them, but rather to be defended from them, so that they may be able to be helped with suitable help, so that they not only may be rooted more deeply in faith, but also may be able to persuade others to conversion more effectively. How great would be the pain and shame for the Christian people, and especially for the adjacent region, if the land acquired by the Lord were lost through the idleness of the faithful, who should strive with all their desires to acquire another one. So that Christ's faithful, like those who are certainly drawn by the certain reward, may be more encouraged to help them, we grant to all the Saxons, except those who have vowed or promised to go to the aid of the Holy Land, who are going or living in Livonia to help the converts, for three years, the pardon of their sins, which is granted to those who are going to the Holy Land, to them and their families and all their goods, under the protection of the apostolic see and ours. Therefore we admonish and exhort you in all urgency, commanding it to you by apostolic letters, that you provide and attend carefully, how salutary it is for a man to put his soul for that which he guards and keeps for himself, and that you serve willingly him who served us for his stipend on the cross, helping the said converts, so that in those parts the Christian people may be increased in number and in merit, and for you a greater reward may be paid by God, who repays more than is hoped those who are obedient to him faithfully. Given in the Lateran, 15th January, in the sixth year. REGESTO: Papa Honorius III a Saxonibus, qui proficiscentes et morantes in Livonia pro conversis, eis proficiscentibus et morantibus pro triennium peccatorum suorum veniam indult. Dat. 1232, I Feb.

We received letters of the abbot and the convent of Mulembrunnena, in which they inform us that Albert of Lechimchan, a knight, who died because of a fire and a homicide, was detained by the bond of excommunication. After being seized by a serious illness, he confessed his sins to his priest with a true heart and swore an oath that he would come to the apostolic see, accepting the will of the same. Absolved by the aforementioned priest, he partook of the body and blood of the Lord and fulfilled the debt of nature. Therefore, the aforementioned abbot and convent humbly asked that we order the handing over of his body to ecclesiastical burial, which he had not yet received. We, trusting in your full brotherhood in the Lord, order you, by apostolic letter, to satisfy with the authority of the Church the heritors of the deceased for the homicide and the fire, and to order, as is necessary, that they be buried in a way pleasing to God and without scandal. Given on the 16th day before the calends of January, in the seventh year. REGESTO: Gregorius IX Gregorio, Spirensi episcopo, auctoritatem. mandat, ut Albertum de Lechimchan, defunctum, ecclesiastice sepulture tradendam prebet, prout et excommunicati debent sepeliri, satisfactis heredibus defuncti super homicidio et incendio. 1223, Iul. 18. Lugduni.

Et quidem multum gavisi sumus in Domino super devotione, quam habes ad nos et ad Romanam ecclesiam matrem Christianorum omnium et magistram, et super pio desiderio, quod habes de deliberatione Terre Sancte, in qua dominus Iesus Christus dignatus est humani generis operari salutem, tradens morti crucis ineffabili pietate se ipsum, ut genus humanum a morte perpetua liberaret. Super morte autem clare memorie.. fratris tui, regis Georianorum, tibi paterno compassi sumus affectu, ac in eo subsequenter gavisi, quod pacifice obtines regnum eius, sicut nobis per ipsas litteras intimasti, optantes ut Deus, in cuius manu sunt iura regnorum et regna, te ac tuum regnum in sua fide ac devotione atque in bonis omnibus amplificet et conservet. Etsi enim absentes simus corpore, presentes tamen spiritu, te ac alios Christianos regni tui cordis oculis intuemur, et delectamur in fide, quam habetis in domino Iesu Christo, cui eo ipso est acceptior fides vestra, quod eam servatis in medio infidelium nationum, inter quas lucetis quasi lucerne in tenebris, et redoletis quasi lilia inter spinas, reportaturi fidei vestre desiderabilem finem, salutem vestrarum videlicet animarum. Propter quod tuam Matth. 102z exhortamur in Domino celsitudinem, ut certa de promissione Christi dicentis: Qui confitebitur me coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram patre meo, qui est in celis; in confessione ac laude sancti nominis eius firmusa stabilisque persistas et ad persistendum in ea subditos tuos exemplo sancte conversationis inducas, ut post huius transitorie vite inevitabilem exitum una cum ipsis regnum merearis consequi sempiternum. Sane super eo quod de passagio carissimi in Christo filii nostri Friderici, illustris Romanorum imperatoris semper augusti et regis Sicilie, certificari desideras, te ac exfortium tuum ad ipsius Terre Sancte succursum magnifice offerendo, fidei tue zelum in Domino commendantes tibi auctoritate presentium declaramus, quod idem imperator ad ipsius terre liberationem magnanimiter ac magnifice se accingit, a festo sancti Iohannis baptiste proximo ad annum unum pro liberanda de manibus infidelium terra ipsa cum innumera fidelium multitudine et alio apparatu imperiali magnificentia digno Christo ductore feliciter transiturus. Monemus igitur serenitatem tuam et hortamur in Domino, quatinus iuxta laudabilem promissionem tuam tuum studeas exfortium taliter preparare, quod tunc possis domino lesu Christo dignum magnitudine tua servitium exhibere. Ut autem tu et subditi tui ad tam sanctum opus vos tanto libentius et devotius preparetis, quanto ex hoc maiora vobis apud Deum premia comparatis, notificamus devotioni tue, quod omnes, qui laborem istum in propriis personis subierint et expensis, et illi etiam, qui non in personis propriis illuc accesserint sed in suis expensis iuxta facultates suas viros idoneos destinaverint, et illi similiter, qui licet in alienis expensis in propriis tamen personis accesserint, plenam peccatorum suorum, de quibus vere contriti fuerint et confessi, veniam dono apostolice indulgentie consequuntur. Huius quoque remissionis sunt illi participes iuxta quantitatem subsidii et devotionis affectum, qui ad subventionem ipsius Terre Sancte de bonis suis congrue ministrabunt aut circa predicta impendent consilium et auxilium oportunum. Hanc tam grandem indulgentiam, in sancta et universali synodo factam omnibus Christianis, presentium auctoritate concedimus specialiter tibi et Christianis omnibus tuo regimini et dicioni subiectis. Tu ergo presentes litteras facias tuis subditis Christi fidelibus recitari, quibus iuxta 25 postulationem tuam benedictionem apostolicam elargimur, promittentes tibi et eis, in quibuscunque oportuerit et decuerit, apostolice sedis gratiam et favorem. regesto_sintetico: Translation in English: To the illustrious queen of the Georgians. We have received your letters, full of the odor of devotion, and have understood their contents carefully. We were very pleased in the Lord for the devotion you have towards us and the Roman Church, mother of all Christians and mistress, and for the pious desire you have for the liberation of the Holy Land, in which the Lord Jesus Christ deigned to work the salvation of the human race, giving himself to death on the cross in ineffable piety, so that the human race may be freed from eternal death. We have been pained with paternal compassion for the death of your brother, the king of the Georgians, and we were pleased for his peaceful succession, as you have informed us by the same letters, desiring that God, whose are the laws of kingdoms and the kingdoms, may amplify and preserve you and your kingdom in his faith and devotion and in all good things. Although we are absent in body, we are present in spirit, and we see you and other Christians of your kingdom with the eyes of the heart, and we are delighted in the faith you have in the Lord Jesus Christ, whose faith is more acceptable to you because you serve it in the midst of infidel nations, among which you shine like a lamp in darkness and smell like lilies among thorns, and you bring the desired end of your faith, which is the salvation of your souls. We exhort you, therefore, with the motherly exhortation, that you may be certain of the promise of Christ, who says: "He who confesses me before men, I will confess him before my Father who is in heaven", to persist firmly and stably in the confession and praise of his holy name, and to lead your subjects to persist in the same example of holy life, so that after the inevitable end of this transitory life you may merit to obtain the eternal kingdom with them. Since you ask us to be informed about the passage of our beloved son in Christ, Frederick, illustrious king of the Romans and king of Sicily, we commend to you with paternal love the zeal of your faith in the Lord, and we declare with the authority of the present letter that the aforesaid king is preparing himself to go to the aid of the Holy Land with great magnanimity and magnificence, and that he will go there with a great multitude of faithful and other imperial apparatus worthy of Christ the leader, so that he may liberate the aforesaid land from the hands of the infidels. We therefore exhort and admonish your serenity to prepare your exhorter and subjects to go there with such devotion, that you may be able to offer to the Lord Jesus Christ a worthy service in proportion to your grandeur. In order that you and your subjects may be prepared to undertake this work with greater joy and devotion, as much as you will have greater rewards from God, we inform you of the devotion of your exhorter, that all those who will take up this labor in their own person and at their own expense, and those who will not go in person but will send suitable men at their own expense, and those who, although they will not go in person, will go at the expense of others, and those who will go at the expense of others in their own person, will receive the plenary remission of their sins, if they have been truly contrite and confessed. Also those who will participate in this remission will be those who, according to the amount of the subsidy and the devotion of their zeal, will contribute to the aid of the Holy Land from their goods or will give advice and help opportune. We grant this indulgence, made in a holy and universal synod to all Christians, to you and all your subjects, to your kingdom and jurisdiction, with the authority of the present letter. You should have the present letters read to your faithful Christians, by which we grant you and them, according to your petition, the favor and grace of the apostolic see. Augustensis episcopus, diocesanus vester, per litteras suas nobis nuper exposuit, quod quidam monachus vester a diabolo, cuius faciebat opera, instigatus, privilegia quedam a sede apostolica monasterio vestro concessa cuiusdam militis instinctu subripuit et in ipsius tradidit potestatem; cuius castro non post multos dies capto ab inimicis ipsius et universis bonis exinde asportatis, predicta privilegia sine bulla fuerunt vobis ab hiis, ad quorum manus devenerant, restituta. De quo cum ingentem tristitiam conceperitis et merorem, dictus episcopus super tanto vobis compatiens detrimento, per predictas litteras nobis humiliter supplicavit, ut dignaremur eadem privilegia innovare. Tu quoque, fili abbas, ad presentiam nostram accedens, uno privilegiorum ipsorum, videlicet Calixti secundi, et rescripto alterius, secundi scilicet Innocentii, nobis exhibitis, cum multa precum instantia petivisti eidem monasterio super tanto discrimine similiter provideri. testo_esteso: Universis presentes litteras inspecturis. Summi providentia principis peculiarem populum, quem pretulerat aliis gratie privilegio specialis, fovebat manna misericordie ac rigoris virga regebat, beneficiis Osea n13. affluens, ultionibus non remissus. Amicus etiam Domini Moyses pro eodem populo vitulum obtulit labiorum et manuum sacrificium non omisit, post supplicationis hostiam holocausto satisfactionis oblato, causam populi coram Domino precibus et Dei causam in populo gladiis prosecutus. Sane in maligno positi mundi malitia, dum impunitis excessibus per campum licentie discurrit effrenis, claustra iuris infringit, aditum pandit iniuriis, legem damnat honesti, privilegium promittit errori, et dum spem impunitatis ad alios prorogat, ad culpam nonnullos invitat, sicque fit penalis impunitas, cum penis reservet maioribus puniendos et per impunite transgressionis exemplar blandiatur aliis ad offensam. Unde interdum utcunque tyrannice parcitur et misericorditer desevitur, cum publice utilitatis intersit, ut excessum vindicta coerceat et pena sit limes offense. Hinc est, quod propter presumptam in quosdam de fratribus nostris temeritatis audaciam nos, ne celestis regis contumeliam, qui honoratur et spernitur in ministris. dissimulationi relinquere ac Christiane religionis opprobrium, dum christi Domini. quos ad Christianorum omnium salubre servitium apostolica sedes assumit, crudeliter impetuntur, dare negligentie videamur, non tanquam iniuriarum ultores nostrarum, sed honoris sponse Christi et immunitatis domus Domini zelatores, de communi fratrum nostrorum consilio hac in perpetuum valitura constitutione sancimus, ut si quis in hoc sacrilegii genus irrepserit, quod sancte Romane ecclesie cardinalem fuerit hostiliter insecutus vel percusserit aut ceperit, vel socius fuerit facientis aut fieri mandaverit vel factum ratum habuerit aut consilium dederit vel favorem. aut postea receptaverit vel defensaverit scienter eundem, sicut reus lese criminis maiestatis perpetuo sit infamis, diffidatus nihilominus et banditus, sit intestabilis, ut nec testamenti liberam habeat factionem nec ad alicuius bona ex testamento vel ab intestato vocetur, quatinus ab omni successione repulsus, publicaque repulsa confusus, minus inveniat sue malitie successorem. Fiant habitationes eius deserte, et ut non sit, qui eas inhabitet, dentur cuncta ipsius edificia in ruinam, et ut perpetue notam infamie perpetua ruina testetur, nullo tempore reparentur. Nullus ei debita reddere, nullus respondere in iudicio teneatur. Quidquid etiam in bonis invenietur ipsius, fisci vel reipublice dominio applicetur, ut ex illis nil transmittat ad posteros, sed potius cum ipso quodammodo damnentur et sua. Si qua vero feuda, locationes, officium vel beneficium spirituale vel temporale ab aliquibus ecclesiis obtinet. sit eis ipso iure privatus; que sic libere ad ecclesias revertantur, quod ecclesiarum rectores de ipsis pro sua voluntate disponant. Quod si filium habet clericum, non prelatum, ecclesiasticum beneficium obtinentem, illo privetur, spe collationis alterius omnino sublata. Nulli preterea talium filiorum atque nepotum ex virili sexu descendentium ab eisdem alicuius aperiatur ianua dignitatis aut honoris ecclesiastici vel mundani. Ad alicuius loci regimen non accedat. Sit ei postulandi negata facultas, sit notarie, iudicatus et quodlibet aliud officium seu ministerium publicum interdictum. In iudiciis eius assertio contra quemque nihil fidei, nihil credulitatis inveniat, ut ad testimonium prorsus reddatur indignus. Sit ei ad ordines ascensus inhibitus, sit ad beneficium vel officium ecclesiasticum negatus accessus, et ut magis famosa sit eius infamia, ad actus legitimos nullus ei pateat aditus, nulla porta pandatur eidem, super aliquo premissorum omni spe dispensationis adempta. Presenti nihilominus adicimus sanctioni, ut ex insecutione predicta, sicut ex iniectione manuum violenta, ipso facto excommunicationis sententiam quis incurrat, et tam insecutor quam alii supradicti tanti mali participes, quamdiu in sua contumacia perdurarint, singulis diebus dominicis et festivis pulsatis campanis et candelis accensis per omnes illius loci ecclesias, in quo tantum fuerit facinus attentatum, nec non civitatum et diocesum vicinarum excommunicati publice nuntientur, nec ab alio quam a Romano pontifice cum fratrum suorum et iniuriam passi consensu possint absolutionis beneficium obtinere, nisi dumtaxat in mortis articulo constituti. Cum autem fuerint absolvendi, primo sufficienter et idonee caveant, quod inferende pene parebunt et auxiliante Domino penitentiam peragent iniungendam. Deinde per omnes illius loci ecclesias principales vicinorumque locorum diebus dominicis et solemnibus incedant nudi coram populo, femoralia tantum habentes et virgas ferentes in manibus, cum quibus per easdem ecclesias publice fustigentur, ituri postmodum ultra mare et ibidem acturi penitentiam per tres annos ad minus, nec exinde postmodum reversuri absque sedis apostolice licentia speciali. Verum cum tales gratiam reconciliationis meruerint, beneficio absolutionis obtento indulgeatur eis licentia, ut suam suorumque iniuriam prosequantur, et debitorum illorum, que contracta fuerint de postmodum acquisitis, repetitio non negetur. Illud autem non duximus omittendum, quod si quis fuerit in premissis nudo consilio vel simplici favore culpabilis, iudex in talem penam metiatur ex culpa, ut secundum quod excessus exegerit vindicta procedat. Premissis etiam dignum censuimus annectendum. ut si quisquam aliquo predictorum excessuum quemquam de clericis vel religiosis nostre familie vel cardinalium afficere forte presumpserit, proportionetur pena delicto, ita quod vindicta ex equo excessui respondente, ab offensa nostrorum cohibeantur deinceps manus temerarie formidine ultionis, quos Dei vel nostra seu fratrum nostrorum reverentia non coercet. Si quis vero vel per se vel per alium, quod absit, occiderit cardinalem vel evidentem dederit causam mortis, ultra quam premissa contineant, sic in eum potestas iurisdictionis insurgat, sic rigor ultionis insiliat, quod contra vite subsidium mortis solacium invocet, vivens pene non culpe, vindicte speculum non offense. Per hec quoque secularibus potestatibus non adimimus facultatem utendi legibus contra tales, quas adversus sacrilegos catholici principes ediderunt. Quis enim locus regiminis poterit esse tutus? quis rector securitate gaudebit. si Romana ecclesia, que omnium ecclesiarum disponente Domino caput est et magistra, casibus istis subicitur, si eius filii speciales huiusmodi periculis exponuntur? Quem ecclesie flium, quem fidei zelatorem contumella tanta non tangeret et confusio tam aspera non moveret? Porro qui filius est, dolebit, qui fidelis, matre fidei lesa ledetur. Quapropter si princeps, senator, consul, potestas, vel alius dominus seu rector, quocunque nomine censeatur, contra presumptores predictos presentis constitutionis tenorem non fecerit observari, tam ipse quam officiales ipsius infra mensem, postquam res ad notitiam eorum pervenerit, excommunicatione notetur. Quod si populus fuerit circa ista remissus et ad satisfaciendum rectores et officiales eius non compulerit, Romanus pontifex cum suis fratribus omnibus infra mensem exeat, si eum ibidem contigerit tunc morari, et antequam plenarie satisfiat, minime revertatur, nisi forsan inevitabilis ecclesie necessitas immineret, propter quam exitus eius et fratrum periculosus proculdubio redderetur. Preterea si populus rectorem sie excommunicatum tertio monitus, sicut poterit commoneri, a regimine amovere contempserit, subiciatur civitas interdicto, usquequo congrue satisfaciat. Dat. Reate, duodecimo Kal. Decemb. pontificatus nostri anno X.

regesto_sintetico: English translation: To the bishop, provost and dean of Worms. Some time ago the petition of the abbess of Quedlinburg, our beloved in Christ, was presented to us. The petition contained that some vassals and servants of hers and other accomplices of theirs from the diocese of Halberstadt had attempted to destroy the walls of the monastery and those surrounding it, and had inflicted various injuries and damages on it. Moreover, the provost of the abbess, who had been elected thrice but not consecrated, had, like a trespasser, taken possession of the abbey and had handed over to her her own goods and those of the church, and had made donations and grants of them to certain persons. We have therefore written to our beloved brother the archbishop of Magdeburg and his co-judges that they should prevent the abbess from bringing a legal action against those who had committed these injuries, and that they should cause her to make satisfaction for them, and that they should not proceed to inquire into the other matters, such as the trespasses committed by the abbess, which had been the subject of an investigation, in the absence of the legate. But recently it has been reported to us that the abbess has gone to the legate, who had come to Rome, and has asked him to warn the archbishop and his co-judges to proceed to judgment in the matter, as they had neglected to do so on the apostolic mandate. And since the legate did not know that the abbess had been informed of this, he had the privileges of the abbey, which she had held, and certain letters of the apostolic see, brought to her, and as soon as she had learned of this, she had them incised. And as she was afraid of the consequences of this, she submitted to the judgment, and swore to observe it, and the judgment was published, but not by the auctoritas of the one who had issued it, but by the power of the one who had received it. And as this judgment was not made by the one who had been entrusted with the matter, but by one who had been circumvented, we have written to you that you should inform the archbishop and his co-judges that they should cancel this judgment, and should revoke the concessions and grants made by the abbess, and that they should not proceed to inquire into the other matters, and that they should cause the abbess to give back her oath of fealty, which she had sworn to observe, and that they should absolve her from the obligation of observing the judgment, which was made without the authority of the one who issued it, and that they should restore the privileges and ornaments of the church to the place where they were kept before, and that they should cause the prelates of the churches to obey her, according to the custom of their church, and that they should not permit the abbess to alienate the goods and revenues of the church, or to confer them in fief on anyone without the consent of her chapter, and that they should prohibit her from being hospitable to the prelates of the church in an improper way, and that they should not permit her to retain the persons of the castellan of Anhalt and his two men, who had been given to her in fief, and that she should give back to the castellan the three manses which she had taken from him, and that she should give to the bishop of Halberstadt the advocacy of the church of Quandlinburg, which she had taken from him, and that she should give to the count of Anhalt the advocacy of the church of Quandlinburg, which she had taken from him, and that she should give back to the bishop of Halberstadt the benefices which she had given to certain persons, and that she should restore to the church the goods and revenues which she had alienated, and that she should not take the money of the mints and other officials of the church, and that she should not molest or burden the prelates of the church with improper hospitality. If any of the convent, vassals, servants, prelates, clerks, or citizens of the church should assert that the abbess has not observed these things, we have appointed inquisitors, namely, the provost of St. Mary, the provost of Willibert, the provost of Meinard of Halberstadt, and the master of A. of Magdeburg, to inquire into the matter, and if the abbess is found to have committed any of these things, she should be deposed from her office, and the convent should elect another abbess. Latin regesto: Gregorius IX papa II kal. Iunii anno X ad archiepiscopum Magdeburgensem, prepositum Wormaciensem, inquisitorem Halberstadensem, prepositum St. Marie, prepositum Willibertum, prepositum Meinardum, magistrum A. scolasticum, mandat, ut compositionem super castrum Quindelimburgense et alia in regeistro scriptam cancellent et abbatissam Quindeliburgensem ex iuramento absolutant et ei prelatos ecclesiarum obediens faciant. Dat. 26 Maii, anno X.
