Lealensem episcopum ex altera super quibusdam terris, mediantibus venerabili fratre nostro .. Rigensi episcopo et eius collegis, amicabiliter intervenit, prout in litteris inde confectis plenius continetur, sicut rite sine pravitate provide facta est et ab utraque parte sponte recepta, auctoritate apostolica confirmamus et presentis scripti pagina communimus. Ad maiorem autem rei evidentiam tenorem litterarum ipsarum de verbo ad verbum presentibus duximus inserendum. Qui talis est: Hermannus Dei gratia Lealensis episcopus, omnibus hoc scriptum legentibus salutem in eo qui est salus omnium. Notum esse volumus tam futuris quam presentibus, quod de consilio venerabilis fratris nostri domini Alberti Rigensis episcopi et ecclesie sue, peregrinorum quoque ac civium Rigensium cum fratribus militie Christi, iuxta quod in autentico ipsorum continetur, talem fecimus compositionem, ut videlicet a nobis et nostris successoribus teneant ipsi mediam circiter regionem episcopatus nostri iurisdictione civili perpetuo possidendam cum ecclesiis, decimis et omni emolumento temporali, terram videlicet Sackcle l, Normecunde, Moeche cum suis attinentiis et dimidiam partem terre Weigele, salvo nobis in omnibus iure spirituali. In illis igitur terris per ecclesias suas personas idoneas instituent et eas investiendas nobis presentabunt. Pro hiis autem terris nullum nobis temporale servitium aut aliud exhibebunt, nisi quod pro episcopatu nostro contra incursus hostium iugiter decertabunt et in spiritualibus nobis obedient, et cum ratione officii episcopalis ecclesias eorum visitabimus, expensas nobis necessarias ministrabunt. Fluvium autem Emevike! liberum relinquemus, vel gurgustrarum? regis? dimidium eis dimittemus; et ne quis autem eis super hac nostra concessione malitiosum afferat impedimentum, sub anathematis interminatione prohibemus. Et ut factum nostrum robur perpetuum obtineat, hanc cartam inde scribi et sigillo nostro et domini Rigensis episcopi et ecclesie sue muniri fecimus. regesto_sintetico: Translation: To Frederick, illustrious emperor and king of Sicily. You know, we are sure, that we have a sincere affection for you and that we aspire to your honor and name. We therefore recommend to your serenity what we know pertains to your honor. Your highness is well aware that a voice and opinion have been raised among all that your relationship with our beloved son in Christ, John, illustrious king of Jerusalem, has brought about a great elevation of his dignity and that God has magnificently exalted his highness by the bond of affinity with such a great prince. But now, to our great sorrow and the sorrow of many others, the opposite has happened, and the king has been depressed, contrary to our hopes and his own, unless you provide otherwise. All who hear this are astonished and say: “Is it more pleasing to your serenity to show favor to those who live there or to those who are infidels? Is it more terrible to your highness to be afraid of them or to be afraid of them? Who is more useful to the whole business of the Holy Land? Behold, if he were not related to you, he would be worthy to be entrusted with the kingdom. But if he were a simple knight, he should be decorated with royal dignity. Is it more beautiful for him to be the son-in-law of a knight than the king? Will it be more beautiful for his children, whom he will receive as a son-in-law, to have a grandfather who is a knight than a king? These and similar things are spoken by the small and the great, who are astonished at this fact and who detest it. We are also insulted by many because we have been mediators of this affinities and the king's depression is somehow imputed to us. Moreover, through your fact the devotion of many to the aid of the Holy Land has cooled down, as it is said, and you must do something to warm it up again, if you wish to reconcile him with your highness, as is fitting. We therefore desire to remove this cloud from the honor of your name and at the same time to restore the aid of the Holy Land, to which your and the king's reconciliation is most necessary. We therefore beg you, through the favor of Lord Jesus Christ, to consider how absurd it is that such a great man should be depressed because of the relationship of your highness, when it is fitting to exalt those who have obtained this relationship through your highness. Attend also to the utility of the Holy Land and recall the king to the fullness of imperial grace and reconcile him with you so that you may manifest your good will towards him by the deed. If you attentively consider the bond that unites you, you will easily see that there is no one, except the son of your son, who should love you more sincerely than the king. And if you know that we are particularly desirous of this reconciliation, behold, we are sending to you by special messenger the beloved son of the abbot of Viterbo, a man of great prudence, religiosity and fidelity, who is our depositee, and we beg you to treat him carefully in everything that pertains to this matter. Therefore, with great zeal, great care, and great diligence, it is your duty to take care that, for your glory, these shameful and harmful spots are removed, which not only diminish your temporal glory but also take away the eternal one from those who are infected by the aforementioned stain and add them to eternal torments. You, however, do not sincerely desire to apply the remedy to the aforementioned diseases, but you are doing it with fraud, damaging yourselves with fraud, and you adapt yourselves in such a way that the following sentence of Solomon can be applied to you: "They plot against their own blood and bring about their own destruction". For when you are exhorted by the exhortations of your prelates or apostolic threats to proceed against heretical wickedness or to do something in favor of ecclesiastical liberty, you, like experts in appearance, serve your own fame, which you wish to commend to people, rather than your conscience to God, and you superficially follow our statutes on expelling heretics and punishing their supporters, and those who have been expelled from your lands return after some time, and you, as if God's cleverness can be ridiculed, pass them under the cloak of dissimulation, and if you impose pecuniary penalties on them or their supporters, or if you do not impose them, or if you impose them and then secretly restore them to them, you strengthen them in their malice, so that they become secure. In the end, you place statutes on the election, addition, reduction, and change of the consuls. The pretext of the chapter abolishes and reduces to nothing what has been established for the benefit of the faith and ecclesiastical liberty, and it is done in such a way that not without great heart pain we report that heretical wickedness has infected almost the whole province of Lombardy and has almost completely destroyed ecclesiastical liberty in it, so that it has emigrated from its borders, as it is said, and the heretics no longer attack the vineyard of the Lord like foxes but like horses ready for battle, and they presume to rise openly against it, where they publicly preach and lead the flock of people, between whom they, like wolves, duchy the sheep. You, however, have a pure heart, turning to God, and we ask you to preserve the universality of your city from this fear, threatening eternal poverty, which leads to the treasure of confusion, and we warn you to abandon the crafty inventions, by which you deceive others more than yourselves, and to apply to the aforesaid diseases the remedies that have been established by the apostolic authority for the benefit of the faith, for the punishment of heretics and their supporters, and for the conservation of ecclesiastical liberty, and those that have been established by our beloved son Frederick, Roman Emperor, and those that have been expressed in the form of concord between him and some of your prelates, which have been extended to all cities of Lombardy by the apostolic see. We order you to observe them sincerely and faithfully, without any fraud, and to have them observed inviolably by your citizens and subjects, excluded from any kind of fraud, not to compel anyone to the solution of usury or to inflict a penalty on those who, on the contrary, obtain apostolic letters against usurers; doing so, you will bring to rest the stain of infamy, which has obscured your fame, and you will be worthy to be commended for the purity of faith and the conservation of ecclesiastical liberty, and we will know for certain that if you do not obey our salutary admonitions and precepts, and if you presume to favor heretics or their supporters in any way, we will invent something to constrain you and your prelates to pay the penalties for the aforesaid articles. Please take care to do so as wise and provident men, so that I do not have to be forced to consider a severe punishment against you, whose salvation we desire with paternal affection. Given at the Lateran, 23 April, 1216. REGESTO: Gregorius IX, episcopus etc. potestatibus et populis civitatum Lombardie. Cum enim vel vestrorum exhortationibus prelatorum vel apostolicis comminationibus excitamini ad procedendum contra hereticam pravitatem vel ad faciendum aliquid in favorem ecclesiastice libertatis, vos quasi ad oculum servientes, ac studentes potius famam vestram hominibus quam vestram Deo conscientiam commendare, facitis statuta nostra de expellendis hereticis et eorum fautoribus puniendis nec non de conservanda ecclesiastica libertate, ipsaque statuta superficialiter exequentes, hereticos ipsos a finibus vestris expellitis, qui post tempus modicum revertuntur, vosque, quasi Deus vestra possit astutia irrideri, id sub dissimulatione transitis. Si quando vero eis vel eorum fautoribus pecuniariam penam infligitis, aut illam non aufertis eisdem, aut ad solam apparentiam auferentes eis clanculo restituitis, et sic de impunitate securos in sua malitia roboratis. In fine quoque vestrorum ponitis statutorum, ut potestates, consiliarii addendi, minuendi atque mutandi liberam habeant potestatem. Pretextu cuius capituli evacuatur et redit in nichilum, quicquid pro fide catholica vel ecclesiastica libertate fuerat constitutum, et ita factum est, quod non sine magno cordis dolore referimus, ut heretice labis morbus, serpens paulatim ut cancer, provinciam vestram fere totam infecerit, et libertas ecclesiastica pene penitus subversa sit in eadem et ab eius finibus emigrarit, cum Cant. 2,16, heretici iam non vulpes latentes vineam demoliantur Dominicam, set quasi equi parati ad prelium presumant manifeste insurgere contra eam, in quibusdam locis publice Ps. enai. predicando, et quasi tauri inter vaccas populorum, inter videlicet seductibiles animas, ducatum gregis, dum episcopos se appellare presumunt, temere usurpando. Nunquid creditis, quod Deus ista non videat? Nunquid creditis, quod hec mala, nisi correxeritis, semper impunita relinquat? apparato: Greg. IX Reg. Vol. I, 48—49; Lib. I, 165a. Potthast, Reg. 8049.
testo_esteso: Gregorius etc. Frederico, Romanorum imperatori etc. spiritum consilii sanioris. Utinam ita imperialem celsitudinem assuefecisses timori divino, ut illi te tota devotione subiciens, qui tibi subiecit varias nationes, non solum ipsum contra te provocare metueres, ne arguereris ingratitudinis manifeste, set pro perceptis beneficiis ad serviendum sibi totis desideriis aspirares, qui cum non nisi pro te indigeat bonis tuis, nequaquam affectum nedum effectum irremuneratum relinqueret servientis. Utinam quoque benignitatem et patientiam ecclesie Romane humiliter recognoscas; quam cum exasperaveris multipliciter, ultra quam expediat recenseri, ne celsitudinem tuam conviciis velle lacescere videamur, ipsa erga te semper affluens pietatis materne visceribus, tecum numquam processit nisi in spiritu lenitatis. Quare arguimur, et Exod. 23,19. forsitan non indigne, quod quasi coquentes edum in lacte matris te in tuis noxiis voluntatibus fovere videmur in multorum preiudicium et scandalum ecclesie generalis. Licet enim ex eo quod Christi causam, quam videbaris magnanimiter assumpsisse, sperantibus fere omnibus te illam ad finem deducere gloriosum, ita enerviter, ita periculose, ita misere deiecisti, dolor immoderatus, stupor immensus et enormis orror corpus et animam nostram undique circumdederint, ita quod fere in extasi positi de recuperatione Terre Sancte pene penitus cepimus desperare, flentes amarissime nichilominus tot et tantos occasione tui mortuos Christianos et gementes illorum exilium, utinam non excidium!, qui pro tua fiducia iter arripuerunt in eiusdem terre subsidium transfretandi, omne tamen quod potuimus erga te servavimus mansuetudinis moderamen, illam tantum sententiam publicando, quam ipse in te voluntarius feceras promulgari, et retardando illas, quas consensisti ferendas, nisi conditiones alias quas promiseras adimpleres. Ne autem possit quispiam suspicari, quod sinceritatis affectus, quem erga PrOV. 3412. te gerimus, sit ex hoc vel in aliquo diminutus, cum dicatur potius, quod pater filium quem diligit corripit, et e contrario qui parcit virge odit filium, ea que ad salutem anime tue, quam totis visceribus affectamus, pertinere cognoscimus, nec non ea que ad honoris tui augmentum proveniunt, quem libenter in quibus convenit promovemus, serenitati tue non desinimus suadere. Ideoque imperialem mansuetudinem rogamus. monemus et hortamur attente, obsecrantes per aspersionem sanguinis Iesu Christi, quatinus ne, quod absit, de numero sis illorum, de quibus Dominus conqueritur per prophetam dicens: “Percussi eos et non doluerunt, et attriti renuerunt accipere leremss. disciplinam', set potius correptus in misericordia correptionem recipias et medelam, ad solvenda varia vincula, quibus teneris astrictus, instanter intendas, et ad gremium matris ecclesie te desiderabiliter expectantis cum omni celeritate festines, satisfaciendo Deo, qui tibi utique satis fecit, et hominibus iustitiam exhibendo. Sicut enim scire te credimus, contra nos murmuratur immo clamatur, quod prelatorum exilium, ecclesiarum, hospitalium, orphanorum et viduarum nec non aliorum religiosorum spoliationes et alias atroces iniurias visi sumus hactenus sub dissimulatione transire. Illud quoque nobis sepius exprobratur, quod cum ecclesia Romana se ad precum tuarum instantiam, prout ex litteris tuis apparet, fideiussorie obligarit super servanda compositione inter te ac comites Celanensem et Raynaldum de Aversa sollempniter celebratal, ita tue sublimitati detulimus, quod illorum videmur iustitiam sustulisse, qui numquam disponimus cuiquam in suo iure deesse. Nec illorum vociferationes possumus obaudire, qui clamantes quod ad preces pie recordationis Honorii pape predecessoris nostri dilectum filium nobilem virum .. comitem Rogerium ? in tuam recipiens gratiam et favorem promiseras, quod ipsum in nullo minueres set potius augmentares, convitiando concludunt, quod ipsius exilium, quem ipse crucesignari fecisti, et captivitatem filii quasi conniventibus oculis pertransimus, qui afflictis et captivis specialiter tenemur adesse. Ad hec cum universi crucesignati sub speciali sedis apostolice protectione consistant, multi subsanniant convitiantes yronice ac 25 dicentes: “Heccine qualiter sunt protecti, qui cum crucem assumerent potentes et divites, nunc a te deiecti exulant et mendicant!" Preterea cum regnum Sicilie pleno proprietatis iure ad Romanam spectet ecclesiam, non solum calamitatibus oppressorum compassionis affectu confodimur, gementium quod illos in eis sustinemus impie servitutis abusus, quos vix debemus in regnis aliis comportare, set confundimur a vocibus exprobrantium et obloquentium, quod tales afflictiones in hiis, qui ad sedem apostolicam te mediante pertinent, toleramus, quales ipse in hiis qui ad te spectant aliquo medio nullatenus tolerares, cum intersit nostra potissime beneficio consolationis adesse quibuslibet tribulatis. Quare nec illorum penas nec tuas culpas possumus ulterius salva conscientia comportare, presertim cum super hiis iam monitus fueris diligenter. Ut igitur consciencie ac fame tam tue quam nostre propitiari proberis. monemus, rogamus et hortamur et pro dono speciali deposcimus, ut memor quod nil valet homini si universum mundum lucretur, anime vero sue sustineat detrimentum, Matth. 1628. taliter super hiis provideas, quod solo virtutis amore que debita sunt videaris cupere adimplere, nosque facias de tua conversione immo profectu letari; sciturus quod parati 40 sumus ad gratiam, ubi tamen scimus iustitiam non perire. Alioquin, quantumcumque tibi deferre velimus, supradicta nequaquam dissimulare poterimus, quin secundum Deum et iustitiam procedamus. Data Lateran.2

regesto_sintetico: Translation in English: The humble and unworthy patriarch of Jerusalem, Gregory, to the most holy father and lord, Gregory, bishop of the church of Rome, supplicant with the greatest reverence and devotion. We have thought it necessary to inform your holiness about the state of the Holy Land, in order to inform you better about the matter. You should know that on the feast of St. Clement the Emperor went to Joppa and the Christian army followed him. When he was there, the pilgrims ran to the nearby villages to seek victuals; the sultan, who was nearby with his army, ill responded to the messengers of the emperor who had gone there, saying that during the negotiations for peace Joppa should not have been fortified, nor the villages of the sultan damaged. For this, he sent back the messengers with indignation and shame. The emperor then made restore all that the pilgrims had taken from the villages, and the villages were entrusted to the sultan, who began to soothe him. Meanwhile, the sultan sent him some vile and contemptible instruments, which were directed at a turcopole and a tonsor, ordering that his land should abound in such things. The emperor then sent his notary to the sultan to negotiate the peace again; who was received ill by the sultan, and was sent back by him, and was treated turbidly and his goods were seized by the sarracens. After this, the sultan sent him his arms, his own, a helmet, a helmet and a sword, and ordered him to do with the emperor as he pleased, since he would never arm himself against him. The sultan did not respond to this, despising all that was done. Meanwhile, some of the sultan's men, who pretended to love the emperor, said to the notary, if it were agreeable to the sultan, that Count Thomas would return to him, and they would negotiate a peace or a concord between them. The notary then supplicated the sultan with great insistence to grant this favor, and he finally granted it. So the count returned to the sultan, and through him and his familiar, the negotiations for peace, which had been interrupted, were resumed. While this was happening, our poor pilgrims were killed and destroyed indifferently, and, as we have learned, more than 500 of our men were killed, and the sultan's men were not killed by our men or by theirs, since the sultan's men did not reach the number of denarii. Some of our men were even captured, and when they were freed, they were sent back to the sultan in honor, so that those who were bringing them back were plundered by the sarracens on the way, and barely escaped with their lives. Thus those who were persecuted by the enemies of the faith did not have the aid of the prince, and if anyone was offended by him, he was punished by him. It must also be said that it was considered a great shame for Christianity that the emperor asked the sultan to have his men guarded by the sarracens at his expense, and that the sultan agreed to this. testo_esteso: ILittere ad dominum papaml'. Sanctissimo in Christo patri et domino Gregorio, divina providentia summo pontifici, G., miseratione divina patriarcha Ierosolimitanus humilis et indignus, salutem cum summa reverentia et devota pedum oscula beatorum. Sanctitatem” vestram, pater sancte, super statu negotii Terre Sancte duximus presentibus instruendam, ut ex rebus plenius cognitis motus vestre beatitudinis valeat de singulis amplius informari. Sciat igitur sanctitas vestra, quod circa festum beati Clementis ! imperator Ioppen profectus est de Accon, ipsumque secutus est exercitus Christianus. Ipso autem illuc perveniente ac incipiente munire, peregrini ad circumadiacentia casalia cucurrerunt pro victualibus perquirendis; quod audiens soldanus, qui prope erat cum suo exercitu, male respondit nuntiis imperatoris, qui iam de Accon iverant ad eundem, et dixit, quod durante tractatu pacis Ioppen non debuisset causa munitionis faciende venisse, nec frangi sua casalia debuisse; propter que memoratos nuntios cum indignatione et confusione remisit. Ad hec imperator omnia, que peregrini ceperant a casalibus antedictis, fecit restitui, et ipsa casalia cum omnibus affidari, soldanum incipiens sic placare. Eo tempore ei soldanus quedam instrumenta misit vilia et despecta, que directe pretendebant effectum turcopuli et tonsoris, mandans quod terra sua talibus abundaret. Ad hec imperator remisit suum notarium ad soldanum pro tractatu pacis iterum inchoando; qui male receptus a soldano, statim ab eo recessit, fuitque in suo reditu a Sarracenis tractatus turpiter et bonis omnibus spoliatus. Postmodum non sine gravi scandalo peregrinorum ac mira confusione idem notarius est remissus, mittens soldano arma sua propria, loricam scilicet, galeam et gladium, atque mandans, sicut fuit nobis pro certo relatum, quod faceret de ipso imperatore quidquid vellet, quia nunquam contra eum de cetero se armaret. Ad quod nichil respondit soldanus, vilipendens omnia que fiebant. Inter hec quidam de familiaribus soldani, qui imperatorem diligere se fingebat?, dixit notario, si esset de beneplacito soldani, quod comes Thomas? reverteretur ad ipsum, ipsi duo de pace aliqua et concordia iterato tractarent. Super quo sepedictus notarius soldano cum magna instantia supplicavit, ut sibi in hac parte suum prestaret assensum; qui tandem concessit supplicatam gratiam supplicanti. Sic igitur reverso comite ad soldanum, per ipsum et familiarem predictum tractatus pacis, qui modo supradicto in confusionem totius Christianitatis fuerat dissolutus, fuit confusione duplici denuo inchoatus. Quo durante capiebantur nostri miseri peregrini et interficiebantur indifferenter, et secundum quod intelleximus veraciter, sic bene amisimus plusquam quingentos de nostris, et ut verum fateamur, postquam Syriam imperator intravit, a suis vel ab illis de exercitu Christiano capti vel interfecti Sarraceni numerum denarium non attingunt. Immo quidam in exercitu fuit captus, qui statim liberatus, claris vestibus indutus et sic honorifice est soldano remissus, ita quod illi, qui eum ex parte imperatoris conducebant, fuerint a Sarracenis in via bonis omnibus spoliati, vixque mortem evadere potuerunt. Sic itaque qui ab inimicis fidei infestabantur, principis auxilium non habebant; si quisa autem eos ex quacunque 2. Cor. 155. causa offenderet, puniebatur ab eo; unde foris gladius et intus timor nostris assidue imminebat. Nec illud silendum est, quod ad maius dedecus Christianitatis cedere visum fuit. Imperator rogavit soldanum, ut per Sarracenos suos in ipsius imperatoris expensis Christianum exercitum faceret custodiri; quod cum ordinatum a soldano fuisset, quia de lupis erant pastores effecti, multi de nostris sub illa confidentia ceciderunt, et quod cum maxima verecundia referimus et rubore, imperatori soldanus, audiens quod secundum morem Sarracenicum se haberet, misit cantatrices, que et saltatrices dicuntur, et ioculatores, personas quidem non solum infames, verum etiam de quibus inter Christianos haberi mentio non deberet. Cum quibus idem princeps huius mundi vigiliis, potationibus et indumentis et omni more Sarracenico se gerebat. Etsi talia abhorruit exercitus Iesu Christi, adhuc, dante Domino, loco et tempore sanctitatis vestre auribus referent, qui propriis oculis hec viderunt. Erga Sarracenos non solum largus extitit sed effusor, ac si emere vellet pacem, quam obtinere non poterat violentia vel timore. Sane longe ante nativitatem Domini precepit biscottum fieri et galeas et omnia vasa sua pararil; quod audientes Sarraceni, licet eum antea non timerent, ipsum tamen amplius contempserunt. Denique in dominica septuagesime? pacis volens publicare tractatum, qui usque tunc admodum fuerat occultatus, vocavit ad se circiter quatuor de maioribus Syrie, eisque intimavit, quod adeo pauper erat, quoda ibi non poterat moram trahere longiorem, quia iam sibi deficiebant expense, ut consilia eorum eo facilius ad suum propositum ac desiderium inclinaret. Cum autem de paupertate prologum perfecisset, aperuit eis, quod soldanus offerebat ei civitatem sanctam, retento sibi templo Domini, quod a Sarracenis custodiri debebat, ut illud sine tributo intrare possent libere Sarraceni, qui illuc vellent causa peregrinationis venire, et quod civitatem poterat firmare; Bethleem et duo minima casalia, que sunt inter Bethleem supra stratam et Ierusalem; casalia que sunt inter Ierusalem recto itinere usque Ioppen; Nazareth et duo casalia modica, que sunt inter Nazareth et Accon recto itinere; Tyruma cum quibusdam pertinentiis suis, quod non debebat firmari; Sydonem cum plano et duo casalia modica, que sunt in plano. Et sciendum quod patriarche extra civitatem non restituitur unus passus terre, nec domui Sepulchri Dominici, nec hospitali sancti Iohannis, nec de Latina, nec de Iosaphat, non de Templo Domini, nec Montis Oliveti, nec Montis Sion abbatibus, ut brevius dicamus, nichil restituitur extra civitatem preter ea, que sunt superius nominata, que tamen non sunt de casalibus, que ad aliquem pertineant de corpore civitatis, nisi domui Templi ad quam aliqua pertinent ex eis, que sunt inter Ierusalem et Ioppen. Casalia vero, que restituta dicuntur, pauca sunt numero nec plurimum commendanda valore. Ad hec supradicti nobiles responderunt, quod ex quo ita pauper erat, quod ulterius remanere non posset, ei factum illud disconsulere non audebant, ita tamen si civitatem retinere poterat et munire. Postmodum vocati fuerunt magistri domorum et super hoc requisiti; qui una cum episcopis Anglie responderunt, quod sine nostro consilio nichil penitus responderent, dicentes quod nostrum erat consilium potissimum requirendum, tum propter dignitatem patriarchatus, tum quia in illis partibus ac negotio precipue Iesu Christi legationis officio fungebamur. Ad hec imperator respondit, quod nostrum super hoc consilium non requireret nec haberet. Sic igitur imperator clam, nemine de terra presente, presentibus nuntiis soldani, iuravit se servaturum ea que continebantur in quadam charta clausa, que nunquam coram aliquo peregrino nec aliquo de terra lecta fuit vel aperta, nec coram nuntiis soldani ab ipso imperatore baronibus vel magistris recitata, nec ab ipso manifestata soldano; et soldanus contentus fuit solo principis iuramento, nec alterius fuit super hoc securitas requisita, quia bene sciebat imperator, quod si contingeret ab alio hanc securitatem requiri, sicut fieri consuevit, ille qui requireretur vellet sibi explanari singula capitula diligenter, antea quam iuraret. Sed imperator cum male ageret, lucem rationis in omnibus declinabat. Tandem vocatis Theutonicis suis, qui nichil aliud affectabant nisi quod possent visitare sepulchrum, allegare cepit imperator et magister Alemannorum post ipsum, quomodo per eos fuerat exaltatus et quantum in negotio illo eum Dominus honorabat, non suis meritis sed orationibus corundem. Et si omnes alii id disconsulerent, consilio eorum se reputabat contentum, rogans eos ut de honore suo gauderent et cantum in signum exultationis et letitie inchoarent; que sola natio cantum levavit et luminare fecit, omnibus aliis stultitiam reputantibus quod fiebat, cum multi ex iis fraudem iam cognoscerent manifeste. His peractis magister Alemannorum, comes Thomasius et dominus Sydonis iverunt ad soldanum Babylonie, ut super conventionibus initis reciperent sacramentum ab ipso; quo recepto ivit dominus Sydonis ad soldanum Damasci l, ut ab eo similiter reciperet sacramentum. Sed idem soldanus iam presenserat, quod soldanus Babylonie et Seraphius?, avunculi eius, eum exheredare penitus intendebant et inter se dividere terram suam, propter quod se in Damascum recepit, et adunatis suis eis viriliter resistere a conabatur. Qui treugam iurare noluit ullo modo, dicens quod soldanus Babylonie avunculus suus terram ipsius Christianis sine consensu suo reddere de iure non poterat nec debebat. Inter hec magister Alemannorum ad magnificandam vocem, immo ad palliandam principis falsitatem, malitiam atque fraudem, mandavit nobis consulens atque rogans, ut ad exercitum personaliter veniremus, cum peregrinis civitatem sanctam sollempniter intraturi, et quod deinceps ordinari deberent nostro consilio universa, nostrumque adventum imperator plurimum affectabat. Circa idem magister valde sollicitus erga amicos et familiares nostros de exercitu, ut nos ad veniendum inducerent suis precibus cum affectu.....; quorum omnium receptis litteris et perlectis, caute considerandum duximus et notandum, quod imperator sue intendens dilatare fimbrias falsitatis, et attendens quod treuge et conventiones, quas cum soldano inierat fraudulenter et malitiose, omni fundamento veritatis et stabilitatis carerent, nec tam vesanum scelus posset diutius occultari, cum ipse esset de terra recessurus instanter, nec terra, quam se acquisisse iactabat, posset retineri per ipsum, se exoneratum crederet immo honoratum omnino, et nos post recessum suum quacunque occasione dimitteret in acquisitione, quam se fecisse fingebat, vel operis continuatione Ioppen, et si postmodum de Ierusalem aliqua necessitate contingeret nos exire vel opus relinquere imperfectum, diceret : “Ego acquisivi civitatem sanctam, quam perdidit patriarcha et ecclesie Romane legatus; incepi munire Ioppen, et est perdita per eundem', et non solum nobis id verum etiam ecclesie imputaret. Ad hec, pater sancte, licet malitiam imperatoris ac fraudem et circumventionem magistri in hac parte perpenderemus expresse, tamen ad intellecta tunc pretermisimus ex industria respondere, rescribentes magistro, ut transcriptum treuge et omnium conventionum nobis transmitteret de verbo ad verbum, ut habita deliberatione debita quod mandabat possemus confidentius ac securius adimplere. Non enim tutum erat nobis, immo admodum indiscretum, quod nos in manu committeremus soldani, de cuius nobis forma treuge non constabat. Quo intellecto magister incontinenti per fratrem W.a de ordine Predicatorum, penitentiarium nostrum, nobis misit supradictum transcriptum; quo retento ac diligenter notato vidimus in eo inter cetera quedam mirabilia contineri, que sanctitati vestre de verbo ad verbum duximus transmittendat, beate circumspectionis vestre relinquentes iudicio principis huius malitiam evidentem. Nos igitur ex forme treugarum instrumentis, utpote qui nichil aliud querebamus, ex tunc incepimus nostrum consilium ordinare, qualiter in toto negotio procedere deberemus. regesto_sintetico: Translation to English: To the citizens of Gaeta, faithful sons. The apostolic see, as a pious mother, cannot forget the sorrows of its children, who have often been oppressed by many troubles and are now in the depths of affliction. Therefore, desiring to free them from the heavy yoke of servitude, it has undertaken their cause and has borne the expenses and labors innumerable that have resulted from it, not sparing its own faithful. Since you have returned to the faith and to the obedience of the Roman Church, to which it was not doubtful that you were bound, and have adhered to it as subjects and faithful, we decree that you be free from the burdens of servitude and be subject to the sweet yoke and easy burden of the Lord, to whom you have adhered, and that you be recreated by the breasts of consolation of the apostolic see and of your lady, the mother of you all, who have rejoiced in the sorrow that you have endured. Therefore, beloved sons, we wish to provide for your convenience, as the Roman Church has been accustomed to provide for the utility of its subjects, and, inclining to your supplications, with the counsel and assent of our brothers, we grant you the power to elect consuls and rectors, and all the other liberties that the city of Anagni enjoys from the apostolic see. We also grant you the immunity from all obligations in the kingdom, including the payment of passage toll, pedage, falangatico, and datione, which is called 'protection', and half of the amount that is owed to the court for the above-mentioned services, as well as the galearum of the protents. We grant you the power to mint silver coins, on which the image of the head of the blessed Peter with the superscription of your city, and on the other side the image of the pope with the superscription of our name, shall be depicted. We also grant you the freedom to extend or build a new city on Mount Martin, near the present one, so that for each coin minted, you shall pay us and our successors 50 gold tarenes. We also confirm all the liberties and the laudable customs that you had during the time of the illustrious King William in electing consuls, judges and other officials, annuarii, notaries, in the cognition and termination of causes, in the salt duka, in the ports, i.e. in the city and from it to Cannetum, in selling salt, in buying and exporting it, and in transporting it freely to Gaeta, in the labors of hereditary goods that you have in the county of Fundo, and in defending you from your enemies outside the kingdom and in making peace with them. We also grant you the islands of Pontian, Palmeria, Senna, Pantatera and San Martin with their fishermen and tenements, as you had them during the time of the aforesaid king, and all your good customs, saving all the just titles and the obligations due to the court, for which someone from our land shall be placed by the apostolic see, who shall be paid by you annually. The Lord has given you a sword to avenge your enemies, who have resisted his divine power. We have learned that you have sent us your nuncios, P. archbishop of Messina and the judge of the imperial court, P. They told us that you have a pious intention and a holy desire to follow our counsel, which was conceived by divine inspiration. We are pleased and we thank you in the Lord and in his power, who has united the mother with her son and the son with his mother through the spirit of charity, so that the unity of feelings and the identity of the souls, which are burdened with the weight of the honor and the burden of the bishopric and the empire, may be alleviated. regesto_sintetico: Translation to English: .. Bishops of Minden, of Lübeck, and of Ratisbon. The light of eternal light, Lucifer, who was left without light, because, led by the pride of the fallen angel, he incurred the darkness of perpetual blindness, has been lost and has been brought to perdition. He who is lost is the servant of perdition, who, deprived of the eternal delights of the human condition, cannot obtain the dignity of the human condition, because wretched people are often afflicted by the prosperity of the blessed, and Lucifer, thinking that the condition of his wretchedness will be diminished by this, seeks to bring the happy ones to the depth of his own miseries, thinking that he will be able to obtain the condition of his wretchedness. But the malice of the devil, which has been bent on deceit, does not know how to find the lost in the perils, and therefore it has caused the Stedingi, who live in the province of Bremen, to be alienated from the knowledge of the Creator, and to be led to such an extent that they have lost the way of truth and have been taken into the path of folly. They, who have abandoned the path of truth, do not fear God or men, and they despise the doctrine of holy Mother Church, and they attack her liberty. They have become cruel, like ferocious beasts, and they spare neither sex nor age. They shed blood like water, and they slaughter clerics and religious people with a cruel death, and they nail some to the wall, to the shame of the Crucified. They also, in order to manifest their perfidy and contempt for divine power, ask for answers from demons, make waxen images, and consult false prophets, and they commit other works of perversity, which are a source of wonder and a subject of tears. But since we must immediately intervene to stop such great iniquities, in order that their terror may feel the effects of the immediate intervention of the virtue of the faithful, we ask, we command, and we exhort you, through apostolic letters, to take care to take the brothers of the order of the Preachers under your protection, in order to exercise the office of preaching. We order you to put those who live in the dioceses of Paderborn, Hildesheim, Verden, Minden, Ratisbon, and Bremen under the banner of the cross, in order that the faithful living in these dioceses may obtain the fruits of life, and that they may deserve the joys of eternal happiness. We have entrusted the remission of sins to you, and to those who will take part in this work, for 20 days to those who will go to preach, and for 3 years to those who will bear the burden of the work, and for 5 years to those who will be detained in the place. We also remit the remission of sins to those who will contribute from their means to the support of the brothers. We remit the remission of sins to those who will have died in this work, and we forgive them all their sins. We also remit the remission of sins to those who have contradicted you, and we grant you the faculty of imposing ecclesiastical censure on them. We also order you to entrust the brothers who you will find expedient, who belong to the order of the Preachers, with the care of this matter. The indulgence of the apostolic seat is not opposed to them, if they will have made any contribution. Given at Anagni, 28 October, year 6. testo_esteso: .. priori et fratribus ordinis fratrum Predicatorum Warmaciensium. Ad tollendas lites, quas fraternum plerumque odium comitatur, per quas ctiam quies profectusque regularium impeditur, speciali sollicitudine intendere nos oportet, quamquam generaliter omnium fidelium amplecti pacem et querere ex iniuncte nobis amministrationis officio teneamur. Ex parte siquidem vestra fuit propositum coram nobis, quod olim inter vos ex parte una et venerabilem fratrem nostrum episcopum 20 et dilectos filios capitulum Warmaciense ex altera super quibusdam areis, quas in civitate Warmaciensi ad edificandum et habitandum emistis, questione suborta, post compositionem quandam inter vos factam per dilectum filium nostrum Osttonem] Sancti Nicolai in Carcere Tulliano diaconum cardinalem, tunc apostolice sedis legatum, et ordinationem, quam.. decanus Treverensis et coniudices sui delegati a nobis 25 fecerunt, tandem talis inter vos et eundem episcopum amicabilis compositio intervenit, videlicet quod prefatus episcopus vobis et successoribus vestris emendi aream sive locum ad ecclesiam construendam et claustrum et inhabitandi, ubicumque volueritis infra muros civitatis eiusdem, excepto illo loco dumtaxat ubi priores habueratis areas, salva in aliis ordinatione predicta, auctoritatem tribuit et assensum, 30 censu sibi debito in eodem loco quem emendum et construendum duxeritis reservato, prout in litteris confectis exinde plenius continetur. Quare nobis humiliter supplicastis, ut compositionem ipsam apostolico dignaremur munimine roborare. Nulli ergo nostre — confirmationis etc. Si quis autem etc. Dat. Anagnie, IV Idus Februarii, anno sexto.

regesto_sintetico: Translation in English: The Pope Gregory IX writes to the Sultan of Damascus, asking him to acknowledge the path of truth. He mentions the role of the three orders of patriarchs, prophets and apostles, as the “three candelabra” through which God, in His infinite wisdom and goodness, has enlightened humanity, guiding it through history. He recalls the promises made to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and the prophecies of Isaiah and other prophets, which speak of the birth of the Saviour. He describes the miracles performed by Jesus, from the Annunciation to the Resurrection, and the spread of Christianity throughout the world. He exhorts the Sultan to accept the faith of Christ, so that he and his people may be saved, and to receive the Preachers and other Friars Minor who have been sent to preach to him. Gregory IX encourages him to treat them kindly and to listen to their words, so that he may come to know the truth and be enlightened. He reminds him that the faithful, who have been redeemed by the blood of Christ, will be saved, and that he himself may become the ruler of the kingdom of heaven. He writes in the name of God and of the Church, and invokes the testimony of the heavens, the earth and all creatures, so that if the Sultan does not accept the faith, he will have no excuse on the day of judgment. He wishes that the Sultan and his people may be saved, and that the Pope and the Church may have a share in their salvation. REGESTO: Pope Honorius III Gregory IX writes to the Sultan of Damascus, inviting him to accept the Christian faith and asking him to receive the Preachers and other Friars Minor who have been sent to preach to him. (1243, March 12)

regesto_sintetico: Translation in English: To Master Conrad of Marbuch, a preacher of the word of God. Judgement of yours and your research! Who has known the sense of the Lord or who has been his counsellor, that, whereas our wounds have already been exposed in his sight, our iniquities have already reached our heads, whereas the coldness of charity has reached many, iniquity has already abounded, that we, who are miserable in human condition, are caught in so many nets of error, are soiled by so many contaminations, and are so wounded by so many deviations, that many, despising the borders of Sion, have climbed up the heights of Samaria, and, being bound to David's house, say: "We have no part in the house of David nor inheritance in the son of Jesse." But, O good actor and giver of all things, knowing that those who seek him are helped in all good, not in order that he may obtain knowledge by experience, since he knows all things and foresees them from eternity, but in order that we may be made certain of our strength or weakness, and that we may give to understand those who are, pseudochrists and false prophets, about the end of the world and the sunset of the times, as the great doctor says: "It is necessary that there be heresies, so that the tried may be made manifest" (1 Corinthians 11, 19). Since venerable brothers, the archbishop of Mainz and the bishop of Hildesheim, have sent us letters full of great sorrow and not empty of pain, about the abominations of some heretics, which have been brought to our knowledge by you, our heart is saddened by surprise, our soul is greatly troubled, we have been drunken with wormwood, and our mind is filled with bitterness, because the enemy has sent his hand to the desirable things, and has brought to the unhappy men the shame of the passion, so that they commit such things, which it is a shame to say, and which, if they had committed, they would be ashamed. How much we are troubled by sorrow, how much we are tormented by pain, when we hear that the redeemed by Christ are held captive by the devil! Who will not be angry with such contumely of the Creator? Who will not be incensed by such injustice of the Redeemer? What penalty can be taken against such pestilential people? But, since we know that the hand of the Lord is not short (Habacuc 2, 13) so that he could not save and purify them, nor reduce them to the pure wine of scorza (Exodus 19, 1, 40), we, having compassion on them, not because of their contrition, but because of the hand of the Lord, who is not willing that their punishment should be imputed to us, if we did not bind them with the bonds of correction, and anoint them with the oil of meekness, we have resolved to take care of their correction. Since, however, in your mouth there is no word of the Lord bound (Matthew 24, 24), and God has given you a tongue educated, who, since he has poured upon you the rain of his mercy, which gives abundantly to all, is powerful in work and in speech, you, who have been taught by the anointing and have been instructed by the Spirit who proceeds from the Father and the Son, are able to labor in this work and in the sermon, and we, who have given thanks to the dispenser of all graces for the favors which we have received, and have asked him to complete the good work which he has begun, beg, exhort and command you in the Lord, that you may have discretion, and may be able to alleviate their pain and to heal their wounds. Take up the sword of your strength on your thigh, the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, to show them the remedy of their wounds, and to correct them with diligent care and solicitude. But if the lamp of the Lord, the breath of man, which investigates the secrets of the belly, does not illuminate their hearts with your diligent warning, but rather hardens them, as if they had been rejected by divine judgment, because of the greatness of their fault, and they are worthy to be reproached, since in such a great and serious illness more severe remedies are needed, where mild remedies do not help, and to apply iron and fire to their wounds, which do not feel the medicine of fomentation, you, calling, defending and supporting them, will urge all the faithful of Christ to rise up in his aid against them, and to fight against them manfully. regesto_sintetico: Translation in English: To the bishops of Münster, Lübeck and Ratisbon. On account of this, a great scandal has arisen in the lands of the Germans, to such an extent that not only those heretics, but also the heretics of other sects, who had been hiding in secret, have grown strong against the Church of God and the Catholic faith. We therefore, considering that such evil doings are to be remedied with all speed, have granted you our letters in mandato and in remission, so that, taking up the office of preaching, you may strive to induce the faithful in the dioceses of Paderborn, Hildesheim, Verden, Minden, Osnabrück, Bremen and Paderborn to avenge the Lord Christ, and that they may be rewarded with an indulgence, which we have deemed worthy of being expressed in our said letters. On the other hand, we have been asked to take into account the gravity of the situation and to provide a remedy. We have therefore sent you by repeated letters, with all due haste, that you should induce the faithful to take up arms against the heretics, and that you should not cease to instruct them, both by preachers and by other means, to make war against them. If the heretics, having been warned, refuse to repent and to return to the bosom of the Church, we order you, with all due urgency, to use the spiritual and material sword against them, and to make use of the power of arms against them. We also command that those who have taken up arms against them should be rewarded with the indulgence granted to those who go to the aid of the Holy Land. But if the heretics do not obey your warnings, you should proceed with the same zeal as before. Dated at Rome, July 11, year 7. Obeunte siquidem ipsius ecclesie antistite, in successore ipsius eligendo iuxta morem aliarum ecclesiarum cathedralium Saxonie ipsius ecclesie canonicos liberam habere decernimus electionem, nullusque eis invitis per surreptionem aliquam preponatur; set ille in ipsa ecclesia locum et officium pontificis obtineat, quem unanimi voluntate vel de consilio maioris et sanioris partis eiusdem ecclesie capituli de gremio ipsius ecclesie vel aliunde viderint eligendum. Alie vero conventuales ecclesie et plebani ipsius diocesis non se faciende electioni aliquatenus ingerere presumant?, set consensum electioni canonice facte prebeant. Sancimus insuper, ut archidiaconatum Brandeburgensem de Ketin et Rinowe usque Iuterbokb, Iezzant et Dame versus meridiem, et terre de Havelant versus orientem usque ad flumen, quod Odera dicitur, et quantumcumque illuc idem episcopatus in posterum fuerit ampliatus, item versus occidentem usque ad flumen, quod Ila dicitur; preterea de burchwardis Scartowe, Mokerne, Lauborch, excepta ecclesia de Dalechowe, ecclesiam quoque sancti Nicolai in Borch, que ultra Ilam sita est, eo quod filia sit ecclesie sancte Marie in Borch, ad ipsum archidiaconatum, iuxta quod hactenus est observatum, decernimus pertinere. Iesere quoque, Gorceke, Bukowe, Beltez, Nimic, Bricene, Beliz, Sarmunt, Trebin, Lukenwolde, Parcem quoque, Gentin, Milau, Plawe, Pritserwe, Ratenowe, Vrisac, Belin, Cremme, Bothzowe, Cedenic, et in quantum ab ea parte diocesis se extendit, et quecumque territoria vel ville infra hos terminos in posterum fuerint edificate, sicut eum ipsius ecclesie prepositi hactenus rationabiliter possederunt, ita quoque ipsum indivisum et absque diminutione qualibet imperpetuum obtineant, et infra prenotatos terminos iurisdictionem ordinariam exerceant, corrigentes et reformantes in clericis et in laicis et sacramentis ecclesiasticis, que correctione et reformatione viderint expedire, obedientes foveant et confortent, rebelles vero et contumaces corrigant et emendent, ne sanguis eorum de ipsorum manibus requiratur. Parrochianorum quoque in eodem archidiaconatu decedentium vestes meliores cum superpellicio, equum optimum cum pertinentiïs iuxta morem Magdeburgensis ecclesie et suffraganearum ecclesiarum eiusdem metropolis et consuetudinem hactenus observatam presenti scripto ecclesie memorate prepositis confirmamus. Sciendum quoque est, quod dicte Brandeburgensis ecclesie prepositus, qui et episcopalis sedis archidiaconus est, totius diocesis in absentia episcopi curam in omnibus gerit, tam in iudiciis exercendis et curis ecclesiarum conferendis quam in aliis episcopalibus negotiïs procurandis. Mortuo etiam episcopo, nomine ecclesie cathedralis ad usum futuri successoris non solum spiritualia verum temporalia amministrat. Statuimus preterea, ne aliquis plebanus ipsius archidiaconatus in ecclesia sua vicarium instituere aut pensionem ei assignare audeat sine prepositi sui coniventia et consensu. Decernimus insuper statuentes, ut dicte ecclesie canonici a festo sancte pasche usque ad dominicam, qua cantatur: ’Adaperiat', superpelliceis tam in divinis quam in claustro continue utantur; hiemali vero tempore, prout hactenus est observatum. Adicimus insuper, ut si quis fidelium de episcopatu nostro sive undecumque locum sepulture apud ecclesiam ipsam expetierit, nulla ecclesiastica secularisve persona id presumat aliquatenus inhibere. Item statuimus, quod sicut a longe retroactis temporibus observatum est, in die palmarum omnes utriusque civitatis tam nove quam veteris clerici et laici cum sollempni processione ad consecrationem palmarum ad ecclesiam cathedralem Brandeburgensem accedant, nec in aliqua ecclesia civitatis utriusque missa celebretur, quousque consecratio palmarum in ecclesia cathedrali honorifice compleatur, et quod in die ascensionis Domini et in festo apostolorum Petri et Pauli cum sollempni processione cleri et populi utriusque civitatis cathedralis ecclesia, que in honore beati Petri est fundata, sollempniter visitetur. Si quis autem in dictis processionibus observandis, impediendo aut non servando ipsas, contumax fuerit et rebellis, episcopus vel prepositus Brandeburgensis ipsum animadversione debita, videlicet si clericus fuerit plebanus, per penam suspensionis ab officio vel beneficio, si laicus, per sententiam excommunicationis corrigat et emendet. Monachos vero in episcopatu nostro degentes, ad quos cura animarum non spectat, confessiones audire, nisi eorum qui apud ipsos decubuerint, penitentes absolvere, penitentias iniungere, mortuos sepelire sine consensu ipsius archidiaconi et sacerdotum, quibus cura ani4 marum est commissa, omnimodis prohibemus. Prohibemus insuper, ut nulli fratrum vestrorum post factam in ipsa ecclesia professionem fas sit absque prepositi ipsius licentia de ipso loco discedere. Discedentem vero sine communi litterarum vestrarum cautione nullus audeat retinere. Reversus vero, sive de seculo sive de alio claustro redierit, omnium tunc in eadem ecclesia existentium fiat novissimus, nec in conventu so nec in capitulo consentiendi vel contradicendi sive etiam loquendi vocem habeat, nisi post dignam penitentiam peractam de benignitate et consensu totius capituli misericorditer fuerit restitutus. Statuimus insuper et sub pena excommunicationis prohibemus, ut nullus advocatus fratres ipsius ecclesie ad iudicium seculare trahere aut colonos infestare aut res eorum auferre sive exactiones in ipsos quacumque occasione. facere presumat. Set in quarumlibet executione causarum memorate ecclesie defensioni spe remunerationis eterne fideliter deserviat. Decernimus ergo, ut nulli omnino hominum liceat prefatam ecclesiam temere perturbare aut eius possessiones auferre vel ablatas retinere vel in ipsis violentiam exercere, minuere seu quibuslibet vexationibus fatigare, set omnia integra conserventur, eorum pro quorum gubernatione ac sustentatione concessa sunt usibus omnimodis profutura. Ut autem hec omnia inconvulsa perpetuis permaneant temporibus, auctoritate Dei omnipotentis et beatorum apostolorum Petri et Pauli, domini quoque pape Honorii ac nostra quam a Deo habemus, cuncta que huic pagine inscripta sunt, sub anathemate confirmamus, ipsam paginam sigilli nostri munimine roborantes, adhibitis idoneis testibus, quorum nomina sunt hec: Sigebodus Havelbergensis episcopus, Albertus marchio Brandeburgensis, Guncellinus quondam prepositus, Heinricus prior, Rodolfus cellerarius. Thomas custos, Baldewinus camerarius, Godescalcus, Gernotus, Walter magister hospitalis, canonici ipsius ecclesie; Iohannes de Grabov, Gerongus de Borch, Nicolaus de lesere, Rubertus de Gorceke, Alardus de Cidiz, Eustachius de Glineke, Amelricus de Plawe plebani; Fredericus de Hasle, Erwinus de Ieszant, Conradus de Stoltenhagen, Rodulfus Pincerna, Borchardus de Cohestede, Wernerus de Alstermunde laici. Dat. Iesere l, anno ab incarnatione Domini M°CCOXVII°, V Kal. Ianuar. 2 pontificatus nostri anno primo; regnante domino Frederico rege et Romanorum electo, Magdeburgensi vero ecclesie domino Alberto archiepiscopo feliciter presidente. It is just that those who are in the service of God should be free from the disturbance of men. Since you, sons, have been in the service of God in the aforementioned church of Brandenburg, as the apostolic see has learned, for a long time, you have been disturbed by the external troubles of men and the inner peace of the brothers has been lost, the Lord God of the fathers, who has given us the gift of the spirit of his son, has ordained us to be shepherds and to feed his flock, and therefore we, who have been appointed by the Lord to feed the flock of the Lord, have had mercy on your prayers and have resolved to provide for the tranquility of the brothers. regesto_originale: Gregorius IX papa [Iacobol praeposito et capitulo Brandeburgensi bona et iura tam a Sigefrido II episcopo et praedecessoribus eius quam a marchionibus et aliis ecclesiae corum collata confirmat, inserto tenore diplomatis a praefato Sigefrido II eidem ecclesiae concessi. 1233, Dec. 14.
apparato: Greg. IX Reg. Vol IV, 117-119; Lib. VII, 449. Potthast, Reg. 9344.
testo_esteso: .. preposito et capitulo Brandeburgensis ecclesie. Iustis petentium etc. usque: assensu, villas, allodia, possessiones, iura et alia bona, tam a venerabili fratre nostro .. Brandeburgensi episcopo et suis predecessoribus, prout in ipsius episcopi litteris plenius continetur, quam a nobilibus viris marchionibus Brandeburgensibus et aliis Christi fidelibus ecclesie vestre pia et provida liberalitate concessa, necnon libertates et immunitates vobis rationabiliter ab eisdem indultas, ac antiquas et rationabiles ecclesie predicte consuetudines et hactenus observatas, sicut ea omnia iuste ac pacifice possidetis, vobis et per vos eidem ecclesie auctoritate apostolica confirmamus etc. usque: communimus. Ad maiorem autem ecclesie prefate cautelam litterarum ipsarum tenorem de verbo ad verbum presentibus duximus inserendum. Qui talis est: In! nomine sancte et individue Trinitatis. Ego Sifridus secundus Dei gratia Brandeburgensis ecclesie episcopus. Ordinatione divina venerabiles et Deo digni predecessores nostri Wilmarus, Sifridus, Balderammus, Alexius, Nobertus", Baldewinus, Brandeburgenses episcopi, sanctam congregationem regularium canonicorum sub regula beati Augustini et institutione reverentissimi domini Norberti Magdeburgensis archiepiscopi in urbe Brandeburc in sedem episcopalem, quam pie memorie Otto imperator fundavit?, ad servitium Dei adunatam, tempore nostre mortalitatis per nos in via Dei dirigendam, nobis quasi hereditaria successione reliquerunt. Nos itaque eorum devotioni pro parvitate nostra Domino annuente subservientes, prefate congregationi omnimodum affectum nostrum inclinavimus, et ut interna Domino quiete vacent, exteriorem ab eis inquietudinem duximus amovendam. Inde est quod eorum iustis precibus pie annuentes, iura et consuetudines honestas nec non et bona, que eis predecessores nostri, eiusdem ecclesie episcopi, seu principes seculares seu quelibet honoratorum vel privatorum persone iusto iam donationis titulo contulerunt vel adhuc collature sunt, nos auctoritate Dei omnipotentis et beatorum apostolorum Petri et Pauli, in quorum honore eadem ecclesia constructa est, domini Honorii pape et nostra, quam a Deo habemus, confirmamus et presentis pagine munimine stabilimus. In primis siquidem statuentes, ut eadem ecclesia iuxta primam sui institutionem tamquam ecclesia cathedralis libera sit et perpetuis permaneat temporibus, nullaque seu secularis seu regularis ecclesia nichil omnino quacumque occasione iurisdictionis sibi in ipsa ecclesia usurpare presumat, set sicut eadem ecclesia tantum antecessoribus nostris, ita quoque nobis et successoribus nostris sit subiecta. Correctiones quoque discipline regularis et morum reformationes eorundem canonicorum, que vires sui prepositi excesserint, iuxta antiquam et hactenus observatam consuetudinem et Lateranensis statuta concilii per nos et successores nostros nullo penitus interiecto appellationis obstaculo corrigantur. Collaudamus ergo et confirmamus, ut dictus ordo canonicorum regularium, qui secundum Dei timorem et beati Augustini regulam in iamdicta ecclesia dinoseitur institutus, perpetuis ibidem temporibus inviolabiliter observetur. Possessiones vero et bona, que eadem ecclesia auctore Deo possidet, confirmamus eidem, in quibus hec propriis vocabulis duximus exprimenda: locum ipsum, in quo prefata ecclesia sita est, medietatem videlicet urbis Brandenburc, cum omnibus suis pertinentiis, aquis scilicet aquarumque decursibus, exitibus et reditibus; curam etiam animarum totius urbis Brandeburgensis, que eidem ratione sedis cathedralis a bone memorie Wibnar.a ipsius ecclesie episcopo est collata, ut ab ipsius successoribus usque ad nostra tempora est confirmata; ecclesiam quoque beati Bodeardib in forensi villa Pardwin cum dote sua, in qua primitus iidem canonici a pie memorie Wiggero Brandeburgensi episcopo fuerant instituti, a qua postmodum per sancte recordationis Wilinarume dicte ecclesie episcopum in urbem Brandeburgensem sunt transpositi, ipsam inquam ecclesiam sancti Godeardi cum tota parrochia ipsius ville et novo ponte toto et medietate antiqui pontis eiusdem parrochie adiacentibus nec non et tertiam partem decimarum ipsius ville tam frugum quam animalium et aliarum rerum, iuxta quod parrochiales ecclesie per nostram diocesim percipere consueverunt; ecclesiam etiam sancte Marie in monte, qui Harlugeberch dicitur, cum tertia parte decimarum ex adiacentibus vineis, et ecclesiam sancti Nicolai in Luckeberge cum dote sua et uno manso et tertia parte decimarum ipsius ville ad predictam parrochiam in Pardwin pertinentibus, et si que alie ecclesie infra eandem parrochiam fuerint in posterum edificate; sex quoque arearum fundos in ipsa villa Pardwin a fidelibus oblatos, hospitale etiam pauperum in iamdicta villa Pardwin iuxta pontem de Cracowe situm cum ortis et omnibus suis attinentiis, cultis et incultis; tres quoque areas cum ortis suis et pomariis in villa Cracowo; duas insuper lacunas, unam in superiori parte urbis Brandeburch et aliam iuxta hospitale sitas; centum etiam mansos in Zucha sitos, quos bone memorie Otto senior marchio Brandeburgensis pro animabus patris, matris et uxoris sue Iudethe marchionisse, eorum filiis Ottone et Henrico consentientibus, de patrimonio suo obtulit sepedicte ecclesie, cum omnibus pertinentiis suis, cultis et incultis, silvestribus et palustribus, aquis aquarumque decursibus, et quinque modios maioris mensure salis annuatim Brandeburch in thelonio accipiendos; villas quoque Garzeliz, Museliz, Bukowe, Bultiz, Kik et Gorne cum decimis et omnibus pertinentiis earum, cultis et incultis, aquis aquarumque decursibus, silvestribus, palustribus cunctisque utilitatibus, cum duobus lacubus inter Gorne et Siloe sitis; ecclesiam etiam in Verchiezere sitam in territorio Pritzerwe cum dote et areis suis et duobus mansis et tertia parte decimarum totius ville; villam insuper Mertzane d cum tota decima et omnibus pertinentiis suis, silvestribus, palustribus, cultis et incultis, cunctisque utilitatibus, et ecclesiam eiusdem ville cum dote sua et uno manso ad ecclesiam in Verchiezere pertinentem; villas quoque Mukzowe, Tremmene et Thure cum decimis et omnibus appenditiis earum, cultis et incultis, silvestribus et palustribus; ecclesiam etiam in Thure cum dote sua et tertia parte decimarum de villis ad eam pertinentibus; Itzin, Scadebauresdorp, et totam decimam villarum Crelin et Bauresdorp, tam frugum quam animalium; ecclesiam in Goliz cum dote sua et duobus mansis et tertia parte decimarum ipsius ville, et tertiam partem decimarum ville Wachowe cum duobus mansis pertinentibus ad ecclesiam in Goliz; ecclesiam etiam in Niebede cum dote sua et duobus mansis et tertia parte decimarum ipsius ville, et ecclesiam in Swanebeke cum dote sua et tertia parte decimarum eiusdem pertinentem ad ecclesiam in Niebleke; ecclesiam quoque in Zachowe cum dote sua et duobus mansis et tota decima ex agris eidem ville adiacentibus, necnon et decimam carnium totam, et tertiam partem decimarum de villis ad ipsam ecclesiam pertinentibus, videlicet Lodiz, Parne et Werdere; molendinum quoque in Clinke cum area sua, aquis quoque et aquarum decursibus, villam insuper Damme dictam a bone memorie Rodolfo de Iericho marchioni Ottoni resignatam et ab eo cum omnibus ad ipsam pertinentibus, cultis et incultis, silvestribus, palustribus dicte ecclesie Brandeburgensi oblatam, et decimas omnes eiusdem ville a pie memorie Wilmaro ipsius ecclesie episcopo in usus eorundem fratrum concessas; totam insuper villam Pluzin in Zucha sitam cum ecclesia ipsius et omnibus decimis et omnibus appenditiis, cultis et incultis, palustribus et campestribus; villam quoque Sconlo dictam, in qua sunt triginta mansi, cum decimis et omnibus appenditiis suis, cultis et incultis, campestribus et palustribus; ecclesiam quoque de Marcowe cum dote sua et duobus mansis et tertia parte decimarum eiusdem ville et ville Markede; ecclesiam quoque in Cotsin cum dote sua, scilicet cum duobus mansis in agris ville Clebeloe ei designatis et ad eandem ecclesiam in consecratione dotis nomine confirmatis, et tribus areis in eadem villa Cotsin, quas sacerdos Teodericus de manibus laicorum sub testimonio villanorum redimens in unam redegit; capellam etiam in Clebeloc, eidem matrici ecclesie in Cotsin attinentem, cum dote sua et tertia parte decimarum eiusdem ville; tertiam quoque partem decimarum dicte ecclesie Cotsin et villarum ad eam pertinentium, videlicet Stolp et Porets et alterius Sclavice ville Poréts; ecclesiam quoque in Oyne cum filia sua, videlicet ecclesia in Golisdorp, cum areis et mansis et tertia parte decimarum earundem villarum et villarum Modelendorp et Canisdorp a predecessoribus nostris bone memorie Norberto et Baldewino episcopis dicte ecclesie oblatam; vineam etiam eorundem canonicorum in monte Arlungorum versus orientem in ipsius montis latere iacentem. Confirmamus insuper dilecto filio Alverico dicte ecclesie preposito eiusque successoribus curam animarum de ecclesiis, que ad usus dictorum canonicorum impresentiarum pertinent aut in posterum pertinebunt, concedentes ut earundem ecclesiarum fructus, prout expedire viderint, in usus proprios convertant. Liceat quoque ipsis in eisdem ecclesiis, iuxta quod ab antecessoribus nostris est concessum, de fratribus suis viros idoneos instituere plebanos, qui curam in ipsis gerant animarum. Predecessorum quoque nostrorum vestigiis inherentes, rationabiles et honestas consuetudines et iura dicte Brandeburgensis ecclesie nichilominus duximus confirmandas. But because of the long journey and the dangers of war, and because many kingdoms are between you and us, I have not seen it fit to send a man of noble birth to you, lest my man should be harmed by evil and wicked people in the middle, and I should lose them. For this reason, from the third year of indiction until the present seventh year of indiction, I have sent six persons dressed as monks, who had a vow and who came from those parts to visit the tombs of St. Peter and St. James, to your holiness, that they might not be recognized and hindered by our enemies. But two of them returned, and the other four did not return, and I do not know why. And I believe that the two who returned could not tell your holiness of the messages I sent to you, nor did they bring back letters to me for my certainty. Therefore, I have considered sending a man of noble birth to you, who could come to you, and I have sent him to the emperor of the Germans, Frederick, to be associated with him, that he may send him to you. I have therefore sent my faithful man, John of Gabra, to your holiness, with these letters and a small business, which would be an occasion for a letter of faith. But first, I sent him to the emperor and asked him to direct him to your holiness, and I hope that he will not be neglectful. And since I sent him to the emperor, I did not write in the letters anything but the will of my heart and my mandates to John of Gabra, that he may speak to your holiness with his own voice, and that what he will say to you may be received as if it were from my mouth. And he has also other letters from us, written in Syriac, sealed with a golden bull. Notifico sanctitati tue, quod iam dudum disposueram unum magnatem vassallum meum ad vestram mittere sanctitatem ad exponendum vobis affectionem nostram, quam erga vestram gerimus sanctitatem, et ad tractandum inter ambos amicitiam et pacem et ad disperdendum et destruendum inimicum; sed propter longam viam guerrarumque discrimina, et quia non pauca regna adiacent inter vos et nos, non vidimus esse tutum aliquem magnatem hominem destinare, ne a malis et invidis hominibus, qui sunt in medio, vassalli mei malum paterentur, et amitterem eosdem homines meos. Ac propter hoc ab anno tertie indictionis usque ad presentem diem instantis septime indictionis usque ad sex personas sub habitu monachali, tanquam humiles homines qui votum habent et accedunt de partibus istis adorandum limina Sancti Petri et Sancti Iacobi, ad vestram sanctitatem direxi, ne forte cognoscerentur et ab inimicis impedirentur. De ipsis autem duo reversi sunt, reliqui vero quatuor quare non fuere reversi nescio, et sieut reor, nec ipsi duo monachi, qui fuerunt reversi, potuerunt exponere sanctitati vestre nuntiationes meas, quas sanctitati vestre mittebam, nec etiam litteras reportaverunt mihi ad certitudinem. Quamobrem necessarium duxi unum magnum hominem meum fidelem mittere ad exponendum tibi voluntatem meam, meditansque in memetipso atque considerans aliud non inveni ingenium, ut posset homo meus pervenire ad vos, nisi istum hominem meum, quem ad imperatorem Theutonicorum Fridericum transmitto, ut ipse, associato homine meo homini suo, ipsum ad vestram sanctitatem transmittat. Nunc itaque misis fidelissimum et propriumb soldanice potestatis mee, hominem Christianum, nomine Iohannem de Gabra, ad sanctitatem vestram cum litteris meis et quodam parvo negotio, quod esset occasio litterarum ad fidem; sed prius quidem misi eum ad imperatorem et rogavi eundem, ut cum ordinatione sua ipsum ad vestram dirigat sanctitatem, et spero quod ipse non erit negligens; et pro eo quod ipsum ad imperatorem direxi, nullam causam vel nullum negotium in litteris annotavi, sed totam voluntatem meam et mandata mea eidem fideli meo Iohanni Gabra commisi, ut ipse viva voce sanctitati tue loquatur, et quidquid ipse vobis locutus fuerit, tanquam ab ore meo recipiatur a sanctitate vestra; ac preter litteras istas habet etiam alias litteras a nobis Syro sermone sub bulla similiter aurea sigillatas. Perlectis autem litteris et auditis ab eodem, quamcumque 2 voluntatem habuerit vestra sanctitas, mittat nuntium suum ad implendam voluntatem utriusque partis. Scriptum mense Maï indict. VII. II. Nuntiationes Iohannis Gabra, nuntii soldani Iconii. Ego Iohannes Gabra, servus et nuntius domini mei soldani Iconii, adoro et 30 osculor vestigia sanctorum pedum sanctitatis tue, et notifico atque expono sanctitati tue ex parte domini mei ea, que mihi precepit vobis oretenus exponenda. In primis vult idem dominus meus, ut habeat sanctitatem vestram amicam, sicut habet Theutonicorum dominum Fredericum cum cautione iuramenti, et ut mittas nuntium tuum ad eundem dominum meum, ut iuret idem dominus meus. Et si hoc factum fuerit inter 35 utrosque, paratus est idem dominus meus iuvare vos et pugnare vobiscum ad recuperandum Ierusalem et omnes terras, quas habuerunt Christiani in tempore Saladini; et quando volueris mittere ad eum nuntium tuum, paratus est idem dominus meus adimplere predicta. Peto etiam ego predictus Iohannes, ut quando nuntium vestrum miseris ad dominum meum, predictas nuntiationes meas deferat in scriptis secum ad 40 dominum meum ad maiorem cautelam et certitudinem. III. Nobili et egregio principi soldano Iconii viam agnoscere veritatis. Dilectum filium Iohannem Gabram, Christianum, virum sapientem, providum et discretum, nuntium tuum, et litteras, quas nobis per ipsum dirigere curavisti, letanter recepimus et benigne, et tam earuma continentiam quam ea, que idem ex parte tua nobis exponere voluit, intelleximus diligenter. Sane devotionem, quam ad nos et ad apostolicam sedem habere dignosceris, dignis in Domino laudibus commendantes, nobilitati tue significatione presentium intimamus, quod discretos nuntios, quam cito poterimus, ad magnitudinis tue presentiam auctore Domino dirigemus, per quos super iis, que significasti nobis, prudentie tue curabimus plenius respondere. Dat. Perusii, XIII Kalend. Aprilis, pontificatus nostri anno VIII. IV. Nobili et egregio principi soldano Yconii viam veritatis agnoscere. Dilectum filium Iohannem Gabram, Christianum, virum sapientem, providum et discretum, nuntium tuum, quem ad nos karissimus in Christo filius noster Fridericus etc. transmisit, ad ipsius imperatoris duximus presentiam remittendum, imperialem excellentiam rogantes attentius et hortantes, ut eo ad magnitudinem tuam regredi cupiente, de suo reditu iuxta imperatorie celsitudinis decentiam provideret. Dat. Perusii. XIII Kal. Aprilis, pontificatus nostri anno octavo.

regesto_sintetico: English translation: To the archbishops and bishops, abbots and other prelates of churches established in Lombardy, the March of Tervis, and Romania. We wish that the days would come and the shadows would incline, and the cloud of crimes would be removed from the midst of the Church of Canterbury: and the whirlwind's cloud, which has hitherto covered almost all your territories, that the one to whom the winds and the sea obey, who turns the storm into calm, and who, according to the secret counsel of his mercy, knows how to heal the wounds of the afflicted, would bring serenity. How great a tribulation has pressed and is pressing the parts, how great a persecution has led and is leading the Christian people, how much the parts have been worn down by wars and how much the monasteries and churches have been shaken by various hardships, can hardly be recounted. It has been granted to us to hear it with a bitter heart, and to you, as the Lord has disposed, to experience. And although the Roman Church, the pious mother who cannot forget her children, has striven for the reform of peace with great effort, writing letters and sending messengers to induce brothers of ours to be joined, not once but several times, and not to one but to several, in order to be freed from their hardships and to follow the pure way, it has not yet been possible to apply a suitable remedy, since the procurer of the schism has been at work. Since therefore the vicar of the king of the pacific, who was willing to reconcile the servant to the Lord, has delivered himself to death, we gladly think about the consolations of peace to those who are near and to those who are far, and we consider that we cannot any longer hide the perils of the souls, the damage of goods, the desolation of churches, the ruin of monasteries, and the scattering of the Christian people without harm to our conscience and without the loss of provisions. Moreover, since the help of the Holy Land, to which the Christian people aspires, is impeded by this fact, and the little foxes that destroy the vineyard of the Lord and the venomous snake that grows in malice are strengthened, we desire that the land, which has long languished and is languishing, may enjoy the desired peace, and that the mountains may bring forth the sweetness and the hills the joy, so that the Church may bring forth the fruits of good things, as the heavens pour down the rain. Therefore we have deputed our venerable brother, the patriarch of Antioch, a man indeed provident and learned, whom we have greatly accepted for his devotion and for the merits of his brothers, with full power of legation to the parts, in order that he may pull down and destroy what he knows should be destroyed, build and plant what he knows should be built and planted. We command you, therefore, that you receive the said patriarch, as the legate of the apostolic see and a great person in the Church of God, and that you treat him with joy and honor, and that you attend to and follow his wholesome counsels and commands with humility and devotion, so that you may observe inviolably what he shall have established for the reform of peace and the negotiation of faith, for the conservation of ecclesiastical liberty, for the correction of morals, and for the salvation of souls. Otherwise, we shall consider the sentence which he shall have pronounced against the rebels as valid, and we shall cause it to be firmly observed. Given at Perugia, on the 11th kalends of June, in the ninth year. In the same way to the noble men, marquises, counts, barons, magistrates, cities, and all the inhabitants of Lombardy, the March of Tervis, and Romania. In the same way to the duke of the Venetians. In the same way to the patriarch of Grado and his suffragans.
