Exeamus ad Iesum, secundum apostolum, extra castra, improperium eius portantes, Hebr. 13,13. ut videlicet ipsius opprobrium proprium reputemus, quasi nobis ipsis illatas sibi iniurias existimantes, ut sicut ipse defectus nostros nascendo sustinuit et dolores moriendo portavit, dum nascendo minoratus est paulo minus ab angelisa, ac se ipsum Philip. 2,7. exinanivit formam servi accipiens, in similitudinemb hominum factus et habitu inventus ut homo ac moriendo, captus, tractus, vinctus, cesus, illusus alapis, crucifixus, mortuus, lanceatus extitit et sepultus, sic, quamquam non sit similitudo creature ad creatorem, ut tamen aliquid saltem retribuamus ei pro omnibus que retribuit ipse nobis, iniuria nos tangat ipsius, ut subveniamus pauperi Iesu Christo ad relevandas contumelias, Matth. 27440. quibus ei a fidei nostre hostibus exprobratur, insultantibus ipsis et dicentibus: “Si filius Dei es, salvum facias temetipsum; si quid potes, libera terram nativitatis tue de manibus nostris, et crucis cultoribus restituas crucem tuam'. Certe ignominia est populo Christiano, quod ille rex regum, qui fecit omnia, de propria sede pulsus pro Psal. 104,11. nostris facinoribus terram, que hereditatis sue funiculus est, amisit, in qua corporaliter Baruch 3,38. visus est cum hominibus conversatus et in qua universa redemptionis nostre sacramenta patravit. O, quam anxie clamaret apostolus hodie, si nunc in mundo maneret: "Exeamus ad Iesum extra castra, improperium eius portantes', forte diceret: “Exeamus Gen. 12,1. exemplo Abrahe de terra, domibus et cognatione nostra corporali et mystica, ut eamus in terram illam olim inclytam et Christi sanguine consecratam, ut expulsis exinde cum Dei adiutorio Amorrheis, cum luda Machabeo montem Sion ascendamus mundare sancta et renovare, coronis ornantes aureis templum Domini dei nostri'. Clamat Matth. 1624. etiam ipse Christus: “Qui vult’, inquit, “venire post me, abneget semetipsum et tollat crucem suam et sequatur me’, quasi dicat: “Bellum instat, aciem castrorum dispono; ergo qui meus est, me sequatur. Qui enim vult venire mecum ad gloriam, sequatur me ad pugnam, quia qui vult regnare, oportet compati; quanquam non sint condigne passiones huius temporis ad futuram gloriam, quam in nobis credimus revelandam. Clamat nichilominus illa miserabilis Ierusalem mater nostra, que merito peccatorum nostrorum bibit de manu Domini calicem ire eius, suas nobis exponens angustias et in sui doloris remedium affectus a nobis expectans filiales, si forte tristemur cum ipsa et doleamus, si eam diligimus, vicem eius. Quis enim est, qui non tam validis clamoribus excitatus ad vindicandas Christi sui tam atroces iniurias se accingat? Nunquid non rei proditionis apud filium Dei erimus, si ad eruendam terram de manibus impiorum, ad eum ex patris eterna Psal. 28. donatione, qui gentes in hereditatem et in possessionem terre terminos sibi dedit, ac matris de regali prosapia descendentis successoria hereditate pertinentem, non totis viribus laboremus? Non est quidem novum, quod terra illa iudicio divino percutitur, sed nec est insolitum, ut flagellata et castigata sanetur; nam poterat eam Dominus sola voluntate servare, sed forsitan voluit experiri et in notitiam ducere aliorum, si quis tangeretur eius iniuria et ad ipsam ulciscendam se aliquis prepararet. Licet autem ad recuperationem ipsius terre multum laboraverit hactenus populus Christianus, licet multi principes orthodoxi assumpto crucis signaculo, ut hereditatem Domini de manibus eruerent iniquorum, ad partes transfretaverint transmarinas, licet quam plures, quos in hostes zelus divine legis armaverat, in manibus traditi persequentium adhuc forsitan ferreis detineantur compedibus et squallore carPsal. 85,7. ceris macerentur, licet non pauci, faciente cum eis Domino signum in bonum, calicem gustaverint passionis et martyrio fuerint coronati: nondum tamen exigentibus culpis populi Christiani tante voluit Dominus miserie misereri, illo dante forsan occasionem vel causam, quod etsi ad tempus circa hoc ferbuerit devotio Christiana, in tempore tamen tepuit fervor eius, et sic non continuatis presidiis defectum passa est graviter causa Christi. Cum igitur treuge cum Sarracenis inite modico sint tempore durature, ne si, quod absit, invenitur Christiana professio imparata, verendum sit, quod non solum difficilis terre recuperatio iam amisse, verum etiam desperabilis retentio sit retente: cupientes acies Dominicas instaurare ac per continuata presidia Christi negotio provideri, de fratrum nostrorum consilio militiam Christianam in partibus transmarinis, que iugiter contra hostes fidei prelium Domini prelietur, ad minus usque ad decem annos providimus instruendam, de fidelium elemosinis subsidium continuum habituram. Ut autem quod intendimus melius et efficacius impleatur, exemplo apostoli, qui collectas faciebat in gentibus, ut mitteret illas fratribus egentibus in Ierusalem, sic super hoc duximus providendum, ut quilibet, qui Christiana professione censetur, tam masculus quam femina, tam clerieus quam laicus, et tam subditus quam prelatus, conferat qualibet septimana saltem unum denarium in hoc opus, per manus eorum, qui ad hoc electi fuerint, in subsidium eiusdem militie convertendum; iis dumtaxat exceptis, qui suscepto crucis charactere sunt illuc personaliter profecturia. Ad quod fideliter exequendum in qualibet civitate vel castro, villa vel vico assumantur duo, unus videlicet clericus per episcopum et alter laicus per dominum vel rectorem terre seu locorum communia, fideles et idonei, timentes Deum, qui recipiant sic oblata; et ne forte illum cuius est negotium contingat decipi vel fraudari, in fine cuiuslibet mensis fiat per eosdem clericum et laicum in publico presentibus bonis viris et Deum timentibus ratio de receptis, ut sciatur quid et quantum in opus huiusmodi sit collatum, adhibito illo cautele studio ut de hiis nichil omnino depereat set totum ad opus dicte militie integre conservetur, ita ut, si de loco illo cruce signati aliqui ad partes transfretaverint supradictas, illis prius et potius in transmarinis partibus de ipsa debeant. pecunia stipendia provideri; et in fine cuiuslibet anni coram loci episcopo fiat exinde ratio generalis, ut per locorum episcopos receptorum quantitas Romano pontifici exponatur, que consignata fideliter et deposita per illos, qui ad hoc deputati fuerint, illuc plenarie transmittatur. Confidimus autem in Domino et in potentia virtutis eius speramus, quod si usque ad premissum tempus huiusmodi presidium indeficiens instauretur, reedificabuntur civitates et oppida, et in eis habitatoribus constitutis terra manuteneri poterit auctore Domino et defendi. Ideoque fraternitatem vestram rogamus, monemus et hortamur in Domino, per apostolica vobis scripta districte precipiendo mandantes, quatinus commissos vobis populos moneatis attentius et efficaciter inducatis, in remissionem eis peccaminum iniungentes ac obsecrantes per Patrem et Filium et Spiritum sanctum et per aspersionem sanguinis lesu Christi, ut sicut convenit attendentes qualiter transeunt universa, prout unusquisque destinabit in corde suo, quod 2. Cor. 957. de gratia petimus non ex tristitia aut ex necessitate Domino exolvendo, datores ylares se ostendant. Porro, quamvis id modicum pro unigenito Dei filio a singulis de gratia requiramus, necessitatem tamen alicui non imponimus, quin possit in gazophylacium Domini maiora reponere, set quanto cuiquam Dominus contulit ampliora, tanto ei retributionis equitate pensata debet quilibet maioris devotionis insignia exhibere. Nec dubitent dare illi terrena et pauca brevique tempore duratura, qui contulit universa, que sive volentes sive nolentes nesciunt, quibus sint heredibus relicturi, pro quibus illa bona dantibus sunt promissa, que nec oculus vidit nec auris audivit 1. Cor. 299. nec in cor hominis ascenderunt. Nos enim de omnipotentis Dei misericordia et beatorum Petri et Pauli apostolorum eius auctoritate confisi, omnibus vere penitentibus et confessis, qui elemosinam in hoc opus tam pium et laudabile, prout est dictum superius, duxerint conferendam, duos annos annis singulis de iniuncta sibi penitentia misericorditer relaxamus. Illis autem qui non solum hoc set maiora pro subsidio predicte militie Domino inspirante contulerint, iuxta quantitatem subsidii et devotionis affectum ampliorem concedimus veniam peccatorum. Dat. Perusii, IV Kal. Iulii, anno nono. In eundem modum scriptum est universis archiepiscopis et eorum suffraganeis.

We are deeply troubled by this, and can hardly find the words to express or write it down. We have learned that the wickedness of the wicked has increased to such an extent that they know that justice is the foundation of peace, but they commit injustices and destroy peace, and do not distinguish between the sacred and the profane, and they rob and plunder both ecclesiastical and secular goods; unless they are opposed, their pride will always grow and will bring irreparable damage to the entire province. We wish to provide a remedy to this pestilence, so we strongly command you by apostolic letters, under penalty of the apostolic ban, to take arms publicly to suppress this pestilence, to expel and exclude from your territories those who, in your province, are committing these outrages, to fight against those who are robbing, plundering and killing, and to punish them so severely that they will be deterred from sin. If anyone buys stolen goods or plunder, he shall be obliged to return them absolutely without any compensation, and the buyer shall have a lawsuit against the seller, with the prohibition of appeal. regesto_originale: Gregorius IX papa Ffridericol Romanorum imperatori scribit se sententiam interdicti, quam [Theodericus) archiepiscopus Ravennas in cives Acconenses promulgaverit, relaxasse. Rogat, ut cum nuntii Acconensium ordinationi ecclesiae se committere velint, sibi de iis, quae in cedula quam mittat contineantur, voluntatis suae beneplacitum insinuet. — Sequitur cedula, in qua papa exponit, quibus conditionibus pax in Terra Sancta reformanda sit. 1235, Sept. 22.

regesto_sintetico: Translation in English: To Louis, illustrious king of France. You, who governs the kingdom of eternal dominion, who has elevated the church on the foundation of the eternal faith, who, stirring kings of the earth to obedience with his advice and princes of the world to devotion with many examples, have it that the church is honored by God, since he, the immortal, offered his form of a servant to the cross and the torment of death did not fear to undergo for her, exalting him who offers his service to her and perpetuating his kingdom, who favors you in your vows, which you offer to God the Father. Moreover, you can gather from your ancestors and especially from the illustrious memory of Charles the Great that, diligently attending the way in which the aforesaid Charles, obeying the Roman pontiff, vicar of Jesus Christ and successor of blessed Peter, to whom the Lord has entrusted the laws of earthly and heavenly kingdoms, offered himself to many labors and anguishes for the defense of the church, how great a report of honor, praise and glory he obtained from it. But perhaps it has not reached your knowledge that he, having often gathered a large army of warriors against her persecutors, triumphed magnificently over them; and that, when the emperor of Constantinople neglected to defend the liberty of the church, the church, obtaining the power of spiritual and material sword from God, as she exerts and is exerted, entrusted the empire to Charles, who not only suppressed the violators of the liberty of the church but also the disturbers of the goods of the church, continuing the grace that Zaccharias pope had granted to your father Philip, who had exalted him to the throne of the kingdom of the Franks. For this reason, Charles decreed that all those who were subject to the jurisdiction of the church should observe the statute established by Theodosius the emperor for the liberty of the church, namely that whoever had a case should be directed to the judgment of the bishop of the church, even if one party refused, and that all cases, which were treated in the court of the prefect and also in the civil court, should be terminated by the sentence of the bishops, which should have the firmness of perpetuity, and that the case, which was decided by their judgment, should not be reviewed by anyone. From which you can gather by manifest reason that it is not right and not decent that the honor of the church, which is known to be endowed with a grand privilege of liberty, should be diminished in those immunities, which are known to be less than the aforesaid. But the rest of his successors, your ancestors, considering that the exaltation of the churches was an example similar to their own, were considered defenders of the Christian faith, the mother, and, attending that they could not repay God, who exalted them to the glory of the kingdom, with anything similar, they decorated the churches with many riches, they donated them with many liberties, or rather they preserved them in the liberty, which they had acquired, considering it unworthy that the place, where the divine name is exalted, where Christ is immolated for the redemption of our crimes on the altar, should be subjected to the burdens of servitude, since it is worthy of honor above the understanding of man. If therefore the vineyard preserves its origin and the sap vivifies the branches and the root, it is hardly believed that the offspring, which receives honor from its origin, should not produce similar virtues. But rather it is hoped that the grace of goodness, which was innate in them, will not allow you to act in such a way that you may derogate from the liberty and honor of the Roman church and its members, since the taste of the fountains is not denied to those who flow from it. But behold, we have heard and we lament that you, dear son, and the barons of the kingdom, using the advice of evil men, are trying to reduce the church, which has regenerated you from the womb of sanctification and offers you to God the Father as an immaculate bride, to servitude, as if you did not want to be called freely sons but servants, or rather as if you wanted to make the church of God a servant, which has liberated you from perpetual servitude. But you have decreed that men of your kingdom should not be forced to respond in ecclesiastical court, not even if they are excommunicated by a bishop, and that, if a bishop pronounces an excommunication, it should be relaxed by the prince, and that, what is worse, the archbishops, bishops and other ecclesiastical persons and their men should be forced to obey the judgment of your court, although the church of Gaul had used this liberty in the kingdom of France from ancient times. Consider, dear son, consider how those who advise you in this way care about your advantage and your honor, who, wishing to fish in troubled waters, begin to put a stain on your glory, so that from this they may be able to report their own advantages, not yours. Consider how indecent it may be for you to allow the oppression of the churches to be the primitiae of your kingdom, since the advice of your enemies is leading you to this. What else? It is fitting that, frequently revolving the secrets of your heart, you understand that not only your predecessors, from whom you have received honor, and who have obtained a great title of praise and honor from the church, but also many long ago, have tried to honor the church with all their strength, and that Valentinian the emperor said to the suffragans of Milan: “You should consider as your superior the bishop, who sits in the papal throne, and you should submit your heads to him, and, as men who sin, you should seek the remedies of the church, and you should not hear those who try to lead the church to affliction with evil suggestions. Hence, we have written to the king to ask him to honor the church and to correct the wrongs done to her, and to protect the persons of the church from the harm that they suffer. REGESTO:Gregorius IX, papa, Ludovico Francorum rege, qui ecclesiam Gallicanam in pristino statu et honore conservare faciat, ut homines eius non teneantur in foro ecclesiastico respondere, si iudex ecclesiasticus eis excommunicationis sententiam tulerit, et quod ecclesiarum Senonensi et aliis dicantur illata damna et iniuriae absque diminutione satisfieri faciat. regesto_sintetico: Translation to English: To the patriarchs of Aquileia and Grado, the archbishops of Milan, Ravenna, and Genoa, and the bishops of Pavia, Piacenza, and Ferrara, and the abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, archpriests, prepositors, and other ecclesiastical prelates established in their cities and dioceses. We know not how to profit from the children of the Father, but the Father's love always brings forth increase and never ceases to care for their progress. Thus, now as from ancient times, if only there were a comparison between the creator and the creature, and between the work and the worker, who created them and redeemed them with his precious blood, the Lord, who is rich in mercy, always follows them with abundant blessings, protecting them from dangers and procuring for them remedies of salvation, so that they may be refreshed in the present with the comfort of peace and in the future be satiated with the sweetness of eternal felicity. For the same Lord, who while still on earth was established for the salvation of the human race, innumerable ways of mercy multiplied for the recreation of the multitude of people. He provided for the ineffable providence of God, so that since the prince of darkness, who was to trouble the reborn fountain of baptism, was to be tempted by many thorns, he would leave behind a vicar on earth and one endowed with singular power and a multitude of remedies, through whom the peace of the apostolic see would be brought to the world and the possibility of attaining the heavenly country would be fully opened. Now, since he sits at the right hand of majesty, he has given them, who, by the disposition of God, are deputed to carry out the service of the excellent bride of the church, namely, the holy mother church, to preach the doctrine of virtues to all faithful, to bring them peace, and to promote the desire of attaining the rewards of the heavens. Hence, since the provinces of Lombardy, Marquisate of Tervis, and Romagnolo have been in a state of discord, which has caused more troubles than should be described, we, as we trust in the inspiration of the spirit who has given to the saints the power to direct the world to the glory of salvation, have decided to send one of the most worthy members of the church, namely, our venerable brother bishop of Prenestino, apostolic legate, who has chosen to renounce the treasures of the world and the things of the flesh, and has not ceased to be considered worthy of the love of God and of the people. We have given him the full power of legation, hoping that, as he is considered more worthy to be loved by the one who is more generous in granting graces to those who live a virtuous life, he may more easily and happily accomplish the works of salvation and of grace. We therefore ask and exhort you, through Christ our Lord, by apostolic letters, to provide that the aforesaid bishop, whom we receive in our person and wish to be treated with filial reverence, may be received as a bringer of peace, and that you may do everything in your power to provide for him with all the honor you know and can, and that you may, with the same solicitude, procure for him that he may have the power to promote the things that bring honor to God and the church and the liberty of the church, as well as the reform of the states and, in particular, of the aforesaid provinces, and that he may be able to abolish the stains of heresy and to promote the business of the Holy Land, which we have entrusted to him in a special way, as we consider him to be bound to us by a greater obligation. Nam si te ad id imperii reformatio invitavit, nos causa imperii, cuius deformatio in dispendium ecclesie Romane redundat, ecclesiarum utilitas, que longum sub bellorum fluctibus discidium patitur, et animarum periculum, pro quibus possessori celi et terre ad ratiocinium obligamur, ad procuranda bona concordie debuerunt fortius excitasse. Unde nichil de tuo iure usurpasse, de tuo nichil, licet contrarium asseras, occupasse officio credimur, si nos, de quorum consilio te ad id in principio, medio et fine procedere, sicut pluries promisisti?, decuerat, prompti nostrum summo creditori exolvere debitum invenimur. Quare premissa more artificis, cuius considerationi se primitus offerunt que ultimo in operatione concurrunt, diligentius attendentes, illum, ut per eum nostrum impleremus ministerium, elegimus in hac parte ministrum, qui eo tibi et quibuscumque discordantibus minori posset haberi ratione suspectus, quo eius mens terrenis desideriis absoluta suis actibus fermenti minus ingereret odii vel amoris, qui se ipsum et sua relinquens in divini amoris altitudinem evolasset. Quis illius sinceritati rugam suspicionis obicere, quis illius puritatem nevo duplicitatis opposito poterit obfuscare, quem suscepta professionis beate religio carni et mundo abstulit, quem Deo fructus laudabilium operum et vite sanctitas commendavit? Nec enim locus originis recte contra eum in suspicionis argumentum inducitur!, cum non bonitas hominis deformetur a loco, set potius loci malitia per hominem reformetur. Probat hoc, quod nec pietati Christi quicquam mundus subtraxit impius, nec celum fecit sanctum demonem nec hominem paradisus. Genus etiam ad tuam intentionem non sufficere, immo nec proficere creditur, quia frustra in illo parentele vitia condempnantur, qui per conversationis sancte munditiam a patria et parentibus, quasi in virum mutatus alium, factus est penitus peregrinus. Quid plura? Frustra quid ad probationem alicuius inducitur, quod illud nec frequenter nec inseparabiliter comitatur. Suffragatur autem ad hoc testimonium dilecti filii.. magistri hospitalis sancte Marie Teutonicorum?, et ei, quoda alia vice ipsum cum dilecto filio nostro Ottone Sancti Nicolai in Carcere Tulliano diacono cardinali transmissum 3 tibi suspectum fuisse asseris, refragatur, cum ipsum nichil fecisse, unde celsitudini imperiali suspectus merito deberet haberi, coram nobis publica voce dixerit et eum circa observationem iustitie plurimum commendarit. Erubescere igitur poterit novus logyeus de nobis mali alicuius initium vel participium paralogismo concludere, cuius falsitatem etiam imperiti de longe speculantes possunt luce clarius improbare, cum publice bonum et manifesta boni species fuerit, quod legatus ad reformandam pacem inter te ac Lombardos a nobis destinatus accessit, cui nichil posseb credimus imputari, si eo presente sedata sint intestina bella Placentie, si alique civitates Lombardie, cladibus preliorum oppresse, ad pacis fuerint dulcedinem invitate. Quinimmo tibi ad infamiam reputatur, quod, ecclesia suoc prefato mediante legato, pacem imperii dedigneris vel non patiaris potius reformari. Set est fortasse qui dicat, quod dum contra fas et licitum episcopum prefatum tuis non habes votis omnino propitium, eum imperialibus extimes desideriis inimicum. et quo equalius eundem ad quodlibet oppositorum extremum, ut utraque unum efficiat, declinare perspexeris, eo fortius ipsum celsitudinis tue profectibus contrarium suspiceris. De quo, si placot, obtrectationis cossent obloquia, cuiuslibet prudentis et boni principis moribus inimica, qui sic ius suum discrete prosequitur, quod in nullius, presertim timentis Deum et episcopi, detractionem armatur. Verum ne aliqua de sede apostolica vere vel apparenter excellentie tue querela consurgat, tibi contra predictum legatum, quem d nondum probatio seu confessio obiecti criminis et ignoti convincit, experiri volenti sumus iustitiam exhibere parati. Ceterum, ne super imperialis celsitudinis de cohercenda, ut tuis verbis utamur, contumacia Lombardorum petitionee responsionem videamur per oblivionem vel negligentiam distulisse, dictus magister tibi satisfacere potuit, de cuius consilio dilectum filium G. 4 subdiaconum et capellanum nostrum ad tractandum de pace duximus destinandum. Quare responsio tibi grata non poterat fieri, per quem tractatum concordie contingebat penitus impediri. Nec etiam nobis de obiecta eis contumacia constitit, ad quos pro facto imperii mandatum apostolicum, cui superba cervice restiterint, nullatenus emanavit; quinimmo compromissum in manus nostras venerabili fratre nostro.. patriarcha Antiocheno? procurante teque petente firmantes, etsi infra tempus nunciis tuis pro tua voluntate prefixum ad nostram presentiam venire nequiverint, maculam tamen erga te, si dici potest, commisse contumacie per sequentis obedientiam compromiss a se videntur penitus abstersisse!. Igitur si nostre te faceresa doctrine discipulumb, si apostolici processus circa honorem tuum sepe sepius habiti imitareris exemplum, iusta monita nostra super commissis in regno corrigendis excessibus, pluries ab annis preteritis replicata et toties passa repulsionis iniuriam, ad debitum exauditionis admitteres, iniusta quoque, que nunquam tibi credimus ex certa scientia direxisse, procul ab imperialis limine concessionis arceres. Set ecce super facto ecclesiarum regni, quod tibi in litteris nostris primo directis? sub genere indefinite proponitur, quod ad hoc non tenearis quasi dubia respondere, a te reali responsione preterita vocali commentario incongrue respondetur 3, tum quia frustra requiritur, ut singularia speciei vel specialia fidem faciant generi, cum genus et species manifestam ex se prebent notitiam veritati, et cum individuorum scientia quasi ex infinitate confunditur, ad doctrinam universalium supervacue singularia colliguntur; tum quia que in primis litteris sub indefinita, in se tamen aliorum definita notitia fuere proposita, ex superabundanti in litteris nostris ad te secundo currentibus t per multa fuerunt particularia declarata, sicut in epistola tua responsiva? conicitur, que in se ipsa quibusdam particularibus verbaliter respondendo, quod in premissis falsum implicet, improbatur; cuius pollicitis de satisfactione prestanda quibusdam ecclesiis et personis, sicut e non in principio, sic in fine non credimus, qui simili promissione delusos multoties nos dolemus. Indigne ergo super oppressionibus predictarum ecclesiarum et hominum regni, in quo nullus manum vel pedem absque tuo movet imperio, affirmativam nostre propositionis negativa ignorantie imperialis interimis, quibus consensum vel originem prestitisse, cum nuntiis et litteris apostolicis ac clamoribus passorum iniurias, cas tuis auribus pluries inculcatas non solum scire set etiam plene potueris emendare, minime dubitaris. Quod ex illo tuarum litterarum tenore manifeste colligitur, qui pro iurium conservatione tuorum te nonnulla immutasse circa ecclesias, et tibi super non restituenda eis possessione ablata nostrum in facto Civitatis Castelle suffragari magisterium suffragatur d, cum in causa tua superioris debueris expetiisse et expectasse iudicium; nisi forte vulgus respondeat, quod iuxta placitum terminos regum transgrederis, dum contra ius aggrederis officia sacerdotum. Qualiter autem contra conscientiam nostram, ut asseris, denegata tibi possessionis civitatis predicte intentionie tue opituletur restitutio, non videmus, cum cives Castellani, qui se tibi violato sacramento fidei, ignorante ecclesia, prodiderunt, excellentie tue nullum ius per hoc in seipsis acquirere, nullum nobis circa possessionem, cum iurisdictionem civitatis et civium quasi possideret ecclesia, prodendo potuerunt preiudicium generare; male namque agitur, cum dominisf prediorum, si tantums precario possidentibus non requiritur possessionis initium, leges possessionum evertere et extraneis iura conferre valeant possessorum. Et ideo, si prudenter attenderes, quod Gen. 29. lignum vite est in paradisi medio positum, sic in centro tuorum finium prudenter persisteres, quod nequaquam incaute ad iudicanda secreta conscientie nostre, cuius 10b. 16 20 iudex in celo est conseius in excelsis, proprie ruinam conscientie metuens evolasses, cum regum colla et principum submitti videas genibus sacerdotum, et Christiani imperatores subdere debeant executiones suas non solum Romano pontifici, quin etiam aliis presulibus non preferre 6, nec non Dominus sedem apostolicam, cuius iudicio orbem terrarum subicit, in occultis et manifestis a nemine iudicandam, soli suo iudicio reservarit. At fortassis ignoras, quod Oza morte percutitur, eo quod arcam Domini 2 Reg. 67. inclinatam manu temeraria sustinere conabatur, et tribus Chaath, que vasa tabernaculi Num. 4.15. propriis involuta portabat humeris, paribus addicitur detrimentis, si tabernaculum solius Aaron dispositioni commissum ingredi vel vasa sanctuarii, priusquam involuta fuerint, ulla curiositate audeat intueri. Quare si te ad notoria facta tua speculanda reduceres, non solum de nostra, immo iudicare de conscientia etiam cuiuslibet tui subditi dubitares. Ergo quia de conscientia agitur, ut contra conscientiam secundum conscientiam procedatur, cum nostre fuisset conscientie liquidum, quod de reddendis possessionibus ecclesie Romane ad te pervenientibus pluries prestiteras iuramentum, non videbatur esse boni filii a patre petere, quod nec salva conscientia poteras detinere, eo quod nec ecclesia vitium spoliantis incurrerit, cui commoda sui iuris constitutionis beneficium integra reservavit. Nec est verisimile in hac parte nos fratrum nostrorum consilium despexisse, cum super hoc nuntii tui inceptum prosequi noluissenta iudicium; et ideo nondum erat in his eorum consilium requirendum. Esto preterea quod ecclesiis cum principibus permutare, sicut in tuis litteris? excusationem allegas, utroque iure conceditur; inique tamen ad dampnosam et non voluntariam huiusmodi celebrationem contractuum, presertim sine superioris assensu et contra iuramentum de non alienandis ecclesiasticis possessionibus, quas pro animarum salute relictas sic alienantes et recipientes sacrilegii crimen incurrunt, prestitum, compelluntur, quia quod in ecclesiarum favorem iure permittitur fieri, non debet ad lesionem earum per iniuriam retorqueric. Esto quod aliqua beneficia vacantia conferas; ut curam tamen animarum illis annexam committere valeas, ius spirituale, quod non cadit in laicum, non permittit, et in locum viventium, quos a gradu suo nec propria culpa nec sui iudicis sententia deicit, alios substitui ius datum celitus interdicit. Esto quod in collatione beneficiorum morientibus succedas, ut dicis, episcopis; maiorem in hoc ipsis non adipisceris potestatem, nec nos ob id, qui eis viventibus conferre beneficia non collata potuimus, iam te locum tenente ne dicamus usurpante pontifieis, apostolice amittimus plenitudinem potestatis. Venerabilis insuper frater noster Cephaludensis episcopus, archidiaconus Salernitanus et Sorane civitatis ecclesie, dum eos ad examen nostre considerationis adducimus, quare istid perpetui exilii et ille perpetue patiantur ruine dispendia, ignoramus, nisi quod dum contra pacem inter te ac ecclesiam reformatam spiritualia sicut secularia iudicas, dum eos, qui suo domino stant aut cadunt, non convictos nec confessos, pena iudicium prevenientee, condemnas, divini iudicii thronum aggrederis, et leges, quibus digne submittitur principatus, a lare patrio exulare compellis. De illo, qui se Geracensem dicit episcopum, tacemus ad presens, quem electio canonica pretermissa vel per impressionem habita ecclesie Geracensif matrimonialiter alligare non potuit, cuius consecratio, forma ecclesiastica sicut dicitur destituta, nec sibi executionem officii contulit nec ipsum illius ecclesie vel alterius episcopum esse fecit. Vincula vero nepotis regis Tuneti, si ea recta acie considerationis inspiceres, in quantam iuris et divini nominis contumeliam compeditum alligent, plene scires, quia indigne seductus asseritur, qui ad notitiam vere fidei aliquo inducente vel Deo potius inspirante vocatur; quin potius, quantums probationes, quod preter offensam regis eiusdem et non circumventus  ad nos accederet recepturus baptismatis sacramentum, expostulas, aperte colligitur. Et idem clara multorum voce utinam non dicatur, quod apostolos et discipulos veritatis non sine Magistri iniuria manifesta innuis seductores, qui inimicos crucis Christi ad agnitionem lucis eterne monitis invitarunt salutaribus et invitant, et ex eo tacite asseris non debere Deo contra hominem obediri, quod dictum nepotem credis debuisse prefati regis licentiam prestolari, cum tibi non liceat ignorare, quod tantus est favor baptismatis, ut etiam servos, sicut a iugo criminis, sic invitis dominis infidelibus et eos converti nolentibus a catena eximat servitutis. Utinam lex Domini Deut. 4, 20 convertens animas sic omnes fideles seduceret, quod eos de fornace ferrea Pharaonis eductos ad vere fidei notitiam evocaret! Utinam omnes fideles sic suos superiores offenderent, quod ad auditorium celeste vocati preconi parerent Dominico et in se tam salutari contumacia suorum offensam principum provocarent! Tolosano comiti etsi lata in eum excommunicationis sententia nequiverit privilegium immunitatis afferre vel iuri tuo preiudicium generare, debuit tamen ei favorem communionis imperialis auferre, quam sibi nequibas preter anime tue periculum, que tibi omni thesauro debet esse carior, indulgere, ut hoc saltem rubore perfusus, ad sinum matris rediret ecclesie et tibi sine salutis tue dispendio posset debitum servitium exhibere. Ceterum, ne nostro quod verum est patefaciente responso dicta exaggerare cogamur et gesta, calamo nostro brevitatem indicimus, et ne super eo quod de lege regia et episcopis scripseras, honorem tuum obice veritatis exasperet, prohibemus. Set vade ad tuorum memoriam predecessorum et inspice, transi ad felicis recordationis Constantini, Caroli Magni, Arcadii et Valentiniani imperatorum exempla et ea diligentius speculare, ubi infallibilis solutionis a conclusio sine instantia super premissis accipitur, ubi reprobanda false opinionis assumptio confutatur. Illud autem minime preterimus, toti mundo publice manifestum, quod predictus Constantinus, qui singularem super universa mundi climata monarchiam obtinebat, una cum toto senatu et populo, non solum Urbis set in toto imperio Romano constituto, unanimi omnium accedente consensu, dignum esse decernens, ut sicut principis apostolorum vicarius in toto orbe sacerdotii et animarum regebat imperium, sic in universo mundo rerum obtineret et corporum principatum, et existimans illum terrena debere sub habena iustitie regere, cui Dominum noverat in terris celestium regimen commisisse, Romano pontifici signa et sceptra imperialia, Urbem cum toto ducatu suo, quam sparsis in ea pecuniis nobis Iob. 4ouis. turbare moliris i, illius sequens exemplum qui absorbens fluvium non miratur, et sperans quod Iordanis influat in os eius, suo est voto fraudatus, nec non et imperium cure perpetuo tradidit, et nefarium reputans, ut ubi caput totius Christiane religionis ab imperatore celesti disponitur, ibidem terrenus imperator potestate aliqua fungeretur, Italiam apostolice dispositioni relinquens, sibi novam in Grecia mansionem elegit; de qua postmodum in persona prefati magnifici Caroli, qui iugum a Romana ecclesia vix ferendum impositum pia debere docuit devotione portari, sedes apostolica transferens in Germanos, predecessoribus tuis, sicut et in tua persona recolis esse factum, in consecrationis et inunctionis munere, nichil de substantia sue iurisdictionis imminuens, imperii tribunal supposuit et gladii potestatem in subsecuta coronatione concessit; ex quo iuri apostolice sedis et non minus fidei ac honori tuo derogare convinceris, dum factorem proprium non agnoscis. Ex eo autem non modicam notam indevotionis incurris, quod nobis et fratribus nostris sacrilegii maculam conaris impingere, quia cos quibus a te ecclesie ac ecclesiastica, beneficia conferuntur reputantes indignos, de tuo videmur iudicio disputare, non attendens quod sacerdotes Christi regum et principum omnium fidelium patres et magistri censentur. Nonne miserabilis insanie esse cognoscitur, si filius patrem, discipulus magistrum conetur arguere, a quibus non solum in terris set in celis sese ligari posse institutione divina docetur? Omnes enim, nisi quorum oculus aliquo erroris pulvere obturatur, agnoscunt, quod cum tu ipse apostolice examinationi, sicut testantur premissa, subiaceas, multo fortius de illorum possumus indignitate cognoscere, qui de manu tua noscuntur dignitatem aliquam suscepisse, eo quod quidquid speciei subicitur, de illo genus necessario predicatur. Hoc in personis ecclesiasticis negari non potest, quibus nos ex constitutione divina preficimur; imperialis vero potentia ex sola usurpatione in huiusmodi in iniuriam divini nominis aliquoties dominatur, in eo rhetorico fucata colore quod apud reges terrarum et principes de ecclesia, que usque modo non modicum imperiali pepercit honori, te depositurum querelas!, quibusdam apud eos iam depositis?, comminaris. Premissa quoque, quantumcumque sint gravia, quantumcumque a iuris tramite sint remota, minora tamen in oculis nostris respectu illius iniurie reputantur, que creatori nostro in hoc evidentius irrogatur, quod turbis undecumque collectis Crucifixi fidem et nomen publice predicari, ne qua ex hoc tuo contingant regno dispendia, non permittens, recuperationem Terre Sancte et crucis negotium impedis, ad cuius consummationem contra consilium tuum de bonis tuorum conferri fidelium interdicis. Quocirca celsitudinem tuam rogandam duximus et monendam, quatenus sub potenti manu Dei, cui clara sunt abscondita tenebrarum, sic humiliari procures, sic omnes sponse sue iniurias studeas emendare, quod te taliter exaltasse eum nequaquam peniteat et sue maiestatis oculos a tuis processibus non avertat, nosque de imperialibus profectibus possimus non immerito in Domino gratularia. Dat. Reate, X Kal. Novemb. anno decimo.<|eot_id|><|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>

regesto_originale: Gregorius IX papa Friderico Romanorum imperatori ad querelas de processu Hacobil episcopi Praenestini prolatas respondet et argumenta, quibus ad suam purgationem usus est, refellit; in memoriam ei redigit imperatores examinationi apostolicae subiacere, cumque fortiter monet, ut iniurias Romanae et regni Siciliae ecclesiis illatas emendare studeat vel timeat, ne Deus ab eius processibus oculos avertat. 1236, Oct. 23.

Friderico, Romanorum imperatori etc. Si memoriam beneficiorum conditoris eterni, que per ministerium sponse sue in sublimes personas et humiles largiter emanarunt, humane ingratitudinis oblivio non deleret, sia dominus noster lesus Christus, iudex vivorum et mortuorum, iudicaturus apertis libris conscientie et revelatis tenebrarum operibus universos, ut Dominus timeretur, origo virtutum, fides, inconcussa persisteret, opera statera iustitie ponderaret: Psal, 7299. verba sub veritatis signaculo clauderentur et os contra Deum non poneretur in celum, unde tonitrua prodeunt et fulgura contra persecutores suos sepe mittit Deus et dominus ultionum. Sane ex pluribus litteris ad nos et fratres nostros nuper ab imperiali excellentia destinatis ! plura collegimus, que si stylus mitigasset humilior et amaritudinem pagine dulcorasset affectus reverentie filialis, virtus discretionis sub manna dulcedinis irascibilem spiritum temperasset et imago Dei, que resultat in speculo rationis, ac similitudo eius, que per affectum bonum et zelum rectitudinis in potentiis anime naturalibus invenitur, non fuissent sic scribendo forsitan deformate. Set inter cetera epistole tue textum, quib processum venerabilis fratris nostri.. Penestrini episcopi, apostolice sedis legati, detestabilem et enormem asserit, nosque totius culpe eidem obiecte principio vel saltem participio non carere conscribit, iustitie norma non sequitur et iustificata in suis operibus veritas detestatur. Cum enim ad exemplum mediatoris Dei et hominum, qui ut pacem inter Deum et hominem reformaret, formam suscipere non est dedignatus humanam, scissuras scismatis ad integritatem reducere unitatis sedes apostolica teneatur, nostre quo Deo et homini astringimur servitutis officium in Lombardiam pro sedanda imperii et Lombardorum discordia compulit destinare legatum, qui et dissidentes ad imperiale mandatum reconciliatos reduceret et inter populos discordantes pacis federa reformaret. Nec illud nostrum tam sanctum, tam salubre potuit impedire set potius debuit adiuvare propositum, quod te in Lombardiam pro extirpanda heretica pravitate, subsidio Terre Sancte et recuperatione iurium ecclesie ac imperii nec non pro reformatione pacis proclamabas esse venturum. Nam si te ad id imperii reformatio invitavit, nos causa imperii, cuius deformatio in dispendium ecclesie Romane redundat, ecclesiarum utilitas, que longum sub bellorum fluctibus discidium patitur, et animarum periculum, pro quibus possessori celi et terre ad ratiocinium obligamur, ad procuranda bona concordie debuerunt fortius excitasse. Unde nichil de tuo iure usurpasse, de tuo nichil, licet contrarium asseras, occupasse officio credimur, si nos, de quorum consilio te ad id in principio, medio et fine procedere, sicut pluries promisisti ?, decuerat, prompti nostrum summo creditori exolvere debitum invenimur. Quare premissa more artificis, cuius considerationi se primitus offerunt que ultimo in operatione concurrunt, diligentius attendentes, illum, ut per eum nostrum impleremus ministerium, elegimus in hac parte ministrum, qui eo tibi et quibuscumque discordantibus minori posset haberi ratione suspectus, quo eius mens terrenis desideriis absoluta suis actibus fermenti minus ingereret odii vel amoris, qui se ipsum et sua relinquens in divini amoris altitudinem evolasset. Quis illius sinceritati rugam suspicionis obicere, quis illius puritatem nevo duplicitatis opposito poterit obfuscare, quem suscepta professionis beate religio carni et mundo abstulit, quem Deo fructus laudabilium operum et vite sanctitas commendavit? Nec enim locus originis recte contra eum in suspicionis argumentum inducitur !, cum non bonitas hominis deformetur a loco, set potius loci malitia per hominem reformetur. Probat hoc, quod nec pietati Christi quicquam mundus subtraxit impius, nec celum fecit sanctum demonem nec hominem paradisus. Genus etiam ad tuam intentionem non sufficere, immo nec proficere creditur, quia frustra in illo parentele vitia condempnantur, qui per conversationis sancte munditiam a patria et parentibus, quasi in virum mutatus alium, factus est penitus peregrinus. Quid plura? Frustra quid ad probationem alicuius inducitur, quod illud nec frequenter nec inseparabiliter comitatur. Suffragatur autem ad hoc testimonium dilecti filii.. magistri hospitalis sancte Marie Teutonicorum?, et ei, quoda alia vice ipsum cum dilecto filio nostro Ottone Sancti Nicolai in Carcere Tulliano diacono cardinali transmissum 3 tibi suspectum fuisse asseris, refragatur, cum ipsum nichil fecisse, unde celsitudini imperiali suspectus merito deberet haberi, coram nobis publica voce dixerit et eum circa observationem iustitie plurimum commendarit. Erubescere igitur poterit novus logyeus de nobis mali alicuius initium vel participium paralogismo concludere, cuius falsitatem etiam imperiti de longe speculantes possunt luce clarius improbare, cum publice bonum et manifesta boni species fuerit, quod legatus ad reformandam pacem inter te ac Lombardos a nobis destinatus accessit, cui nichil posseb credimus imputari, si eo presente sedata sint intestina bella Placentie, si alique civitates Lombardie, cladibus preliorum oppresse, ad pacis fuerint dulcedinem invitate. Quinimmo tibi ad infamiam reputatur, quod, ecclesia suoc prefato mediante legato, pacem imperii dedigneris vel non patiaris potius reformari. Set est fortasse qui dicat, quod dum contra fas et licitum episcopum prefatum tuis non habes votis omnino propitium, eum imperialibus extimes desideriis inimicum. et quo equalius eundem ad quodlibet oppositorum extremum, ut utraque unum efficiat, declinare perspexeris, eo fortius ipsum celsitudinis tue profectibus contrarium suspiceris. De quo, si placot, obtrectationis cossent obloquia, cuiuslibet prudentis et boni principis moribus inimica, qui sic ius suum discrete prosequitur, quod in nullius, presertim timentis Deum et episcopi, detractionem armatur. Verum ne aliqua de sede apostolica vere vel apparenter excellentie tue querela consurgat, tibi contra predictum legatum, quem d nondum probatio seu confessio obiecti criminis et ignoti convincit, experiri volenti sumus iustitiam exhibere parati. Ceterum, ne super imperialis celsitudinis de cohercenda, ut tuis verbis utamur, contumacia Lombardorum petitionee responsionem videamur per oblivionem vel negligentiam distulisse, dictus magister tibi satisfacere potuit, de cuius consilio dilectum filium G. 4 subdiaconum et capellanum nostrum ad tractandum de pace duximus destinandum. Quare responsio tibi grata non poterat fieri, per quem tractatum concordie contingebat penitus impediri. Nec etiam nobis de obiecta eis contumacia constitit, ad quos pro facto imperii mandatum apostolicum, cui superba cervice restiterint, nullatenus emanavit; quinimmo compromissum in manus nostras venerabili fratre nostro.. patriarcha Antiocheno ? procurante teque petente firmantes, etsi infra tempus nunciis tuis pro tua voluntate prefixum ad nostram presentiam venire nequiverint, maculam tamen erga te, si dici potest, commisse contumacie per sequentis obedientiam compromiss a se videntur penitus abstersisse !. Igitur si nostre te faceresa doctrine discipulumb, si apostolici processus circa honorem tuum sepe sepius habiti imitareris exemplum, iusta monita nostra super commissis in regno corrigendis excessibus, pluries ab annis preteritis replicata et toties passa repulsionis iniuriam, ad debitum exauditionis admitteres, iniusta quoque, que nunquam tibi credimus ex certa scientia direxisse, procul ab imperialis limine concessionis arceres. Set ecce super facto ecclesiarum regni, quod tibi in litteris nostris primo directis ? sub genere indefinite proponitur, quod ad hoc non tenearis quasi dubia respondere, a te reali responsione preterita vocali commentario incongrue respondetur 3, tum quia frustra requiritur, ut singularia speciei vel specialia fidem faciant generi, cum genus et species manifestam ex se prebent notitiam veritati, et cum individuorum scientia quasi ex infinitate confunditur, ad doctrinam universalium supervacue singularia colliguntur; tum quia que in primis litteris sub indefinita, in se tamen aliorum definita notitia fuere proposita, ex superabundanti in litteris nostris ad te secundo currentibus t per multa fuerunt particularia declarata, sicut in epistola tua responsiva ? conicitur, que in se ipsa quibusdam particularibus verbaliter respondendo, quod in premissis falsum implicet, improbatur; cuius pollicitis de satisfactione prestanda quibusdam ecclesiis et personis, sicut e non in principio, sic in fine non credimus, qui simili promissione delusos multoties nos dolemus. Indigne ergo super oppressionibus predictarum ecclesiarum et hominum regni, in quo nullus manum vel pedem absque tuo movet imperio, affirmativam nostre propositionis negativa ignorantie imperialis interimis, quibus consensum vel originem prestitisse, cum nuntiis et litteris apostolicis ac clamoribus passorum iniurias, cas tuis auribus pluries inculcatas non solum scire set etiam plene potueris emendare, minime dubitaris. Quod ex illo tuarum litterarum tenore manifeste colligitur, qui pro iurium conservatione tuorum te nonnulla immutasse circa ecclesias, et tibi super non restituenda eis possessione ablata nostrum in facto Civitatis Castelle suffragari magisterium suffragatur d, cum in causa tua superioris debueris expetiisse et expectasse iudicium; nisi forte vulgus respondeat, quod iuxta placitum terminos regum transgrederis, dum contra ius aggrederis officia sacerdotum. Qualiter autem contra conscientiam nostram, ut asseris, denegata tibi possessionis civitatis predicte intentionie tue opituletur restitutio, non videmus, cum cives Castellani, qui se tibi violato sacramento fidei, ignorante ecclesia, prodiderunt, excellentie tue nullum ius per hoc in seipsis acquirere, nullum nobis circa possessionem, cum iurisdictionem civitatis et civium quasi possideret ecclesia, prodendo potuerunt preiudicium generare; male namque agitur, cum dominisf prediorum, si tantums precario possidentibus non requiritur possessionis initium, leges possessionum evertere et extraneis iura conferre valeant possessorum. Et ideo, si prudenter attenderes, quod Gen. 29. lignum vite est in paradisi medio positum, sic in centro tuorum finium prudenter persisteres, quod nequaquam incaute ad iudicanda secreta conscientie nostre, cuius 10b. 16 20 iudex in celo est conseius in excelsis, proprie ruinam conscientie metuens evolasses, cum regum colla et principum submitti videas genibus sacerdotum, et Christiani imperatores subdere debeant executiones suas non solum Romano pontifici, quin etiam aliis presulibus non preferre 6, nec non Dominus sedem apostolicam, cuius iudicio orbem terrarum subicit, in occultis et manifestis a nemine iudicandam, soli suo iudicio reservarit. At fortassis ignoras, quod Oza morte percutitur, eo quod arcam Domini 2 Reg. 67. inclinatam manu temeraria sustinere conabatur, et tribus Chaath, que vasa tabernaculi Num. 4.15. propriis involuta portabat humeris, paribus addicitur detrimentis, si tabernaculum solius Aaron dispositioni commissum ingredi vel vasa sanctuarii, priusquam involuta fuerint, ulla curiositate audeat intueri. Quare si te ad notoria facta tua speculanda reduceres, non solum de nostra, immo iudicare de conscientia etiam cuiuslibet tui subditi dubitares. Ergo quia de conscientia agitur, ut contra conscientiam secundum conscientiam procedatur, cum nostre fuisset conscientie liquidum, quod de reddendis possessionibus ecclesie Romane ad te pervenientibus pluries prestiteras iuramentum, non videbatur esse boni filii a patre petere, quod nec salva conscientia poteras detinere, eo quod nec ecclesia vitium spoliantis incurrerit, cui commoda sui iuris constitutionis beneficium integra reservavit. Nec est verisimile in hac parte nos fratrum nostrorum consilium despexisse, cum super hoc nuntii tui inceptum prosequi noluissenta iudicium; et ideo nondum erat in his eorum consilium requirendum. Esto preterea quod ecclesiis cum principibus permutare, sicut in tuis litteris? excusationem allegas, utroque iure conceditur; inique tamen ad dampnosam et non voluntariam huiusmodi celebrationem contractuum, presertim sine superioris assensu et contra iuramentum de non alienandis ecclesiasticis possessionibus, quas pro animarum salute relictas sic alienantes et recipientes sacrilegii crimen incurrunt, prestitum, compelluntur, quia quod in ecclesiarum favorem iure permittitur fieri, non debet ad lesionem earum per iniuriam retorqueric. Esto quod aliqua beneficia vacantia conferas; ut curam tamen animarum illis annexam committere valeas, ius spirituale, quod non cadit in laicum, non permittit, et in locum viventium, quos a gradu suo nec propria culpa nec sui iudicis sententia deicit, alios substitui ius datum celitus interdicit. Esto quod in collatione beneficiorum morientibus succedas, ut dicis, episcopis; maiorem in hoc ipsis non adipisceris potestatem, nec nos ob id, qui eis viventibus conferre beneficia non collata potuimus, iam te locum tenente ne dicamus usurpante pontifieis, apostolice amittimus plenitudinem potestatis. Venerabilis insuper frater noster Cephaludensis episcopus, archidiaconus Salernitanus et Sorane civitatis ecclesie, dum eos ad examen nostre considerationis adducimus, quare istid perpetui exilii et ille perpetue patiantur ruine dispendia, ignoramus, nisi quod dum contra pacem inter te ac ecclesiam reformatam spiritualia sicut secularia iudicas, dum eos, qui suo domino stant aut cadunt, non convictos nec confessos, pena iudicium prevenientee, condemnas, divini iudicii thronum aggrederis, et leges, quibus digne submittitur principatus, a lare patrio exulare compellis. De illo, qui se Geracensem dicit episcopum, tacemus ad presens, quem electio canonica pretermissa vel per impressionem habita ecclesie Geracensif matrimonialiter alligare non potuit, cuius consecratio, forma ecclesiastica sicut dicitur destituta, nec sibi executionem officii contulit nec ipsum illius ecclesie vel alterius episcopum esse fecit. Vincula vero nepotis regis Tuneti, si ea recta acie considerationis inspiceres, in quantam iuris et divini nominis contumeliam compeditum alligent, plene scires, quia indigne seductus asseritur, qui ad notitiam vere fidei aliquo inducente vel Deo potius inspirante vocatur; quin potius, quantums probationes, quod preter offensam regis eiusdem et non circumventus  ad nos accederet recepturus baptismatis sacramentum, expostulas, aperte colligitur. Et idem clara multorum voce utinam non dicatur, quod apostolos et discipulos veritatis non sine Magistri iniuria manifesta innuis seductores, qui inimicos crucis Christi ad agnitionem lucis eterne monitis invitarunt salutaribus et invitant, et ex eo tacite asseris non debere Deo contra hominem obediri, quod dictum nepotem credis debuisse prefati regis licentiam prestolari, cum tibi non liceat ignorare, quod tantus est favor baptismatis, ut etiam servos, sicut a iugo criminis, sic invitis dominis infidelibus et eos converti nolentibus a catena eximat servitutis. Utinam lex Domini Deut. 4, 20 convertens animas sic omnes fideles seduceret, quod eos de fornace ferrea Pharaonis eductos ad vere fidei notitiam evocaret! Utinam omnes fideles sic suos superiores offenderent, quod ad auditorium celeste vocati preconi parerent Dominico et in se tam salutari contumacia suorum offensam principum provocarent! Tolosano comiti etsi lata in eum excommunicationis sententia nequiverit privilegium immunitatis afferre vel iuri tuo preiudicium generare, debuit tamen ei favorem communionis imperialis auferre, quam sibi nequibas preter anime tue periculum, que tibi omni thesauro debet esse carior, indulgere, ut hoc saltem rubore perfusus, ad sinum matris rediret ecclesie et tibi sine salutis tue dispendio posset debitum servitium exhibere. Ceterum, ne nostro quod verum est patefaciente responso dicta exaggerare cogamur et gesta, calamo nostro brevitatem indicimus, et ne super eo quod de lege regia et episcopis scripseras, honorem tuum obice veritatis exasperet, prohibemus. Set vade ad tuorum memoriam predecessorum et inspice, transi ad felicis recordationis Constantini, Caroli Magni, Arcadii et Valentiniani imperatorum exempla et ea diligentius speculare, ubi infallibilis solutionis a conclusio sine instantia super premissis accipitur, ubi reprobanda false opinionis assumptio confutatur. Illud autem minime preterimus, toti mundo publice manifestum, quod predictus Constantinus, qui singularem super universa mundi climata monarchiam obtinebat, una cum toto senatu et populo, non solum Urbis set in toto imperio Romano constituto, unanimi omnium accedente consensu, dignum esse decernens, ut sicut principis apostolorum vicarius in toto orbe sacerdotii et animarum regebat imperium, sic in universo mundo rerum obtineret et corporum principatum, et existimans illum terrena debere sub habena iustitie regere, cui Dominum noverat in terris celestium regimen commisisse, Romano pontifici signa et sceptra imperialia, Urbem cum toto ducatu suo, quam sparsis in ea pecuniis nobis Iob. 4ouis. turbare moliris i, illius sequens exemplum qui absorbens fluvium non miratur, et sperans quod Iordanis influat in os eius, suo est voto fraudatus, nec non et imperium cure perpetuo tradidit, et nefarium reputans, ut ubi caput totius Christiane religionis ab imperatore celesti disponitur, ibidem terrenus imperator potestate aliqua fungeretur, Italiam apostolice dispositioni relinquens, sibi novam in Grecia mansionem elegit; de qua postmodum in persona prefati magnifici Caroli, qui iugum a Romana ecclesia vix ferendum impositum pia debere docuit devotione portari, sedes apostolica transferens in Germanos, predecessoribus tuis, sicut et in tua persona recolis esse factum, in consecrationis et inunctionis munere, nichil de substantia sue iurisdictionis imminuens, imperii tribunal supposuit et gladii potestatem in subsecuta coronatione concessit; ex quo iuri apostolice sedis et non minus fidei ac honori tuo derogare convinceris, dum factorem proprium non agnoscis. Ex eo autem non modicam notam indevotionis incurris, quod nobis et fratribus nostris sacrilegii maculam conaris impingere, quia cos quibus a te ecclesie ac ecclesiastica, beneficia conferuntur reputantes indignos, de tuo videmur iudicio disputare, non attendens quod sacerdotes Christi regum et principum omnium fidelium patres et magistri censentur. Nonne miserabilis insanie esse cognoscitur, si filius patrem, discipulus magistrum conetur arguere, a quibus non solum in terris set in celis sese ligari posse institutione divina docetur? Omnes enim, nisi quorum oculus aliquo erroris pulvere obturatur, agnoscunt, quod cum tu ipse apostolice examinationi, sicut testantur premissa, subiaceas, multo fortius de illorum possumus indignitate cognoscere, qui de manu tua noscuntur dignitatem aliquam suscepisse, eo quod quidquid speciei subicitur, de illo genus necessario predicatur. Hoc in personis ecclesiasticis negari non potest, quibus nos ex constitutione divina preficimur; imperialis vero potentia ex sola usurpatione in huiusmodi in iniuriam divini nominis aliquoties dominatur, in eo rhetorico fucata colore quod apud reges terrarum et principes de ecclesia, que usque modo non modicum imperiali pepercit honori, te depositurum querelas !, quibusdam apud eos iam depositis ?, comminaris. Premissa quoque, quantumcumque sint gravia, quantumcumque a iuris tramite sint remota, minora tamen in oculis nostris respectu illius iniurie reputantur, que creatori nostro in hoc evidentius irrogatur, quod turbis undecumque collectis Crucifixi fidem et nomen publice predicari, ne qua ex hoc tuo contingant regno dispendia, non permittens, recuperationem Terre Sancte et crucis negotium impedis, ad cuius consummationem contra consilium tuum de bonis tuorum conferri fidelium interdicis. Quocirca celsitudinem tuam rogandam duximus et monendam, quatenus sub potenti manu Dei, cui clara sunt abscondita tenebrarum, sic humiliari procures, sic omnes sponse sue iniurias studeas emendare, quod te taliter exaltasse eum nequaquam peniteat et sue maiestatis oculos a tuis processibus non avertat, nosque de imperialibus profectibus possimus non immerito in Domino gratularia. Dat. Reate, X Kal. Novemb. anno decimo.

You are not unaware, we believe, that we asked you to try to obtain from the emperor, who holds them, the goods that belong to the daughter of the late queen Beatrice, your daughter, which we have asked for many times in the name of the king, our son, because he refused to return them. We resorted to your lordship, seeking your counsel and help. You answered us, as is becoming for a father and vicar of Jesus Christ, that you would not be lacking in counsel and that you would make sure that the right to the goods would be granted to us. Since the emperor, having been guided by a more mature counsel, has many times signified to us that he is willing to return them, provided that he is given the opportunity to send his son, Frederick, to him, we have decided to send him there, following the advice of wise men, whom you have requested to express himself on this matter to your lordship in more detail. We order you to live and die in the obedience of the Roman Church and to be devoted to her honor and exaltation. regesto_sintetico: Translation in English of the text: We, lord Pope Gregory IX, to all who will see or hear this present letter, greeting. The Lord Jesus, the savior of the world, who has been put to death for the redemption of our salvation, is sleeping, as it were, in the vessel of Peter, the mother of the Church. The vessel is beaten by the waves of the tempests of questions, and the anchor of the ship, which is the Church, is shaken. The Lord is sleeping, as it were, in the Ark of Noah, where the Lord has said, "I will make a covenant between me and you, and every living thing of all flesh shall be slain." For the world, which is the ship, is filled with the rage of the beasts, and the wicked have increased, who, as it is written, "are like a wild ass's colt, which came out of the woods, where the people shall not prevail over them, neither shall they be fruitful, and they shall not be multiplied, nor shall they possess the land of the just, nor dwell among the people of the Lord." For it is written, "The wicked shall not stand in the judgment, and sinners in the congregation of the righteous shall not be gathered." They, therefore, who are in the ship of the Church, and are not at rest, and do not desire to be at rest, wish to be saved by the Lord, who is sleeping, as it were, and to be delivered from the waves of the tempests of questions, and from the rage of the beasts, and to be gathered in the congregation of the righteous. For the Lord, who is sleeping, as it were, will not put to sleep the vessel of the Church, nor will He allow it to be destroyed, as long as the prudent men, who are in it, will be vigilant, and will not be asleep. And therefore we, who are at the helm of the vessel, wish to be helped by the hands of the strong, that is to say, of the kings, prelates, and other faithful, that we may be able to put to sleep the Lord, who is sleeping, as it were, and to deliver the vessel of the Church from the waves of the tempests of questions, and from the rage of the beasts, and to gather it in the congregation of the righteous. And therefore we, lord kings, prelates, and other faithful, to whom the present letter shall come, if we have not been able to come to you in person, command you by apostolic authority, that you do not delay in sending to us prudent and worthy men, who shall be at our disposal, that we may be able to provide for the solution of the aforesaid questions, which we have taken up with God's help, and to make provision for the general good of the Church, as you will learn in full from the bearer of these letters. And we command you, that you do not delay in sending them to us, but that you hasten to do so, that we may be able to make provision for the solution of the aforesaid questions, and to make provision for the general good of the Church, as you will learn in full from the bearer of these letters. regesto_sintetico: English translation: The letters of the legate on the obligation of the possessions of the churches of Genoa. To the most holy father and lord, lord G., by the grace of God most holy Roman church supreme pontiff, G. of Romania devoted to you himself comes. Coming to Genoa, brother Nicholas proposed that you had completely wished that I should have the galleys, ushers and other vessels for the transportation and return of the prelates and others who will come to the council from the common of Genoa procured, having received a sufficient guarantee from the common of the said city. Since I have labored and suffered much with the advice of all those, whom you have expressed in your letters, in brief I could not explain the thing, because many wanted to impede it, and it could not be consummated without their advice. I could do nothing on these things, unless first I had solved the common of Genoa one thousand marks for the equipment of galleys and taridas, which they count in the agreement and settlement, of which three thousand five hundred and fifty I had from you and fifty pounds of Genoa, which I gave to the merchants who lent the said marks, for the expenses; for which marks the prelates of Genoa have obligated their possessions to the merchants. And I wrote to lord... bishop of Penestrinot, apostolic see legate, that he pay five thousand marks of silver and fifty-seven, which I promised the merchants for their salary, subtracting the one thousand marks which I received; and the merchants are bound to give to your nuncios within a month after the reception in France two thousand marks and within another month another two thousand marks; and if this money will not be necessary for this business, it will be done with what will please you. The agreements made on the aforesaid business I send enclosed to your holiness between sealed. For the sake of the service that I did for you and the Roman church, I implore and beg you to grant me the license to return unwillingly to Genoa. You have commended to you magister Peter de Guarcino on the church of St. Xystus of Genoa, for whom I have asked you another time. In these few days there have been no prosperity for you, that if it were pleasing to all and accepted by all, it would be said and thought by many in different ways. It follows therefore that, regarding the sad case which has recently befallen you through divine permission, many different opinions and matters of discussion are held about it, which is not pleasing to you and should not move your sincerity or constancy, since you know that human nature has been disposed in such a way that speech is given to all and wisdom is granted to few, it is clear to us and to the intelligent mind that you, having the honor of God and the apostolic see, and the salvation of the universal church, and the merit of obedience, in which consist all virtues, have always had in view, that you have devotedly hastened with the help of many devoted people to the sin of the mother church, although it may be said that it has been appropriately and deservedly deplorable that you did not come with all the haste possible, as we had written to you in our letters, since, although you have been informed by the power of the opposite party that you had not taken the galleys, as much as you could, you did not have the passage to Christ, by which you would be able to cross without any danger, previously provided by the Lord. Since, dear brothers, the lamp of your virtues is not hidden under a bushel, but shines on the lampstand before all, you, who have been constantly faithful to us in Christ, have not allowed the contempt of vanities and the false follies of the insolent to reach you, but you have led them to silence and have been breathing in the Lord, who bears the afflictions of his people with continuous pity. You have always had the trust that we and our brothers are present in spirit, although we are in a different place and bound by different bonds, and we are comforted by the hope of the ineffable mercy of the Redeemer, who has planted the church in his blood and has lifted it up through the tribulations of his elect. We request that you, like the compassion of your feelings and the support of your prayers, so that the Father of mercies and God of all consolation, who has been pleased to grant to the merits of the glorious virgin and the blessed apostles the abundance of mercy, may grant us that, as we have desired and prayed for, we may be able to provide for the tranquility of the church and the peace of the world, so that after the storm of sadness a calm of joy may follow, and that the Catholic faith, which, as we have learned from the letters and the report of the faithful, is being assaulted by the incursion of the pagans in a way more horrible than can be believed, may be preserved inviolably for the glory of the superne majesty and the salvation of the faithful. But since you are dear to us in Christ and we have always had you in our heart with tender love and we can not pass the day without imagining your state with tears, it does not seem to us that it is surprising that we have not written to you or sent you a messenger with the sincerity of your state, and that your sorrow has not been alleviated by any provision of ours, especially since it has not been put aside due to negligence or occupation, but because we feared that your request would not have been granted due to the visitation. The purity and sincere devotion of your ancestors and yours, who not only derive from them by blood but also imitate their steps, deserve special praise. Your serenity has always shown itself so devoted to the Church that you have offered your services to it in the right moment, so that you have sought and have striven to procure for it the honor that it deserves among other princes of the world, and you have sought to obtain for it, by force of arms, the favor of the Roman Church, which has always been like a mother to you. And since we are bound to your ancestors and yours by such great devotion, we are bound to you by the same affection, so that we consider you worthy of the special favor of the Roman Church, and we are delighted by the increase of your prosperity and we are grieved by your misfortune. Recently, we have heard that the Tartars have devastated the Kingdom of Hungary with the sword, and we are struck by a heavy arrow of sorrow, because we have been informed that many Christians have been killed and the kingdom has been devastated. We are even more sorrowful because you, a noble member of the Church, have been wounded by such a cruel blow. But we lift our eyes to God, who, although he sometimes scourges a people with a severe rod for its sins, does not forget to console it afterwards with his mercy. regesto_originale: Innocentius IV papa Fridericum II imperatorem praesente concilio Lugduni congregato omni honore et dignitate sententiando privat, decernens ut qui ei tanquam imperatori pareant, ipso facto excommunicationis vinculo subiaceant. 1245, Iul. 17.
apparato: Inn. IV Reg. Vol. I, 208; Lib. II, cur. 13. Haec epistola anni III, quae una cum 'Istitutionibus concilii Lugdunensis' (Potthast, Reg. p. 996) post curiales anni II in Regestis legitur, licet saepius edita sit, nusquam tamen satis emendata invenitur, et sincerum exemplar Regestorum nunc primo profertur; quod v. Cl. A. Mau nobis praebuit, qui exemplar Raynaldi, Ann. eccl. a. 1245, § 33–45, cum Regestis contulit et ex eis correxit [R.). Raynaldus enim non Regesta exscripsit, sed formam epistolae proposuit simillimam ei, quam Binius, Concil., Coloniae a. 1606, t. III, pars II, p. 1485 imprimi fecerat, in qua verba authentica quasi exornata et amplificata sunt, in eum modum quem in summis dictaminis saepius reperimus. Raynaldum editores Bull. Taur. t. III, p. 510 secuti sunt. Eandem formam amplificatam cum Regestis collatam, sed minus diligenter, Cherubinus, Magn. Bull, Romae 1638, t. I, p. 94, praebere videtur (Ch.); nam aliquot locis editionis eius verba Raynaldi, quae V. Cl. A. Mau delevit neque authentica continent, inveniuntur, aliis ipsa verba Regestorum comparent. Cum editione Ch., nonnullis levibus variantibus exceptis, concordant: Concil., Paris. a. 1644, t. XXVIII, p. 424; Labbe, Conc. t. XI, p. 640; Hardouin, Conc. t. VII, p. 381; Lúnig, Cod. Ital. dipl. t. II, p. 901, n. 27; Dumont, Corps univ. dipl. t. I, p. 192; Mansi, Conc. t. XXIII, p. 613. — Authentica proposuerunt: 1) Matthaeus Paris., Chron, maior. a. 1245, ed. Luard t. IV, p. 445 (A I/, quem Dumont, l. c. p. 190 exscripsit, 2) Bzovius, Ann. eccl. a. 1245, 8 3 (A 2/, 3) Ann. Placent. Gib. a. 1245 in SS. t. XVIII, p. 490 (A 3/. Haec authentica multis locis inter se discrepant et praecipue A 3 mendis scatet. Litteras notatas correctas ideoque minus faciles lectu et authenticorum et Regestorum fontem fuisse ex aliquot variantibus conici potest. Potthast, Reg. 11733; Berger 1868.

Dilecti filii nobilis viri Bartholomeus Pesce, your, and brother Radulfus of the order of the Holy Trinity, dear sons of the noble man R., bishop of Cornwall, your brother's nuncio, who recently came to our presence, asked us for three things: first, that we would conserve for you and for them the right which they have in the county of Cornwall, except for the dowry that they owe you and them for their wives and for the agreement and contract between you and the late bishop of Provence, in which the contract contains the mediation of the county; second, that we would send someone from our side to prohibit the noble man Charles, brother of our dear son in Christ, the king of France, from occupying the cities, villages and castles of the county of Cornwall, until a full discussion is held before us and the aforementioned case is decided, so that you and your brother may return to the right of which they have been deprived by the grant of dispensation made by us to Charles; third, that we would not admit the will, which was made by the late bishop of Provence, of which mention is made, until we had knowledge of its contents and the said bishop had revoked it and died intestate. We therefore respond to the request of our beloved son, Master Laurence, your nuncio, who has been sent to the apostolic see and has several times invoked our ears, that although we are bound by the office of apostolic administration to protect all who are considered to be Christians, inasmuch as we love you and your brother, whom we hold to be dear to us and to the Roman church, we have resolved to conserve your right and that of your brother, which is due to you and him, and we wish to do so not more than out of pastoral solicitude, but also out of our own wish. To make the prohibition, however, which we have mentioned above, we do not see how we can proceed at present, because no one has come before us to demand justice for you and your brother in the form of a lawsuit. On the other hand, we have heard that you and your brother, who do not wish to proceed in the form of a lawsuit, have protested to us in our presence, and when the merits of the case of the parties are known, we do not yet know anything certain about the right. Nevertheless, we are induced by paternal love, which we wish to promote and increase, and we are moved by the desire to give you and your brother our favour. Therefore, we have ordered the king of the French and Charles to induce you and your brother to surrender the rights of your wives, sisters and relatives in the county of Cornwall, in the name of the salvation of their souls, and to do so in a liberal manner. We do not see, however, that the right of you and your brother has been derogated by our dispensation, nor do we see how it could be derogated. And although we have dispensed with the king of the French, inasmuch as he could have married a woman related to him in the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity, we did not name her specifically in our dispensation, nor did we dispense with any other woman. We do not believe, however, that the late bishop of Provence made a will, unless we are so advised by justice. The text of the letter is as follows: Sifrid, bishop of Magdeburg by God's grace. To all those who will see the present document, be it known that we, in order to bring quiet to the canons of Saint Victor, who are bringing a case against their prepositus on the issue of their prebends, and to the prepositus on the grounds of various defects caused by the turmoil of wars and sterility of times, have decided to divide the income of the prepositus from the income of the stipendium of the brothers in the following way: that no administration be granted to the prepositus in the future. Therefore, let all the above-mentioned income of the church be weighed by the canon of the church on the balance, as well as the prior, the prelates and many canons of Magdeburg, and let the prepositus possess in perpetuity the eight iugera of vineyards in the Mount of Saint Victor, the tenth of Bischofsheim in Eastern Franconia, the tenth of Kistene and the tenth of Rudesheim, with all their appurtenances, on condition that he does not have the power to donate or alienate them in any way to the church; if he does so, he shall incur the penalty of excommunication. The rest of the income that the church now has or will obtain in the future through the largesse of the faithful or any other legitimate title, shall belong freely and entirely to the brothers, not being hindered by the prepositus or his successors. It is also to be understood that this ordinance has been added: that if the Lord grants the church the possibility of redeeming any fiefs, the brothers shall have the freedom to acquire them, and the prepositus, who will then be, shall release the bond of hominium by which he was bound to the brothers who held the redeemed fief; the prepositus himself shall receive, like the brothers, a portion of the income from the redemption of the fiefs. On the contrary, if the prepositus shall be able to acquire or has acquired fiefs, they shall be assigned to the use of the prepositus and his successors.
