Nec est mirum, si de hoc dolemus potissime, tum propter exempli perniciem, quam assumentb exinde alie nationes, tum pro eo quod amicorum offense plus aggravant plusque ledunt, testante Domino per prophetam: “Si inimicus meus maledixisset mihi, supportasseme utique’. Satis quidem Ps. 54, 13. sufficiebant ad presens afflictiones, quas ecclesia patitur, insultus, quibus impetitur, et turbationes, quibus iugiter ab inimico homine ubilibet superseminante zizania molestatur. Non orat necesse, ut quidam ex baronibus Francie afflicte afflictionem adicerent, ipsam novis constitutionibus, vel potius destitutionibus d perturbantes; qui, sicut dolentes audivimus et miramur, ecclesiam, que ipsos ex utero sanctificationis regeneravit in filios ac pro eorum salute immaculatum agnum offert iugiter Deo patri, in servitutem cupientes redigere, ut iam nolint vocari filii libere sed ancille, immo sponsam regis eterni, qui ipsos suo sanguine a servitute perpetua liberavit, conantes miserabiliter ancillare, communi coniuratione et conspiratione contra libertatem ipsius plura, sicut dicitur, gravia et enormia statuerunt, que ius et consuetudinem predicte libertatis absorbent, ecclesie honorem elidunt, scandalum pariunt et pericula generant animarum!. Sane si negotii qualitas diligenter attenditur, si status rerum qualiqualie meditatione pensatur, honori vel strenuitati eorundem baronum non expediebat hoc tempore aggredi sanctam ecclesiam in tali articulo constitutam, cum ingenuif, circumscripto timore divino, ex magnanimitate quadam oppressis, eorum etiam si que fortes precesserint non memorantes iniurias, subvenire soleant eisque in necessitate manum porrigere adiutricem. Verum si dicti barones diligenter attenderent, quod Carolus Magnus ! ecclesiam, a qua omnem honorem susceperat, cupiens honorare, perpetua lege decrevit, ut omnes ipsius iurisdictioni subiecti statutum a Theodosio imperatore pro ecclesie libertate editum inviolabiliter observarent, videlicet ut 'quicunque litem habens, sive petitor fuerit, vel in a initio litis, vel decursis temporum curriculis, sive cum negotium peroratur, sive cum iam ceperit promi sententia, si iudicium elegerit sacrosancte sedis antistitis, illico sine aliqua dubitatione, etiamsi pars altera refragatur, ad episcoporum iudicium cum sermone litigantium dirigatur, et omnes cause, que pretorio et etiam civili iure tractantur, episcoporum terminateb sententiis, perpetue robur obtineant firmitatis, et negotium, quod iudicio ipsorum deciditur, nequaquam ulterius ab aliquo retractetur'. Ex quo manifesta potestis ratione perpendere, quam iniquum videatur et absonum, si honor ecclesie, que tam grandis libertatis privilegio donata dinoscitur, in illis immunitatibus, que multo predictis noscuntur esse minores, nostris temporibus decurtetur. Si alias barones ipsi pensarent, quod omnes, qui presumunt statuta condere contra ecclesiasticam libertatem, sunt ipso facto excommunicationis sententia innodati, forsitan non processissent ad talia nec etiam persisterent in eisdem; sed quia fortassis ad eorum non pervenerec notitiam, ut occasio de ignorantia et quod non fuerint moniti omnino tollatur, ipsa eis, quod desistant ab huiusmodi, per aliquos vestrum, quos ad hec idoneos videritis, nuntiari volumus et exponi ac eos ad id sollicitis monitis et exhortationibus diligenter induci. Quod si forte ad hoc prefati barones flecti nequiverint, aliquid de insufflate ipsorum auribus fermento nequitie retinentes, cum scriptum sit: Es. 58, 6. “Ne prospera te allevent nec adversa demittant', vos, sperantes in illo, qui colligationes impietatis et fasciculos deprimentes sua virtute dissolvit, ac considerantes quod Ps. 4, 2. ecclesia, contra quam etiam porte inferi non prevalebunt, consuevit in tribulatione iuxta verbum propheticum dilatari, statuatis vosmetipsos in defensione ecclesiastice Ierem. 1,is. libertatis exemplo prophete civitatem munitam et columnam ferream, nichil penitus metuentes; sed cordis armati constantia, quam nulla possit persecutionis penetrare sagitta, murum pro domo Domini vos viriliter opponentes, ea libertate, in cuius possessione adhuc extitistis et qua hactenus usi estis, confidenter utamini, et contra rebelles procedentes prout convenit, statuta contra libertatem ecclesiasticam attemptata irrita nuntiando, vos aut subditos vestros ipsius non permittatis commodo spoliari, pro firmo scientes, quod cum ecclesiam Gallicanam speciali affectione inter ceteras orbis ecclesias diligamus, vobis omnimodum in conservatione iurium et libertatum vestrarum, dante Domino, consilium et auxilium impendemus. Ceterum, cum olim felicis recordationis Honorius papa predecessor noster in omnes aliqua statuta contra ecclesiasticam libertatem edentes excommunicationis sententiam tulerit, et super hoc canonem late sententie promulgaritd, nos ipsius tenorem, ut eum solempniter publicari et servari in vestris diocesibus — non obstantibus indulgentiis vel privilegiis quibuscunque ab apostolica sede concessis — appellatione postposita faciatis, vobis duximus transmittendum; qui talis est?: Noveritis, quod nos in basilica principis apostolorum etc. usque: iudicata. Dat. Lugduni, II Non. Ianuar. anno IV.

regesto_sintetico: English translation: To the illustrious king of France. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth exult, because God, who in the precious blood of his only son has founded the church, has newly illuminated his face upon it, so that what was believed to be in danger of being destroyed by the tempest of the rebels, seems to have obtained securely the fullness of honor and the effect of freedom. We, dear son of grace, have heard your joy and have perceived the gladness of the church, which, since you, son of a glorious king, have taken origin from a royal stock, and have produced the fruit of honor and of grace, which has always been accustomed to produce for the church, without delay, with fervent ardor of the holy spirit, have decreed, that, with the unanimous counsel of our brothers, the queen of France and your noble brothers, that you should go with a victorious army, without any delay, to defend the church, which you recognize as our father. We, with our brothers, are filled with an incredible joy by the divine glory, which we glorify in the mind of the eternal king, who has infused in you, his king, such a pious and laudable affection, that it is worthy to be known by all, and to be remembered by posterity. And it is not surprising, since you have chosen to offer yourself to the succor of the mother church, not only to expose your substance, but also to appoint your person, in the midst of kings, as a shield, to defend her against the attacks of the adversaries of the church. May God recompense you with an inestimable reward for this merit, that the blessed assembly of eternal princes may be crowned with his glory. We also pray that he may deign to grant to your progenitors, of happy memory, the same glory, that they may enjoy the glory of the saints in heaven, and that we, who rejoice in the festival of our joy, may be able to recompense you and yours with a worthy honor and a due ornament. We have, therefore, been pleased to exhort your serenity, in the name of the Lord, to offer yourself to the succor of the church, and to have her defended, that, when the adversary shall see that she is aided by you, he may be converted to the Lord, or, if he has some interior light, he may be forced to perceive that the church, which the Lord has instituted and governed, does not suffer that her dignity be vacant on his account. We command, however, that you do not prepare for the journey, nor send an army, until you shall have received our letters or our nuncio. regesto_sintetico: English translation: To the cardinal-deacon of St. George in Velum Aureum, papal legate. With regard to the fact that, as it has been proposed by the beloved daughter of Christ, noblewoman of Austria, before us, the master and brothers of the Teutonic Knights in Austria in Starnberg and in Gutenstein and some other castles, the treasure and other movables and immovables, which belong to her from the grant made to her by the former duke of Austria, her paternal uncle, from the imperial privilege, are to be detained: we order that the said master and brothers, as they are bound, restore all the aforesaid things to the said duchess intact and, in order to satisfy the damages which, as she claims, she has incurred on account of the aforesaid, be compelled, by the censures of the Church, removed by way of appeal, through you or through others, by the present writ. regesto_sintetico: Translation in English: We, the Pope, send greetings to the podestà, consiglio, and people of Pavia. We pay attention and carefully think about the fact that the late emperor Frederick seeks to bring harm to the Church and its faithful by many treacherous and deceitful means. Since it is necessary to prevent this evil for the present, we order you to do what is necessary to make those who seek to harm the Church and the faithful pay for their evil deeds. Therefore, we command that you decree that all those who have been found to have dealt with or to have dealt with Frederick in favor of him and to the detriment of your city or the society of Lombardy, since the time when you returned to devotion to the Church, shall pay all their goods to the common use of your city. We forbid them and their children and grandchildren from being elected or appointed to any offices or powers in your city or in any other city of the society of Lombardy. Those who have the temerity to be elected or appointed to such offices or powers shall be bound by the sentence of excommunication and their lands shall be seized by ecclesiastical interdict. Non enim potest a piis animis absque gemitu cogitari regnum, quod sub priscis regibus libertatis gloria, nobilitatis decore, sinceritate fidei, opulentia rerum et iocunda populi frequentia prepollebat, in tantam servitutis miseriam, ignobilitatis iniuriam, lapsum fidei, exinanitionis angustiam et tam grave populorum excidium corruisse. Sed et Romana ecclesia super hiis pre ceteris profundius ingemiscit, que peculiares filios, eiusdem regni videlicet incolas, quos ad ingenuam genuerat libertatem, videt a gremio materne communionis abstractos duro vinculo mancipari, ut non minus illos conterat impressio tyrampni urgentis ad onera insueta, quam olim filios Israel presserit inclementia Pharaonis. Propter quod contra eum, quem innumera preter hec mala ab honoris sui culmine deiecerunt, quia in quo positus esset gradu eminentie factus insipiens non agnovit, ac fautores ipsius induendum est zeli pallium ad vindictam et in oppressorum presidium, quorum nos interpellant amara suspiria, potentius adsurgendum, ut excutere grave iugum dominii et in libertatem resurgere valeant filiorum ac singulis proprii status prior conditio reformetur. Ad hoc autem invitanda sunt subsidia oportuna fidelium, tuba verbi crucis vivifice altius solito intonante, et contra tyrampnicam feritatem summi regis signa victricia explicanda, in quibus conteri solent maligni superbarum exercitus potestatum. Illi vero, cuiuscumque ordinis vel conditionis extiterint, quos, maxime postquam exercitus ecclesie introducendus in regnum illuc Deo duce pervenerit, tam inconsulta vesania eidem F. tenuerit alligatos, ut potius velint tanquam servi sub ipsius perire tyrampnide quam ad libertatis gloriosa premia redeuntes in sinu libere matris cum filiis contineri, sciant exnunc, ne in posterum habeant ex ignorantie allegatione presidium, se, si fuerint civitates vel oppida, privilegiis et honoribus civitatum et immunitatibus quibuscumque, si comites aut barones vel qualescumque alii militari honore decorati seu quilibet alii laici, feudis, iuribus ac ceteris temporalibus bonis suis, si autem clerici, ecclesiasticis dignitatibus et beneficiis pro sue rebellionis ac perfidie pertinatia perpetuo spoliatos. regesto_sintetico: Translation to English: Dear Master Gregory, bishop of Magdeburg and Master Henry, bishop of Speyer, the task of God and the Church, which our beloved son Henry, illustrious king of the Romans, with the power of virtue is pursuing, should be promoted by the apostolic see with such a measure that he may easily and successfully attain the end. Therefore, we commit to your discretion through the present, with the authority of the apostolic see, that you should collect the redemption of the cross of the crusaders, the offerings and the legacies or donations made to the lord pope or other persons, as well as the offerings from any other source, and, after absolving those who have vowed the cross from their vow, you should assign them to the king, in such a way that they are as free as possible, absolving them from their vows and offering them the remission of their sins. If you are unable to do this by yourselves, you should entrust it to those whom you deem suitable, and if they are obstructed by any privileges obtained or to be obtained from the apostolic see, you should not give any attention to them, nor should you make any mention of them in the letters. If you do not both of you fulfill this task, we warn you that you will incur the penalty. Given at Lyons, 4 January, year 6 of our pontificate. regesto_sintetico: English translation: To the abbot and convent of Wettinhgen of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Constance. Although those things that are done by our mandate have full strength in themselves, so that they may be even stronger in their firmness, we willingly support them with apostolic protection, so that they may remain unharmed, since they are protected by our favor. Since, as your beloved son, brother Werner, has proposed to us, the bishop of Constance, your good memory, bishop H. of the same diocese, has granted to you by our special mandate and authority that you may have the right to retain the church of Riehaim in the diocese of Constance, in which you have the right of patronage, free of charge, as soon as it becomes vacant, but on condition that a suitable portion is left to the vicar serving in it for his maintenance and for the support of other burdens of the same church, as is contained in the letters in which this has been done, whose tenor we have inserted word for word in these presents: In the name of the Lord, Amen. Henry, bishop of Constance, to the beloved sons Conrad, abbot, and the convent of the monastery of Wettinhgen of the Cistercian order, greetings. The work of piety is done when Christ's poor, who in the profession of religion continually serve, are helped. Therefore, since we have received the apostolic letters in these words: Innocentius, bishop etc. to the venerable brother H., bishop of Constance etc. (see above, p. 153). The Roman church has always condescended to the prayers of its devoted sons and has granted a favor benevolent towards them. Therefore, since the noble men Hermann, the elder and Hermann, the younger, counts of Kiburchs, devoted to the Roman church, have brought to us with their urgent supplication that we should do them a special favor towards the monastery of Wettinhgen in the diocese of Constance, we, wishing to do them a favor through the intercession of your fraternity, order by apostolic letters that you grant to the abbot Conrad and the convent of the same monastery that, since they have been gravely damaged by the enemies of the church in temporal matters because of the imminent discord, we have granted that you may have the right to retain the church of Riehaim in the diocese of Constance, in which you have the right of patronage, free of charge, as soon as it becomes vacant, but on condition that a suitable portion is left to the vicar serving in it for his maintenance and for the support of other burdens of the same church. Given at Lyons, February 6, in the fifth year of our pontificate. We, attending the reasons and causes contained in the above-mentioned letters, which are supported by the truth, and especially taking into account the situation of the monastery in question, in which the religion of the faithful serving there is flourishing, and having been inclined to the needs of the same monastery, which is especially necessary in these times, have granted to you by apostolic authority and our favor that you may have the right to retain the church of Riehaim in our diocese, in which you have the right of patronage, free of charge, as soon as it becomes vacant, but on condition that a suitable portion is left to the vicar serving in it for his maintenance and for the support of other burdens of the same church, saving and excepting the right of our diocese and of our successors. Therefore, we decree that none of our letters and concessions made to you in the matter be prejudiced or nullified. Given at Constantia, in the year of the Lord 1248, June 10, indiction VI. By order of the lord pope. Gregory, bishop of Basle, has been given to them for this a conservation. Dat. Constantie, anno Domini MCCXLVIII°, X Kal. Iunii.

regesto_originale: Eidem. Cuma te ad partes etc. usque: destinemus, discretioni tue presentium auctoritate concedimus, ut si forte impeditus fueris, quod idem regnum nequeas libere introire, vel si exinde te pro aliqua causa exire oportuerit ac ad partes alias declinare, possis inibi existendo legationis officium in predicto regno nichilominus exercere. Dat. ut supra. Eidem. Cumb te ad partes etc. usque: destinemus, nos, ut eo efficacius huiusmodi officium exequi valeas, quo maiori fueris per nos auctoritate munitus, discretioni tue recipiendi cessiones tam archiepiscoporum et episcoporum quam prelatorum aliorum, sive sint exempti sive non, tue legationis, liberam tenore presentium concedimus potestatem. Dat. ut supra. k. Eide m. Cume te ad partes etc. usque: destinemus, discretioni tue dispensandi cum clericis tue legationis defectum natalium patientibus, quod — huiusmodi non obstante defectu — in susceptis ministrare ordinibus, ascendere ad maiores d ac ecclesiastica beneficia seu 20 personatus vel dignitates, pontificali dumtaxat excepta, etiam si curam habeant animarum annexam, obtinere valeant, auctoritate presentium concedimus facultatem. Dat. ut supra. Ei dem. Cume te ad partes etc. usque: destinemus, clericis, qui tecum permanserint et 2 quos pro agendis ecclesie duxeris destinandos, ut f quamdiu tecum fuerint vel negotiis ipsius ecclesie de mandato [tuols institerint peragendis, integre recipiant beneficiorum suorum proventus, distributionibus cotidianis exceptis, ac si personaliter in ecclesiis, in quibus beneficia ipsa obtinent, residerent. — privilegio, indulgentia, statuto et consuetudine iuramento seu quacumque alia firmitate vallatis nequaquam obstantibus — 20 auctoritate presentium indulgemus. Nulli ergo etc Dat. ut supra. XXIV. Innocentius IV papa Perusinis mandat, ut credant et faciant, quae Pfetrus) cardinalis legatus iis proposuerit. 1249, Apr. 17.

Vacante olim Cameracensi ecclesia! et ipsius canonicis die ad eligendum prefixa in unum convenientibus, nonnulli ex eis in venerabilem fratrem nostrum Nicolaum de Fontanis? If the said canons serve in the said church or reside there, they should receive the revenues of their prebend in the same way as the other canons who serve or reside there. This order extends to the canons who have resided in the said church before taking the cross. Those, however, who have not resided in the said church, should receive no more than what the time they spent on the expedition in Aquitaine will be computed to them as time of residence, if they wish. Master John of Peis, master John of Gothegni, and Simon called Dagores should not incur any penalty for not having resided in the said church. John of Colonia, William of Aquensis, and the provost of Rheims should be able to be absent for a year, if they wish, without incurring any penalty. The canons of the cross who have resided in the said church should not incur any penalty for their absence. We order that this order be carried out by ecclesiastical censure, and that the judgments which have been pronounced against those who have observed it be revoked. We grant dispensation to those who have incurred irregularity because of it, and we make them restore to the said church what has been taken or retained from it on account of this. We do not want this order to be extended in the future against the privileges and customs of the said church, unless it is contrary to the consuetudine or the statute, or to the oath or to some other firmness.
